articles.title: NBA Free-Agent Tracker 2026 and Updates on All the Latest Contract Signings, Trades
articles.summary: It's been arguably one of the busiest offseasons in recent NBA memory. Giannis Antetokounmpo is now a member of the Miami Heat. LeBron James and Jaylen Brown have joined forces on the Philadelphia 76ers.
articles.body:
It's been arguably one of the busiest offseasons in recent NBA memory. Giannis Antetokounmpo is now a member of the Miami Heat. LeBron James and Jaylen Brown have joined forces on the Philadelphia 76ers.

Keep it locked right here for all the latest roster moves as teams around the league try to close the gap with the champion Knicks.

Georges Niang and the Golden State Warriors have agreed to a one-year, $3.9 million contract, per ESPN's Shams Charania .

Guard Brandon Williams and the Golden State Warriors agreed to terms on a one-year, $2.6 million contract, according to ESPN's Shams Charania .

DeMar DeRozan and the Denver Nuggets have agreed to a contract in free agency, according to NBA insider Chris Haynes .

James Harden and the Cleveland Cavaliers agreed to terms on a new three-year, $97 million contract that includes a player option, according to ESPN's Shams Charania .

The Cleveland Cavaliers, Denver Nuggets and Los Angeles Clippers have agreed to a trade sending Peyton Watson to the Cavs, Max Strus to the Clippers and an unprotected 2031 first-round pick and a 2032 second-round pick to the Nuggets, per ESPN's Shams Charania .

Watson will sign a new four-year, $88 million deal to join the Cavs, per Charania. The contract includes a player option and a trade kicker.

Forward Malik Dia agreed to a two-way deal with the New Orleans Pelicans after going undrafted out of Ole Miss, according to ESPN's Shams Charania .

Forward Haywood Highsmith agreed to a one-year contract to return to the Phoenix Suns, agent Jerry Dianis told ESPN's Shams Charania .

Trendon Watford agreed to a one-year, $2.9 million contract with the New Orleans Pelicans in free agency, according to ESPN's Shams Charania .

The Cleveland Cavaliers traded guard Dennis Schroder to the Charlotte Hornets in exchange for Tre Mann, according to ESPN's Shams Charania .

The Portland Trail Blazers have signed free agent Jeremy Sochan, per ESPN's Shams Charania . The forward ended last season winning the NBA title with the New York Knicks.

The Golden State Warriors have re-signed Gary Payton II on a one-year, $3.9 million deal, per Shams Charania of ESPN.

Christian Koloko and the New Orleans Pelicans have agreed to a one-year deal, per HoopsHype's Michael Scotto .

Draymond Green has signed a one-year, $27.7 million deal to return to the Golden State Warriors after initially declining his player option, per Shams Charania of ESPN.

The Denver Nuggets are matching the Oklahoma City Thunder's two-year, $12 million offer sheet on Spencer Jones, per ESPN's Shams Charania . By doing so, Denver is now in the second apron, Charania added.

Kobe Bufkin and the New Orleans Pelicans have agreed to a one-year contract, per HoopsHype's Michael Scotto .

Kentavious Caldwell-Pope Signs with 76ers

Kentavious Caldwell-Pope has agreed to a buyout with the Memphis Grizzlies and will sign a one-year, $3.9 million contract to join the Philadelphia 76ers after clearing waivers, per ESPN's Shams Charania .

Spencer Jones has agreed to a two-year, $12 million offer sheet with the Oklahoma City Thunder, per Shams Charania of ESPN. The Denver Nuggets will have 48 hours to match the contract, per Charania.

LeBron James and the Philadelphia 76ers agreed to terms on a two-year, $8 million contract, according to ESPN's Shams Charania .

Jordan Walsh and the Boston Celtics reportedly agreed to a three-year, $15 million contract extension, per Shams Charania of ESPN.

The Los Angeles Lakers have signed Arthur Kaluma to a two-way contract, per Shams Charania of ESPN.

Jett Howard has reportedly agreed to a two-way deal with the Dallas Mavericks, according to Marc Stein .

The Los Angeles Lakers have reportedly signed Matisse Thybulle to a one-year deal worth $3.3 million, according to Shams Charania of ESPN.

Lu Dort Traded to Hawks, Risacher Traded to Mavs

"The Oklahoma City Thunder trading All-Defensive wing Lu Dort to the Atlanta Hawks in a three-team deal that sends three second-round picks to OKC, former No. 1 pick Zaccharie Risacher to the Dallas Mavericks and Ryan Nembhard to Atlanta," according to ESPN's Shams Charania .

Jordan McLaughlin and the San Antonio Spurs have agreed to a new one-year, $3.3 million contract, per Shams Charania of ESPN.

The Los Angeles Lakers have reportedly signed former Brooklyn Nets forward Ziaire Williams to a one-year, $3 million contract, per Shams Charania of ESPN.

The Denver Nuggets have signed Alpha Diallo to a one-year, $1.4 million contract, per Shams Charania of ESPN.

Gary Trent Jr. and the Milwaukee Bucks agreed to terms on a four-year, $64 million contract, according to ESPN's Shams Charania .

Victor Wembanyama Signs Spurs Contract Extension

Victor Wembanyama and the San Antonio Spurs agreed to a five-year, $252 million maximum rookie-scale contract extension, per ESPN's Shams Charania . The deal includes a player option for the fifth year.

Charles Bassey Agrees to New Warriors Contract

Center Charles Bassey and the Golden State Warriors agreed to a new one-year contract, according to ESPN's Shams Charania .

Jordan Clarkson and the New York Knicks agreed to a one-year $3.9 million contract in free agency.

The Utah Jazz and Mo Bamba have agreed to a two-year contract, per ESPN's Shams Charania .

Larry Nance Jr. and the Indiana Pacers agreed to terms on a one-year, $4 million contract, according to ESPN's Shams Charania .

Quinten Post's Offer Sheet Not Matched By Warriors

The Golden State Warriors are not matching the three-year, $30 million offer sheet the Grizzlies made to Quinten Post, meaning he will now join Memphis ahead of the 2026-27 season, per ESPN's Shams Charania .

The Washington Wizards are sending D'Angelo Russell, a future second-round pick and a future second-round pick swap to the Memphis Grizzlies in the 6-team sign-and-trade involving Khris Middleton, per ESPN's Shams Charania .

Khris Middleton has agreed to a three-year, $17.6 million contract with the Washington Wizards via sign-and-trade, per ESPN's Shams Charania .

The contract is part of a larger six-team deal involving the Dallas Mavericks, Detroit Pistons, Memphis Grizzlies, Milwaukee Bucks and Los Angeles Clippers, Charania added.

John Collins, Gary Harris and Taurean Prince (Pistons), Isaiah Stewart (Grizzlies), Santi Aldama (Mavericks) and Caris LeVert (Bucks) are included in the deal, per Charania.

The Detroit Pistons are trading Caris LeVert and two second-round picks to the Milwaukee Bucks in exchange for Taurean Prince and Gary Harris, per ESPN's Shams Charania .

Center Kevon Looney agreed to a one-year, $3.9 million contract with the Los Angeles Lakers, Life Sports Agency CEO Todd Ramasar told ESPN's S hams Charania .

Donovan Mitchell Signs Contract Extension with Cavaliers

Donovan Mitchell and the Cleveland Cavaliers agreed to a four-year, $237 million maximum contract extension with a player option for the 2030-31 season and a full trade kicker.

Rui Hachimura reportedly agreed to a two-year, $28 million contract with the Los Angeles Clippers after leaving the Los Angeles Lakers in free agency, according to ESPN's Shams Charania .

Quinten Post to Sign Grizzlies' Offer Sheet

RFA Quinten Post reportedly agreed to sign a three-year, $30 million offer sheet with the Memphis Grizzlies, according to ESPN's Shams Charania . "The Golden State Warriors have until 11:59pm ET on Tuesday to match," noted Charania.

Guard Kam Jones and the Milwaukee Bucks agreed to terms on a two-way contract, according to ESPN's Shams Charania .

The Utah Jazz are signing Josh Okogie to a two-year, $12 million contract, per ESPN's Shams Charania .

Andre Drummond has reportedly agreed to a one-year, $3.9 million contract with the New York Knicks according to Shams Charania of ESPN.

Jordan Miller to Sign New Clippers Contract

Restricted free agent Jordan Miller and the Los Angeles Clippers agreed to terms on a new three-year, $15.3 million contract, according to ESPN's Shams Charania .

Forward Trey Lyles and the Minnesota Timberwolves agreed to terms on a one-year deal, according to HoopsHype's Michael Scotto .

The Los Angeles Lakers are trading center Deandre Ayton to the Washington Wizards for Jaden Hardy and second-round picks in 2031 and 2032, per ESPN's Shams Charania .

Caleb Love has reportedly signed a two-way contract with the Philadelphia 76ers according to Shams Charania of ESPN.

The Charlotte Hornets acquired forward Dorian Finney-Smith and three second-round picks in a trade with the Houston Rockets, according to ESPN's Shams Charania .

The deal allows the Rockets to "open roster flexibility" after landing Marcus Smart and Bogdan Bogdanovic, Charania reported.

Rayan Rupert has reportedly signed a two-way contract with the Philadelphia 76ers according to Shams Charania of ESPN.

Javonte Green Agrees to Pistons Contract

Forward Javonte Green and the Detroit Pistons agreed to terms on a new one-year, $3.95 million contract, according to ESPN's Shams Charania .

Neemias Queta Agrees to Celtics Extension

Center Neemias Queta and the Boston Celtics agreed to terms on a four-year, $56 million contract extension, according to ESPN's Shams Charania .

Tari Eason Agrees to New Rockets Contract

Forward Tari Eason and the Houston Rockets agreed to a new five-year, $81.5 million contract, according to ESPN's Shams Charania .

The deal is reportedly fully guaranteed.

Former Golden State Warriors guard Pat Spencer reportedly agreed to a two-way contract with the Phoenix Suns, per Shams Charania of ESPN.

Tyus Jones Agrees to New Nuggets Contract

Guard Tyus Jones and the Denver Nuggets agreed to a new one-year contract, according to ESPN's Shams Charania .

Kenrich Williams Agrees to New Thunder Contract

Kenrich Williams and the Oklahoma City Thunder agreed to a new one-year, $5 million contract, according to NBA insider Chris Haynes .

Kyle Anderson Agrees to Raptors Contract

Former Minnesota Timberwolves forward Kyle Anderson agreed to a one-year, $3.9 million contract with the Toronto Raptors, according to ESPN's Shams Charania .

Anfernee Simons Agrees to 76ers Contract

Former Chicago Bulls guard Anfernee Simons agreed to a two-year, $12.3 million contract with the Philadelphia 76ers, according to ESPN's Shams Charania .

Marvin Bagley III has reportedly agreed to a one-year deal with the Denver Nuggets, according to Shams Charania of ESPN.

The Memphis Grizzlies are trading Santi Aldama to the Dallas Mavericks in exchange for AJ Johnson, a protected 2030 Warriors first-round pick and two future second-round picks, per ESPN's Shams Charania .

The Boston Celtics are trading Jaylen Brown to the Philadelphia 76ers in exchange for Paul George, two first-round picks and two second-round picks, per ESPN's Shams Charania .

Former Detroit Pistons forward Tobias Harris agreed to a two-year, $31 million contract with the San Antonio Spurs, according to ESPN's Shams Charania .

Former Los Angeles Lakers center Jaxson Hayes agreed to a two-year, $12 million contract with the Utah Jazz, according to ESPN's Tim MacMahon .

The deal reportedly includes a team option for the second season.

Kelly Oubre Jr. Agrees to Pacers Contract

Former Philadelphia 76ers forward Kelly Oubre Jr. agreed to a two-year contract worth nearly $17 million with the Indiana Pacers, according to ESPN's Shams Charania .

Jamir Watkins and the Washington Wizards agreed to terms on a two-way contract, the team announced .

Jonathan Isaac Agrees to New Magic Contract

Jonathan Isaac and the Orlando Magic agreed to a new one-year contract, according to HoopsHype's Michael Scotto .

Guard Alijah Martin and the Toronto Raptors agreed to terms on a new two-year, $4.8 million contract, according to ESPN's Shams Charania .

De'Anthony Melton Re-Signs with Warriors

Guard De'Anthony Melton and the Golden State Warriors agreed to terms on a new two-year, $11 million contract, according to ESPN's Shams Charania .

Former Chicago Bulls guard Collin Sexton agreed to a two-year, $19 million contract with the Los Angeles Lakers, according to ESPN's Shams Charania .

Quentin Grimes Agrees to Lakers Contract

Former Philadelphia 76ers guard Quentin Grimes agreed to a four-year, $60 million contract with the Los Angeles Lakers, according to ESPN's Shams Charania .

F/C Sandro Mamukelashvili reportedly agreed to a four-year, $52 million contract with the Los Angeles Lakers after leaving the Toronto Raptors in free agency, according to ESPN's Shams Charania .

The Los Angeles Lakers reportedly traded for Utah Jazz center Walker Kessler and will sign a four-year, $130 million contract, according to ESPN's Shams Charania . The Jazz will receive unprotected first-round picks in 2031 and 2033 and first-round swaps in 2028 and 2030, according to Charania.

Mitchell Robinson reportedly agreed to a three-year, $47.4 million with the Boston Celtics after leaving the New York Knicks in free agency, according to ESPN's Shams Charania .

Guard Jevon Carter has agreed to re-sign with the Orlando Magic on a one-year, $3.5 million deal, according to ESPN's Shams Charania .

Moe Wagner and the Brooklyn Nets agreed to terms on a two-year, $19 million deal, according to ESPN's Shams Charania .

Point guard Mike Conley Jr. and the Boston Celtics agreed to terms on a one-year deal, according to ESPN's Shams Charania .

Center Nikola Vucevic and the Orlando Magic agreed to terms on a one-year, $3.9 million deal, according to ESPN's Shams Charania .

Former New York Knicks center Ariel Hukporti and the Philadelphia 76ers agreed to terms on a one-year, $3.4 million contract, according to ESPN's Shams Charania .

Norman Powell and the Chicago Bulls agreed to a two-year, $45 million contract, according to ESPN's Shams Charania .

John Collins has reportedly agreed to a three-year, $51 million contract with the Detroit Pistons, per Shams Charania of ESPN.

Marcus Smart reportedly agreed to a two-year, $13 million contract with a player option for the second season, per Shams Charania of ESPN.

Bogdan Bogdanovic and the Houston Rockets have agreed to a one-year contract, per ESPN's Shams Charania .

Dean Wade joined the Philadelphia 76ers on a four-year contract worth $39 million, per ESPN's Shams Charania.

Zach Collins is headed back to the Chicago Bulls. The veteran big man signed a two-year, $17 million contract extension, per ESPN's Shams Charania.

Luke Kennard has agreed to a two-year, $13 million contract with the Phoenix Suns. Kennard has a player option for the second season, per ESPN's Shams Charania.

Keon Ellis has opted to join the Brooklyn Nets on a two-year deal worth $18 million, per ESPN's Shams Charania.

Kobe Sanders agreed to a four-year contract worth $11.2 million to stay with the Los Angeles Clippers, per ESPN's Shams Charania.

Branden Carlson signed a one-year deal with the Portland Trail Blazers. The former Oklahoma City big man inked a deal worth $2.5 million, per ESPN's Shams Charania.

Tim Hardaway Jr. has signed a contract with the Miami Heat, per NBA insider Chris Haynes.

Hardaway inked a one-year, $6.5 million deal, per ESPN's Shams Charania.

Bones Hyland has reached a deal with the Minnesota Timberwolves to return to the Western Conference team on a one-year deal, per The Athletic's Jon Krawczynski.

Veteran center DeAndre Jordan will re-sign with the New Orleans Pelicans on a one-year contract, per ESPN's Shams Charania.

Ousmane Dieng is returning to the Milwaukee Bucks on a three-year, $17.5 million contract, per ESPN's Shams Charania.

Forward Precious Achiuwa and the Sacramento Kings reportedly agreed to terms on a new two-year, $11.5 million contract, according to NBA insider Chris Haynes .

The Toronto Raptors have agreed to acquire Kawhi Leonard in a trade with the Los Angeles Clippers.

The Clippers are receiving Brandon Ingram, Gradey Dick, unprotected first-round picks in 2031 and 2033, second-round picks in 2030 and 2033 and a 2027 first-round pick swap from Toronto, per ESPN's Shams Charania.

Center Jock Landale plans to sign a new one-year, $14 million contract with the Atlanta Hawks, according to ESPN's Shams Charania .

LeBron James will test free agency after deciding that he won't return to the Los Angeles Lakers, Klutch Sports CEO Rich Paul told ESPN's Shams Charania .

Robert Williams III Re-Signs with Blazers

Robert Williams III agreed to a three-year, $44 million contract with the Portland Trail Blazers, his agent confirmed to ESPN's Shams Charania .

Simone Fontecchio Intends to Sign New Heat Contract

Simone Fontecchio reportedly is set to return to the Miami Heat on a one-year contract, per Shams Charania of ESPN.

Ja Morant reportedly has been traded to the Portland Trail Blazers and the Memphis Grizzlies will receive Jerami Grant and Kris Murray, according to ESPN's Shams Charania .

Harrison Barnes Intends to Sign New Spurs Contract

Forward Harrison Barnes intends to sign a new one-year, $8 million deal to return to the San Antonio Spurs, according to ESPN's Shams Charania .

Kristaps Porzingis Agrees to New Warriors Contract

Center Kristaps Porzingis and the Golden State Warriors agreed to a new two-year, $40 million contract, Excel Sports Management agent Jeff Schwartz told ESPN's Shams Charania .

The deal includes a player option for the second season.

Kevin Huerter Intends to Sign New Pistons Contract

Guard Kevin Huerter intends to sign a new three-year, $27 million contract to return to the Detroit Pistons, according to ESPN's Shams Charania .

Jusuf Nurkic Intends to Sign New Jazz Contract

Center Jusuf Nurkic intends to sign a new two-year, $22 million contract with the Utah Jazz, according to ESPN's Shams Charania .

Julian Champagnie Intends to Sign New Spurs Contract

Forward Julian Champagnie intends to sign a new three-year, $45 million contract with the San Antonio Spurs, according to ESPN's Shams Charania .

Landry Shamet Intends to Sign New Knicks Contract

Landry Shamet intends to sign a new four-year, $24 million contract to return to the New York Knicks, according to ESPN's Shams Charania .

Lu Dort's Contract Option Picked Up by Thunder

The Oklahoma City Thunder are exercising Lu Dort's $17.7 million contract option, according to ESPN's Shams Charania .

Brook Lopez's Contract Option Exercised by Clippers

The Los Angeles Clippers exercised Brook Lopez's $9.2 million contract option, according to NBA insider Jake Fischer .

Meanwhile, the team reportedly will not pick up the options for Nicolas Batum or Bogdan Bogdanovic.

Jonathan Kuminga's Option Declined by Hawks

The Atlanta Hawks reportedly declined Jonathan Kuminga's contract option, making him a free agent, according to ESPN's Shams Charania .

The Atlanta Hawks acquired guard Devin Carter and a future second-round pick from the Sacramento Kings, according to ESPN's Shams Charania .

Bradley Beal Declines Clippers Contract Option

Los Angeles Clippers guard Bradley Beal declined his $5.6 million player option and will become a free agent, Priority Sports' Mark Bartelstein told ESPN's Shams Charania .

Thomas Bryant Intends to Sign New Cavaliers Contract

Center Thomas Bryant intends to sign a new one-year deal to return to the Cleveland Cavaliers, according to ESPN's Shams Charania .

Pat Connaughton's Contract Option Picked Up by Hornets

The Charlotte Hornets picked up Pat Connaughton's $3.8 million contract option, according to Rod Boone of the Charlotte Observer .

Walker Kessler Receives Jazz Qualifying Offer

The Utah Jazz issued the qualifying offer to center Walker Kessler, according to The Athletic's Tony Jones . That will make Kessler a restricted free agent.

Jones also reported the team declined team options on Bez Mbeng and Hayden Gray.

Marcus Smart Declines Lakers Contract Option

Los Angeles Lakers guard Marcus Smart declined his $5.4 million contract option and will become a free agent, according to ESPN's Shams Charania .

Ryan Nembhard's Contract Option to Be Exercised by Mavericks

The Dallas Mavericks plan to exercise guard Ryan Nembhard's $2.2 million contract option for the 2026-27 NBA season, according to NBA insider Marc Stein .

Andrew Wiggins Intends to Sign New Heat Contract

Forward Andrew Wiggins intends to sign a new three-year, $64 million contract with the Miami Heat, according to ESPN's Shams Charania .

The deal reportedly includes a player option for the third season.

Dominick Barlow's Contract Option Exercised by 76ers

The Philadelphia 76ers will exercise Dominick Barlow's $3.4 million contract option for the 2026-27 NBA season, according to NBA insider Jake Fischer .

Trayce Jackson-Davis Opts Into Raptors Contract

Raptors center Trayce Jackson-Davis reportedly opted into his $2.4 million player option for the 2026-27 season, according to ESPN's Shams Charania .

Malachi Smith's Contract Option Exercised by Nets

The Brooklyn Nets exercised guard Malachi Smith's $2.2 million contract option for the 2026-27 season, per SNY's Ian Begley .

Deandre Ayton Opts into Lakers Contract Option

Los Angeles Lakers center Deandre Ayton opted into his $8.1 million player option for the 2026-27 NBA season, according to ESPN's Shams Charania .

Day'Ron Sharpe Intends to Sign New Nets Contract

Center Day'Ron Sharpe intends to sign a new two-year, $20 million contract to return to the Brooklyn Nets, according to ESPN's Shams Charania .

The deal will reportedly include a team option for the second season.

Josh Minott Intends to Sign New Nets Contract

Forward Josh Minott intends to sign a new two-year, $9 million contract to return to the Brooklyn Nets, according to ESPN's Shams Charania .

The deal reportedly will include a team option for the second season.

Sandro Mamukelashvili Declines Raptors Contract Option

Toronto Raptors forward Sandro Mamukelashvili declined his $2.8 million player option and will become a free agent, Priority Sports agents George Roussakis and Mark Bartelstein told ESPN's Shams Charania .

Draymond Green Declines Warriors Player Option

Golden State Warriors forward Draymond Green declined his $27.7 million player option and will become a free agent, according to ESPN's Shams Charania .

Per Charania, Green's decision will give Golden State the flexibility to pursue Los Angeles Lakers star LeBron James in free agency and Washington Wizards star Anthony Davis on the trade market. Green reportedly would still be part of the plans for a potential Big 4.

Zach LaVine Opts into Kings Contract Option

Sacramento Kings guard Zach LaVine opted into his $49 million player option for the 2026-27 NBA season, Klutch Sports' Rich Paul told ESPN's Shams Charania .

James Harden Declines Cavaliers Player Option

Cleveland Cavaliers guard James Harden declined his $42.3 million player option for the 2026-27 season, according to ESPN's Shams Charania .

The two sides are reportedly working on a new multiyear contract.

Fred VanVleet Opts into Rockets Player Option

Houston Rockets guard Fred VanVleet opted into his $25 million player option for the 2026-27 NBA season, Klutch Sports' Rich Paul told ESPN's Shams Charania .

Miles Bridges Traded from Hornets to Suns

The Charlotte Hornets traded Miles Bridges, a 2029 first-round draft pick and a 2027 second-round draft pick to the Phoenix Suns for Grayson Allen, Royce O'Neale and a 2033 first-round pick, per ESPN's Shams Charania .

Jose Alvarado declined his $4.5 million player option and agreed to a three-year deal worth more than $14 million with the New York Knicks, per ESPN's Shams Charania .

The deal includes a maximum 15 percent trade kicker and a mutual option, which will allow the two sides to rework it again in 2028 before the final season.

Isaiah Joe Traded from Thunder to Pistons

The Oklahoma City Thunder traded Isaiah Joe to the Detroit Pistons in exchange for two second-round picks, per ESPN's Shams Charania .

articles.title: NBA: Memphis Grizzlies trade two-time All-Star Ja Morant to the Portland Trail Blazers
articles.summary: Ja Morant is hoping to revive his career after it was revealed on Monday the Memphis Grizzlies point guard is set to move to the Portland Trail Blazers in a trade for Jerami Grant and Kris Murray
articles.body:
Ja Morant is headed to Portland, after the Trail Blazers and Memphis Grizzlies agreed on a trade on Monday.

The move will give the two-time All-Star a chance to revive his career, a person with knowledge of the agreement told The Associated Press.

In return, AP understands Portland is sending forwards Jerami Grant and Kris Murray to the Grizzlies as part of the deal,.

It is a big swing by the Trail Blazers and could suggest Portland - with new owner Tom Dundon, whose Carolina Hurricanes just won the Stanley Cup - might not be done making moves.

  • Not got Sky? Get Sky Sports or stream with no contract
  • Choose the Sky Sports push notifications you want
  • Listen to Sky Sports' range of podcasts

Morant adds to a logjam at point guard right now for Portland, with Jrue Holiday, Damian Lillard and Scoot Henderson also on the current roster.

The 26-year-old has averaged 22.4 points for his career but has played only 79 games over the last three seasons due to injuries and suspensions, including a 25-match ban after Morant was seen on a livestream holding a gun while he was in the passenger seat of a vehicle.

That came not long after an eight-game suspension for flashing a gun in a Denver-area nightclub, also captured on social media.

Morant appeared to be on a path toward superstardom after he was drafted as the No 2 selection in the 2019 draft, before he was crowned the Rookie of the Year in 2020 as well as the league's Most Improved Player in 2021-22.

The suspensions, combined, cost Morant about $9m in lost salary. He said in April 2025 that he's made his peace with being a lightning rod for constant criticism.

"I'm kind of used to it," Morant said at that time. "I was pretty much a villain for two years now.

articles.title: NBA: Jaylen Brown traded to 76ers, Paul George to Celtics as Kawhi Leonard traded back to Raptors in dizzying summer
articles.summary: Jaylen Brown has been traded from the 76ers to the Celtics for Paul George and a plethora of draft picks; Brown ends a 10-year tenure in Boston; The move continues a dizzying spree of high profile moves across the NBA, including LeBron James leaving the Lakers
articles.body:
Celtics star Jaylen Brown has been traded to the 76ers for Paul George, two first round picks and two second round picks as the NBA's dizzying summer of moves rages on.

Brown was the 2024 NBA Finals MVP, a five-time All-Star and the league's fourth-leading scorer this past season, and goes to long-time rival 76ers after being beaten 4-3 in a playoff series by his new team with Boston in May.

The move is one of a number of blockbuster trades including All-Star-caliber players across the NBA so far this offseason, including LeBron James leaving the Los Angeles Lakers as a free agent.

  • LeBron James confirms Lakers exit
  • Not got Sky? Get Sky Sports or stream with no contract
  • Choose the Sky Sports push notifications you want
  • Listen to Sky Sports' range of podcasts

Giannis Antetokounmpo has also been traded from Milwaukee to Miami, Kawhi Leonard and Brandon Ingram headlined a swap between the Toronto Raptors and Los Angeles Clippers, and Ja Morant was dealt to Portland by Memphis.

Welcome to Philly, JB!" Pennsylvania Gov. Josh Shapiro posted on social media. "Sixers get way better and, as a bonus, the Celtics got worse!"

It's a move that breaks up what has been one of the league's most successful 1-2 punches in Brown and Jayson Tatum, who helped carry the Celtics to the 2024 NBA title.

Tatum missed most of this past season while recovering from an Achilles tear that happened during the 2025 playoffs, meaning Brown had to carry even more of the load for Boston - and he wound up with career-best averages of 28.7 points, 6.9 rebounds and 5.1 assists per game.

It seemed, though, that Brown has felt underappreciated, especially after it became known that Boston had included him in trade talks with Milwaukee when Antetokounmpo was on the market.

"Nobody has won more combined regular-season and playoff games since I entered the league 10 years ago," Brown posted on social media over the weekend. He's right: The Celtics have won 523 games with Brown in the lineup, including playoff contests, which is six more than Denver has won with Nikola Jokic over that span.

Brown forms a a new Eastern Conference powerhouse with Tyrese Maxey (the league's No 5 scorer this past season) and Joel Embiid (a two-time NBA scoring champion).

The trade ends a tremendously disappointing two-year stint for George, who was traded with two years left on a four-year, $212 million free-agent contract. The 36-year-old George never approached his nine-time All-Star form in Philadelphia and his tenure was marred by a 25-game suspension last season for flunking a drug test.

He averaged just 16.7 points in his two seasons in Philadelphia after topping the 20-point mark in nine straight seasons with Indiana, Oklahoma City and the Los Angeles Clippers.

articles.title: NBA Europe: London and Manchester bid race heats up as crunch meetings take place in New York around World Cup final
articles.summary: NBA chiefs will hold talks with prospective NBA Europe owners in New York this weekend; London is reportedly the most sought-after franchise destination with highest-value bids; Manchester is also one of the target cities, with the league scheduled to start in October 2027
articles.body:
The race to own NBA Europe's first franchises - including those targeted in London and Manchester - reaches New York this weekend as wealthy investors descend for meetings with the NBA's top executives.

NBA Commissioner Adam Silver and Deputy Commissioner Mark Tatum will be speaking to bidders in town ahead of Sunday's World Cup final at MetLife Stadium.

  • Jokic, Doncic, Wembanyama? Amaechi insists UK can produce NBA superstar
  • Magic guard Black reveals how Man City striker Haaland inspires him
  • Download Sky Sports app for analysis, video and more
  • Get Sky Sports or stream with contract-free with NOW

Some of the top capital investment firms in the world are in the US metropolis for the showpiece and Silver intends to make the most of it with a view to shaping the deals for the first franchises, which are expected to drop in the coming weeks and months heading into the autumn.

"We've had tremendous interest from multiple cities in Europe, including cities that we didn't even ask for bids from," Silver said after the NBA's Board of Governors meeting in Las Vegas earlier this week.

"We discussed with our board today that we're in the process of finalising those bids, I think for an initial group of cities. Many of the people who are involved in those bids, the European bidders, are actually going to be in New York for the World Cup final on Sunday.

"Mark and I are going to be attending several meetings with them, given their presence in New York. I would say we're hoping to wrap up some of those deals over the next several weeks and then announcements will be forthcoming."

London is very much at the centre of the bidding race and is reported to be the most heavily contested market with multiple bids topping $1bn, Sky Sports understands.

Sky News has reported that Liberty Global, the majority shareholder of Formula E, tabled an offer for the London franchise and that former Tottenham Hotspur executive chairman Daniel Levy has joined a consortium being assembled with Jahm Najafi, the MSP Sports Capital co-founder.

Sky News also reported that the Reuben family, who hold a stake in Newcastle United, are among the suitors for the London team.

The Athletic reported that Buss Sports Capital - the investment group founded by members of the family who previously owned the Los Angeles Lakers - has bid in several cities, including London, Manchester and Lyon.

Overall, more than 20 groups submitted finalised bids by the end of June, with viable offers in all 12 target cities and multiple bids in the 10-figure range in select markets. City AM has reported that Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund and Chelsea co-owner Todd Boehly were among those credited with interest in London, the most sought-after franchise of all and the market with the most valuable committed bids, reportedly multiple above $1bn.

George Aivazoglou, the NBA's managing director for Europe and the Middle East, told Sky Sports: "We're extremely encouraged by the level of interest in the NBA and FIBA's proposed league in Europe, including from existing basketball and football clubs, outside investors, prospective commercial and media partners, federations, domestic leagues and, most importantly, fans.

"In addition to preserving and celebrating Europe's rich basketball traditions and passionate fanbases, we're particularly excited about the opportunity to bring permanent, world-class basketball to marquee European cities like London and Manchester here in the UK, where basketball fandom and participation are at an all-time high."

What is NBA Europe and what do we know about it?

NBA Europe is the creation of a new professional basketball league with the NBA working in partnership with FIBA, the sport's global governing body.

They are targeting an October 2027 launch - which Adam Silver said last month is very much "on schedule" - and barring an unlikely alliance it will act as a direct challenge to the existing EuroLeague at the top of the European club game. The plan is for 16 teams, 12 of which will be permanent franchises, plus four places earned each year on merit through FIBA competition.

Twelve cities have been targeted for the permanent franchises, London and Manchester, Paris and Lyon, Madrid and Barcelona, Milan and Rome, Berlin and Munich, plus Istanbul and Athens.

The NBA is looking to tap into the European fan culture which left NBA stars very impressed on their most recent European sojourn.

The first owners will be known soon, with announcements to follow and an expectation that the first NBA Europe teams will be unveiled by early autumn.

articles.title: LeBron James joining Philadelphia 76ers for record-extending 24th NBA season as all-time leading scorer returns to east coast
articles.summary: Lebron James will play his record-extending 24th season with the Philadelphia 76ers after weeks of speculation about which team he'll join next; the NBA's all-time leading points scorer says he 'still wants to work' and is hungry to win his fifth NBA championship
articles.body:
LeBron ‌James has decided to join ‌the Philadelphia 76ers for his record-extending 24th NBA ‌season, the league's ‌all-time leading scorer said on Friday

The ‌league's all-time leading scorer spent the last eight seasons of his glittering career with the Los Angeles Lakers, leading them to a title in 2020 after two separate ‌stints with the Cleveland Cavaliers and four years with the Miami Heat.

"This is my last decision," the 41-year-old wrote on X. "I'm not going for money. I'm not going for family. What ​am I really playing for at ⁠this point? I still ⁠want to sacrifice. I still want to work. I still want to ‌grind.

  • Not got Sky? Get Sky Sports or stream with no contract
  • Choose the Sky Sports push notifications you want
  • Listen to Sky Sports' range of podcasts

"I still want to compete, to win and to have a chance at the feeling of ‌winning another championship," James wrote on social media.

"I believe I can help make the Philadelphia 76ers a championship team and I am so excited to ⁠energize a new fan base and ​start this incredible journey one last time."

The ​41-year-old James, who last March surpassed ​Robert Parish's record for most career regular-season games ⁠played, has continued to perform at an elite level despite his age.

He earned a league-record 22nd consecutive ⁠All-Star selection last February during ​a season in which he averaged 20.9 ​points, 6.1 rebounds and 7.2 assists over 60 games.

James had announced at the end of June that he would be leaving the Lakers, explaining that he hoped he had made the fans and his team-mates proud.

"No, THANK YOU!" James said on social media, responding to a post from the Lakers official account, thanking the 41-year-old for his service.

"Truly an honour to wear the (Lakers colours) while trying to continue the greatness & legacies that came before me! Hope I made a few proud during my stint."

James is the NBA's oldest active player and will turn 42 in December.

He is due to become the first player in the league's history to play a 24th season, and notably shared a court with his son, Bronny.

More to follow...

articles.title: LeBron James: Why Philadelphia 76ers offers NBA legend perfect chance to make ultimate GOAT statement
articles.summary: LeBron James will sign a two-year veteran's minimum deal worth around $3.9m a season with the Philadelphia 76ers; NBA legend is chasing the one record nobody in history holds, a title with a fourth different franchise; watch the NBA live on Sky Sports this coming season
articles.body:
There is one line missing from the fullest CV in basketball history and LeBron James has just told the world he is spending his final two seasons chasing it.

The NBA's all-time leading scorer announced his "last decision" on Friday, signing a two-year deal with the Philadelphia 76ers on the veteran's minimum of around $3.9m a season.

A considerable drop from the near $53m he earned last year.

  • NBA Europe: What is it, how does it work and which UK teams are involved?
  • Jokic, Doncic, Wembanyama? Amaechi insists UK can produce NBA superstar
  • Get Sky Sports or stream with no contract

The greatest player of his era – and one who is irrefutably on the sport's Mt. Rushmore as one of its greatest players – acquired at the price of a rookie.

Sit with that for a second.

LeBron James, four rings, 22 All-Star selections, and more points than anyone who has ever graced the league, playing on a contract costing more than $10m less than No 1 pick AJ Dybantsa will be earning with the Washington Wizards this year.

Depending on how the next two seasons go, it is either the bargain of the century or the most expensive cheap contract in the sport's history.

The decision to go to Philly, though, is in keeping with LeBron's DNA and the way he has approached and attacked every challenge he has faced in his career.

This is a man who had every sentimental option on the table. He could've ended with a third spell in Cleveland, a Miami reunion and even a late union with Stephen Curry et al in Golden State.

He rejected the lot. "I still truly love this game, and I have more to give," he wrote.

And everything he has left in the tank is now being aimed squarely at one target.

The final record left for one of the all-time greats

Safe to say, James is not catching Bill Russell's 11 rings with the Boston Celtics. Nobody is, in all likelihood, but that was a very different era for the sport.

James' scoring record is safe. His longevity record, 24 seasons and counting, is arguably safer still.

The only meaningful line left in the book is one nobody has ever written – and that is winning an NBA title with a fourth different franchise.

"I'm not going for money. I'm not going for family," he wrote. "I still want to sacrifice. I still want to work. I still want to grind."

Philadelphia is a franchise built for that kind of hunger. The Sixers have not won it all since 1983, the year before James was born, and have not been past the second round since 2001.

While James has won everywhere he has played. Twice in Miami in 2012 and 2013, the drought-breaker in Cleveland in 2016 and the 2020 triumph across the backdrop of the most emotional year in Los Angeles Lakers' history, won in the NBA bubble due to COVID-19 restrictions.

A ring in Philadelphia would take him to five, level with Kobe Bryant who tragically passed away in a helicopter crash 10 months prior to James leading the Lakers to the title.

It would also hand him a record that stands entirely alone as his own and that is where the ultimate GOAT statement can be made by James.

Michael Jordan's six titles came with one franchise built around him whilst James' claim has always rested on portability, on dragging different organisations to the summit across three decades, and on longevity and consistency which is perhaps unrivalled by any athlete in any sport.

Doing it at 42, on rookie money, in a city that has not seen a parade since the early 1980s, and the debate does not just sway – perhaps it even starts to close.

A fitting soundtrack for the "last decision"

New 76ers team president Mike Gansey had already won the NBA summer before Friday's showstopping announcement.

Trading Paul George and picks to Boston for Jaylen Brown, the 2024 Finals MVP and the league's fourth-leading scorer last season, was the shock of the offseason. Well, before this.

Add Brown, Tyrese Maxey, former MVP Joel Embiid – who called for LeBron to join Philly 12 years ago in a social media post – and the rapidly improving VJ Edgecombe around James and, on paper, Philadelphia has a case for the best starting five in basketball, with a ring-winning coach in Nick Nurse to boot.

The prospect is tantalising for Philly's fanbase, not to mention general NBA fans.

Of course, the impact of locking down LeBron was immediate, too, as Fanatics sold out of No 23 jerseys within hours and the betting markets moved the Sixers straight into the title conversation.

The man himself elected to announce the move with a highlight reel soundtracked by Philadelphia's adopted sports anthem, Meek Mill's Dreams and Nightmares.

It could hardly be more appropriate, too, as there is no soft landing here.

It is a parade down Broad Street or a huge bust, with nothing in between.

The East is brutal, as well, right now. The freshly-minted champion Knicks sit 100 miles up the road waiting to collect their first rings in 53 years, quite possibly with James in the building on opening night.

Meanwhile, Giannis Antetokounmpo has joined Miami, Detroit won 60 games last season and Toronto are waiting on Kawhi Leonard.

The risks inherent in this move are readily apparent, too.

James turns 42 in December and managed 60 games last season and Embiid has played in just 57 across the last two years of what's been an injury-ravaged career.

Stylistically, there are questions too. There is one ball and four players with the resume to demand it, and this franchise has already watched James Harden, Jimmy Butler and George arrive as saviours and leave without even making it to the Eastern Conference Finals, let alone the big show.

But none of them were LeBron James. Nobody is.

For 23 seasons the question has always been about what he's going to do next.

He's now given his answer for the final time.

Two years, one city and the last argument he has to win.

Watch the NBA live on Sky Sports this season or stream contract-free with NOW.

Add Brown, Tyrese Maxey, former MVP Joel Embiid – who called for LeBron to join Philly 12 years ago in a social media post – and the rapidly improving VJ Edgecombe around James and, on paper, Philadelphia has a case for the best starting five in basketball, with a ring-winning coach in Nick Nurse to boot.

The prospect is tantalising for Philly's fanbase, not to mention general NBA fans.

Of course, the impact of locking down LeBron was immediate, too, as Fanatics sold out of No 23 jerseys within hours and the betting markets moved the Sixers straight into the title conversation.

The man himself elected to announce the move with a highlight reel soundtracked by Philadelphia's adopted sports anthem, Meek Mill's Dreams and Nightmares.

It could hardly be more appropriate, too, as there is no soft landing here.

It is a parade down Broad Street or a huge bust, with nothing in between.

The East is brutal, as well, right now. The freshly-minted champion Knicks sit 100 miles up the road waiting to collect their first rings in 53 years, quite possibly with James in the building on opening night.

Meanwhile, Giannis Antetokounmpo has joined Miami, Detroit won 60 games last season and Toronto are waiting on Kawhi Leonard.

The risks inherent in this move are readily apparent, too.

James turns 42 in December and managed 60 games last season and Embiid has played in just 57 across the last two years of what's been an injury-ravaged career.

Stylistically, there are questions too. There is one ball and four players with the resume to demand it, and this franchise has already watched James Harden, Jimmy Butler and George arrive as saviours and leave without even making it to the Eastern Conference Finals, let alone the big show.

But none of them were LeBron James. Nobody is.

For 23 seasons the question has always been about what he's going to do next.

He's now given his answer for the final time.

Two years, one city and the last argument he has to win.

articles.title: LeBron James faces the New York Knicks on NBA opening night with Lakers clash on Christmas Day as signature fixtures announced
articles.summary: LeBron James travels to Madison Square Garden to face the New York Knicks in his first game with the Philadelphia 76ers on opening night; James will return to Los Angeles to face the Lakers on Christmas Day
articles.body:
LeBron James will make his Philadelphia 76ers debut against defending NBA champions the New York Knicks at Madison Square Garden on the opening night of the season.

The blockbuster clash headlines a selection of "signature" fixtures released by the NBA, with the announcement also revealing that James will return to Los Angeles on Christmas Day to face his former team, the Lakers.

Four-time NBA champion James, who signed for the Sixers on a two-year, $8m contract in July, will face the Cleveland Cavaliers - with whom he won the NBA title in 2016 - in his first home game in Philadelphia on October 22.

  • Not got Sky? Get Sky Sports or stream with no contract
  • Choose the Sky Sports push notifications you want
  • Listen to Sky Sports' podcasts

Opening night, taking place on October 20, also features a clash between the Boston Celtics and the Detroit Pistons at 8pm UK time, before the Oklahoma City Thunder take on the San Antonio Spurs in a rematch of last year's Western Conference finals in the late game.

The Christmas Day slate kicks off with an NBA Finals rematch between the San Antonio and the Knicks, before Giannis Antetokounmpo's Miami Heat travel to Boston to face the Celtics.

The NBA also announced that French sensation Victor Wembanyama and the Spurs would be heading to Paris in January to face the New Orleans Pelicans, before the two teams travel to Manchester in the first-ever NBA game at the Co-op Live Arena.

articles.title: Los Angeles Lakers: Jeanie Buss contests siblings' plans to sell ownership stake to Josh Kushner and  Bob Iger
articles.summary: Josh Kushner, the brother of US President Donald Trump's son-in-law Jared, and former Disney chief executive Bob Iger agreed a deal to buy the controlling interest in the Los Angeles Lakers at a valuation of $12.5 billion (£9.3bn) - a record for a professional sports team
articles.body:
Los Angeles Lakers governor Jeanie Buss is contesting her siblings' plans to sell the family's remaining 17.8 per cent ownership stake in the team.

Josh Kushner, the brother of US President Donald Trump's son-in-law Jared, and former Disney chief executive Bob Iger agreed a deal earlier this month to buy the controlling interest in the Lakers at a valuation of $12.5bn (£9.3bn) - a record for a professional sports team.

Kushner and Iger are reportedly buying about 65 per cent of the team from Mark Walter, who also owns a stake in baseball's Los Angeles Dodgers along with Chelsea chairman Todd Boehly. They would own about 83 per cent if they also reach a deal with the Buss family.

  • Los Angeles Lakers to be sold in record-breaking £9bn deal
  • LeBron James faces the New York Knicks on NBA opening night
  • Not got Sky? Get Sky Sports or stream with no contract
  • Choose the Sky Sports push notifications you want

Jeanie Buss has been the Lakers' governor since 2013 and the death of her father Jerry Buss, who had purchased the team in 1979.

She led the family's move to sell a controlling stake of the team to Walter last year at a valuation of $10bn, in a deal that ensured she remained in position until 2030.

The decision to sell would end Jeanie's tenure, because the job requires at least 15 per cent ownership of the team.

The Buss family released a statement on Monday, saying: "We have decided as a family to sell the remaining Buss Family Trust shares to the Bob Iger group as part of the ongoing transaction.

"We love the Lakers, Lakers fans and will continue to support Los Angeles; but it is time to use this opportunity to move on and exit gracefully while we still can."

But Jeannie Buss' attorney, Adam Streisand, wrote to representatives for her five siblings to state that any decision to sell the family trust's ownership stake "would be and is void", according to ESPN.

"Co-trustees are bound to vote to ensure that the minimum 15 per cent ownership requirement is maintained in order to ensure that Jeanie Buss may remain controlling owner," the letter is reported to have said.

"Any attempt by the co-trustees to do otherwise, and any attempt to aid or abet the co-trustees as such, would constitute a breach of trust, breach of fiduciary duty and be in contempt of court."

The Lakers have 17 NBA titles, 11 of which have come under the Buss family's ownership, but the six siblings have been in frequent conflict since their father Jerry's death, with Jeanie firing Jim from his job as the Lakers' head of basketball operations in 2017, followed a week later by a lawsuit against her brothers amid an attempt by Jim and Johnny to oust her as the Lakers' controlling owner.

Joey and Jesse were fired from their front-office jobs with the team last November.

The sale agreement with Kushner and Iger also still has to be approved by the NBA's board of governors, which could take months, and comes after Kushner's name was attached to a controversial plan proposed by FIFA president Gianni Infantino to sell off stakes in the governing body's competitions to private investors.

Thrive Eternal, an American venture capital firm founded by Kushner, was due to lead the proposed investor group for the FIFA Forward Enterprise proposal until plans were scrapped in the face of fierce criticism and threats of boycott from some of its continental confederations, including UEFA.

articles.title: Becky Hammon Ejected After Heated Altercation with WNBA Officials on Video from Dream vs. Aces Game
articles.summary: Becky Hammon's Tuesday evening came to an early end.
articles.body:
Becky Hammon's Tuesday evening came to an early end.

The Las Vegas Aces head coach was ejected in the second quarter of her team's game against the Atlanta Dream. She was upset with something and picked up a technical foul, which only made her angrier and caused her to come on the floor and pick up a second and the ejection that came with it:

Enes Kanter Freedom Ejected from WNBA Game

The double-technical came on an empty offensive possession for the Dream.

However, Hammon appeared frustrated with a no-call or something that happened earlier in the game and let the officials know about it.

It was part of a disappointing opening half for Las Vegas, which saw its first quarter lead turn into an 11-point halftime deficit. Her team had no early answers for the trio of Angel Reese, Allisha Gray and Jordin Canada.

What's more, Atlanta took advantage of its 12 first-half free throws by making all of them.

While the Aces entered Tuesday's contest in solid playoff position at 24-12, they have been inconsistent of late. They lost three of their previous five contests, one of which was a blowout 40-point defeat on the road against the New York Liberty.

As a result of the recent struggles, Las Vegas has fallen into fourth place in the crowded WNBA standings as it and everyone else chases the top-seeded Minnesota Lynx.

As for Hammon, this is her fifth season as the head coach of the Aces. They have established themselves as the gold standard of the league under her coaching and took home three of the last four titles.

articles.title: 3-Team NBA Trade Idea After Cleveland Cavaliers' Failed LeBron James Pursuit
articles.summary: The Cleveland Cavaliers were one of the spurned suitors, hoping LeBron James would return home for a third stint. Once James chose the Philadelphia 76ers, it was assumed free-agent guard James Harden would re-sign with the Cavs.
articles.body:
The Cleveland Cavaliers were one of the spurned suitors, hoping LeBron James would return home for a third stint. Once James chose the Philadelphia 76ers, it was assumed free-agent guard James Harden would re-sign with the Cavs.

Instead, Harden remains unsigned, a situation believed to give Cleveland flexibility to add talent elsewhere on the roster. He could take less in the first year of a three-year contract rather than sign a larger, shorter two-year deal. The Cavaliers then agreed to send Dennis Schröder to the Charlotte Hornets for Tre Mann.

Per Marc Stein , Cleveland is considered "a team to watch" in the Peyton Watson sweepstakes, with Max Strus and Schröder among the players who could be included. The challenge for the Cavs in executing a sign-and-trade for the Denver Nuggets' restricted free-agent forward is staying below the $221.7 million first-apron hard cap while accounting for Watson, Harden and 14 standard contracts.

Assuming the Hornets trade goes through as a standalone transaction—though that could also evolve into a multi-team swap—Cleveland and Denver would need help from a team like the Memphis Grizzlies to bring Watson to the land of wine and gold.

2030 protected first-round pick (from Cavaliers)

$11.6 million trade exception (Peyton Watson)

$5.1 million trade exception (Zeke Nnaji)

2028 Minnesota Timberwolves second-rounder (from Nuggets)

2031 Sacramento Kings second-rounder (from Nuggets)

2032 Sacramento Kings second-rounder (from Cavaliers)

$2.4 million trade exception (GG Jackson II)

The Cavaliers covet a big wing, and Watson at 6'8" is a primary target. Almost 24, the UCLA product shot a career-best 41.1 percent from three-point range last season on 3.6 attempts per game. Averaging 14.6 points per game, he'd fill the slot recently vacated by De'Andre Hunter, who was traded ahead of the February deadline to the Sacramento Kings.

Cleveland also saw vital defender Dean Wade leave for Philadelphia and is parting with Strus in the deal, setting up the starting lineup of Donovan Mitchell, Evan Mobley, Jarrett Allen, Harden, and Watson. Depth would require strong support from Sam Merrill, Jaylon Tyson, Mario Hezonja, Nae'Qwan Tomlin, Thomas Bryant, Craig Porter Jr., and Mann, among others.

As for budget, the Cavs have almost $47 million to spend on Watson and Harden for 2026-27. If that's $23.3 million for Watson on a four-year, $100 million contract, Harden could sign at about $22.5 million for $70.9 million over three years. Both angle for player options before their final seasons, but that's for the franchise to negotiate.

With 14 players under contract, plus three two-ways, the Cavaliers can sign a minimum free agent, possibly after a contract buyout, in March.

Cleveland would fight to protect its 2030 first, with something like top-5 protection; otherwise, unprotected in 2031. Watson is acquired using the expanded traded player exception generated by Strus, which is also a first-apron hard cap trigger.

The Nuggets project to have the highest payroll in the league this season, before considering the $25 million average Watson is believed to be seeking in a new contract.

Many sources around the league anticipated Denver would look to part ways with Cam Johnson, Christian Braun, or even Aaron Gordon to reduce payroll and make room to retain Watson. Instead, the Nuggets weren't seen as aggressively pursuing that path, even as other franchises had greater financial flexibility earlier in the summer.

Watson may have priced himself out of Denver's range. The team would match an offer sheet in the $15 million non-taxpayer mid-level exception range, but even that would drive the team's tax burden to approximately $175 million. Watson, at the numbers the Cavaliers are giving in this scenario, would push that penalty to over $241 million, driving Denver's decision to go in a different direction.

Instead, the Nuggets get a still-promising 21-year-old forward in Jackson from the Grizzlies. The team has room for one more player on a minimum deal, perhaps bringing back Bruce Brown Jr. With Nnaji's exit, the team successfully drops below the second apron with about $54 million in repeater taxes. That's an inevitable burden, but a reasonable one for a franchise maintaining championship aspirations around Nikola Jokić, one of the league's premier players.

Denver also clears Nnaji from next year's books, assuming he opts into his $7.5 million final season. Parting with Watson may be bittersweet, but the Nuggets also yield a first-round pick from the Cavaliers. Jackson is acquired in exchange for Nnaji; the Watson trade exception is for half of his starting salary.

The two trade exceptions aren't likely to factor in this season, as the team officially locks in a second-apron hard cap at $221.7 million by sending cash to the Grizzlies.

Offseason Overreactions for Every Team 🫨

In addition to getting "a pretty man" (per Charles Barkley), the Grizzlies add a capable all-around guard/forward in Strus. For a rebuilding team, the 30-year-old represents a valuable veteran leader to put around rookie No. 3 pick Cameron Boozer.

With the NBA's new lottery system, teams have an incentive to avoid the bottom of the standings. In the competitive Western Conference, Memphis needs to field a reasonably viable squad.

Along with other young players like Cedric Coward, Jaylen Wells, Zach Edey, Olivier-Maxence Prosper, and Karim Lopez, the Grizzlies add Strus to recently acquired vets like Jerami Grant, Isaiah Stewart, and Ty Jerome. The squad isn't likely to push for a playoff berth, but should be able to avoid bottoming out.

Beyond losing Jackson, who is likely to be buried in the rotation given the roster glut at his position, Memphis gains Strus on an expiring contract and three seconds. The team also takes on Nnaji, 25, with one year left on his deal via player option. Whether he's a part of the team's future or expendable is up to the franchise, but the Cavaliers and Nuggets subsidize almost half of his two-year deal, sending $3.5 million apiece to the Grizzlies.

Both Strus and Nnaji are absorbed via the preexisting Jaren Jackson Jr. trade exception, leaving a $4.7 million remainder. Memphis already has a first-apron hard cap but is nowhere near the $200.4 million luxury tax line.

The larger issue for the franchise is roster space. Before the trade, the team waives D'Angelo Russell, Kris Murray, and AJ Johnson—each acquired in larger deals this offseason and expendable to the Grizzlies. One more trade or cut would be needed before opening night, likely Taylor Hendricks or Nnaji, even with the latter's additional year on the books.

It's not an earth-shattering deal for the Grizzlies, helping the Cavaliers round out their roster, the Nuggets under the second apron, and resolving Watson's restricted free agency—but Nnaji's contract is light, the second-rounders are valuable, and Strus is a solid get for a team that can't afford to be dreadful.

Or Memphis can choose to pivot and flip his expiring contract ahead of the February trade deadline, as several playoff-caliber teams would view him favorably.

articles.title: Angel Reese, A'ja Wilson's Final Box Score Stats, Highlights as Dream Beat Aces Amid Hammon Ejection
articles.summary: The Atlanta Dream's trio of All-Stars—guards Rhyne Howard and Allisha Gray plus forward Angel Reese—dominated on both ends Tuesday evening en route to a 97-82 road win over the Las Vegas Aces despite WNBA MVP favorite A'ja Wilson's 27-point, 14-rebound outing.
articles.body:
The Atlanta Dream's trio of All-Stars—guards Rhyne Howard and Allisha Gray plus forward Angel Reese—dominated on both ends Tuesday evening en route to a 97-82 road win over the Las Vegas Aces despite WNBA MVP favorite A'ja Wilson's 27-point, 14-rebound outing.

Here's a look at some box score statistics and highlights.

Reese posted her 24th double-double of the season and now averages 15.7 points and 12.0 rebounds per game.

She also helped spearhead a tremendous defensive effort. The Dream amassed 15 steals, including four apiece from Howard and Reese. Atlanta also held Wilson to 7-of-18 shooting.

Howard, a four-time All-Star, continues to drop buckets with another 20-plus point game.

Gray also stayed hot after scoring 61 total points over her previous two games against the Connecticut Sun (29 points in just 28 minutes) and Indiana Fever (32 points, tied for her WNBA career-high).

Atlanta turned this game around in the second quarter after trailing 25-24 entering the frame. The Dream outscored the Aces 28-16 and ultimately took a 52-41 halftime lead.

Reese, Howard and Gray all hit threes during the second quarter.

Las Vegas didn't go away and cut the Dream lead to six points (88-82) after a pair of Wilson free throws with 1:46 remaining in regulation. Wilson certainly had her moments in this one.

However, the Dream ended the game on a 9-0 run. Gray got it started with a jumper, and then Jordin Canada made a layup after a Reese steal. Howard closed the scoring with a three-point play and then a pair of free throws.

This game also saw Aces head coach Becky Hammon get ejected following two technicals in the second quarter.

"(Hammon) felt like A'ja (Wilson) had gotten fouled a couple of times," Aces assistant coach Charlene Thomas-Swinson told reporters postgame (Hammon did not speak with the media after the contest). "It is the lens of a referee being able to not see the right angle, but you see.

"(Hammon) had asked for that a couple of times, and unfortunately it just didn't work out."

The fifth-place Dream, who now hold a 22-13 record, will play the second matchup of its four-game Western Conference road trip at the Los Angeles Sparks. The third-place Aces (24-13) will host the Connecticut Sun.

articles.title: Caitlin Clark Calls Out Fever's Play and Canada's Air Conditioning on Video After Win vs. Tempo
articles.summary: The Indiana Fever fought through a valiant effort from the Toronto Temple and the lack of an effective cooling system in the Coca-Cola Coliseum to earn their fifth straight win on Tuesday night.
articles.body:
The Indiana Fever fought through a valiant effort from the Toronto Temple and the lack of an effective cooling system in the Coca-Cola Coliseum to earn their fifth straight win on Tuesday night.

After the Fever's 101-95 victory in Toronto, Caitlin Clark told ESPN's Holly Rowe they "didn't play their best" but they were "happy to take a win when we can get it."

Asked about Kelsey Mitchell's fourth-quarter absence, Clark joked it would "probably be helpful" if Canada had air conditioning because it was "a million degrees" in the arena.

Mitchell was able to extend her streak of 20-point games to 20, tying the WNBA record originally set by A'ja Wilson. She sat out the fourth quarter due to being "overheated," per Fever head coach Stephanie White .

"This is two games in a row where we played in really, really hot environments," White said. "All indications are right now that she was just overheated."

Even though the heat from the arena was causing Mitchell problems, the real flames were coming from Clark and the Fever's offense. They hit the 100-point mark for the 16th time in 36 games.

Clark finished with 24 points and seven assists in 33 minutes. She has scored at least 20 points in six consecutive games. The three-time All-Star is averaging 26..1 points on 41.4 percent three-point shooting and 9.2 assists per game in 12 starts since July 17.

Indiana has won 10 of its last 12 games to improve to 24-12 overall. The Fever are in sole possession of third place in the playoff standings and just two games behind the Golden State Valkyries for the No. 2 seed.

Next up for Clark and the Fever is a matchup with Paige Bueckers and the Dallas Wings on Thursday.

articles.title: Angel Reese 'Didn't Sleep' After Missing Potential GW Shot in Dream's Loss to Caitlin Clark, Fever
articles.summary: Atlanta Dream forward Angel Reese told reporters that she "didn't sleep" after her team's tough 95-91 overtime home loss to the Indiana Fever on Sunday, when the three-time All-Star missed a game-winning layup attempt with three seconds left in regulation.
articles.body:
Atlanta Dream forward Angel Reese told reporters that she "didn't sleep" after her team's tough 95-91 overtime home loss to the Indiana Fever on Sunday, when the three-time All-Star missed a game-winning layup attempt with three seconds left in regulation.

Reese provided those remarks Tuesday after she and her team bounced back with a 97-82 road win over the Las Vegas Aces.

Reese was asked in the postgame press conference about stepping up defensively against WNBA MVP favorite A'ja Wilson, especially with Dream forward Brionna Jones dealing with a leg injury that sidelined her for this matchup.

She provided this response (6:25 mark), per MTMV Sports Network.

"Yeah, I knew how much my team needed me. Like I said last game, it was very tough for me. I didn't sleep, and the competitor in me wanted to win that game so bad, I replayed that play so many times, but I'm like, why would I let one moment dictate everything else that I have going on that is positive?

"So just being able to show up again for my team. It would have been negative for me not to come out tonight and just bounce back, and I knew they expected it from me, so just being able to do it obviously against [Aces star center A'ja Wilson], trying to deflect as many passes as I can, I mean she's going to get her shots up of course. But just knowing my spots and how great I am defensively to put pressure on her."

The Fever and Dream were tied at 81 as time wound down on Sunday. Dream guard Rhyne Howard launched a deep three-pointer, but the shot ended up being an airball. Reese was perfectly positioned for the rebound but missed the putback. Indiana led for the final 3:31 of overtime en route to the win, and Caitlin Clark guided the Fever with a team-high 26 points.

It was a mixed game for Reese, who had 15 points, 14 rebounds and six assists. However, she also went 5-of-16 from the field and committed four turnovers.

Reese responded quite well on Tuesday, though, with 21 points, 10 rebounds, four assists and four steals. She played tough defense on Wilson, who was productive as usual (27 points, 14 rebounds) but shot 7-of-18.

Atlanta has now won nine of 12 games to move to 22-13 overall, good enough for fifth in the WNBA standings. The Dream will look to maintain that positive momentum on Thursday at the Los Angeles Sparks.

articles.title: Tyrese Maxey Says 76ers Players Can't Have an 'Ego' After LeBron James Contract, Jaylen Brown Trade
articles.summary: After significant changes that brought in Jaylen Brown and LeBron James, the Philadelphia 76ers will start the 2026-27 season trying to figure out how the new pieces fit in with the already-established players on the roster.
articles.body:
After significant changes that brought in Jaylen Brown and LeBron James, the Philadelphia 76ers will start the 2026-27 season trying to figure out how the new pieces fit in with the already-established players on the roster.

Speaking to Sam Yip of HoopsHype about the offseason acquisitions, Sixers star Tyrese Maxey explained the most important thing for all of them is not having any "ego" that gets in the way of what they want to collectively accomplish:

"I think the biggest thing is we can't have anybody, nobody on this team can have an ego. We have two guys that have won regular-season MVPs, two guys that have won Finals MVPs, multiple gold medal winners on this team, multiple 25-plus points per game, All-Stars, All-NBA. We're all pretty accomplished. So the ego has to drop and you have to do it collectively."

Jayson Tatum's dad blunt about Celtics roster

Amid all of the justified excitement in Philadelphia about Brown and James came questions of how a team with four ball-dominant players would have enough touches to keep them all involved and maximize their skill sets.

There is also the need for VJ Edgecombe to get more opportunities as he tries to build on a strong rookie season into a potential All-Star after being selected with the No. 3 overall pick in the 2025 NBA draft.

Maxey and Brown both averaged more than 21 field-goal attempts per game last season. Joel Embiid has averaged at least 18 field-goal attempts per game in four of the last five seasons.

James got acclimated to sacrificing offensive production last season with the Los Angeles Lakers with Luka Dončić and Austin Reaves as the primary scoring engines.

76ers general manager Mike Gansey explained the issue of touches as a positive because it means on "any given night, anyone can be the guy."

It's a task that head coach Nick Nurse and his staff will have to figure out, but there is also going to be a feeling-out process early in the season while Maxey, Brown, James, Edgecombe and Joel Embiid figure out how to play together.

The depth of star talent also allows the Sixers to ease the burden on players like James and Embiid given the former's age and latter's injury history. Keeping everyone healthy and at close to peak form by the time the playoffs come around is the most critical thing for Philadelphia in 2026-27.

articles.title: Paige Bueckers, Azzi Fudd Discuss Relationship in New Video from UConn Dynasty Documentary
articles.summary: Dallas Wings stars Paige Bueckers and Azzi Fudd are publicly speaking about their romantic relationship for the first time since becoming WNBA teammates in a UConn women's basketball documentary being released this weekend on Apple TV.
articles.body:
Dallas Wings stars Paige Bueckers and Azzi Fudd are publicly speaking about their romantic relationship for the first time since becoming WNBA teammates in a UConn women's basketball documentary being released this weekend on Apple TV.

Bueckers talked about Fudd, who joined UConn during Bueckers' sophomore year, in a clip released Wednesday by the streaming platform.

"It kind of just meshed as soon as we met," Bueckers said in the clip. "She's sweet, she's genuine. She has a huge, caring heart. We kind of felt a spark a little bit different than what would just be a normal friendship."

Fudd added: "Paige and I are a couple, and everyone close to us that was important knew, but it was kind of one of those things— it's private, not a secret, but it's private."

The Wings drafted Fudd with the No. 1 pick in April, one year after selecting Bueckers at the top of the 2025 draft.

Fudd and Bueckers have since asked reporters for privacy about their relationship during Fudd's rookie WNBA season.

Apple TV's docuseries "The Dynasty: UConn Huskies" is set to premiere Friday.

The three-part docuseries starts with coach Geno Auriemma joining the program in 1985 and features interviews with former Huskies stars including Rebecca Lobo, Sue Bird and Diana Taurasi before culminating in Fudd and Bueckers' national title run in 2025.

articles.title: Patrick Beverley Defends Russell Westbrook, Calls Out Media for Portrayal of NBA Icon's Game
articles.summary: Russell Westbrook's retirement from the NBA surprised those who felt he still had something left in the tank, even one of his longtime rivals.
articles.body:
Russell Westbrook's retirement from the NBA surprised those who felt he still had something left in the tank, even one of his longtime rivals.

During the latest episode of The Pat Bev Show , former NBA point guard Patrick Beverley, who once had a contentious relationship with Westbrook before teaming together on the Los Angeles Lakers, asserted that the media played a role in the diminished perception of the nine-time All-Star, forcing him to end his career prematurely.

"I'm going to be honest. I felt like he had a lot of game left. I feel like he played really well last season. I think the media killed his game," Beverley said (h/t BasketNews.com ). "I'm going to be honest. I think the media is so strong that it allowed fans to call him names and have opinions about his game, which also forced team owners, GMs, and presidents to look at him a certain way."

Jayson Tatum's dad blunt about Celtics roster

Westbrook ended his 18-year NBA career after spending the 2025-26 season with the Sacramento Kings. He was a productive contributor with averages of 15.2 points, 6.7 assists and 5.4 rebounds across 64 games. He reportedly had offers from the Kings and Washington Wizards to continue his career, but he turned them down to retire on his own terms.

Still, Beverley said he felt Westbrook was more talented than a host of other NBA players and deserved another chance to extend his career.

"When you talk about guards in the NBA, and no disrespect to guys on current teams, but when you talk about Lonnie Walker, he's a good friend of mine, but if he can make an NBA team, Russell Westbrook can make an NBA team without a doubt," Beverley said.

articles.title: Sparks' Nneka Ogwumike to Retire from WNBA After 2026 Season, Won Title and MVP in 2016
articles.summary: Los Angeles Sparks forward Nneka Ogwumike is calling it a career this year.
articles.body:
Los Angeles Sparks forward Nneka Ogwumike is calling it a career this year.

During an interview for Boardroom with Taylor Rooks, Ogwumike announced that she will retire at the end of the 2026 season. The 15-year veteran spent 13 years with the Sparks and helped lead the team to a WNBA championship in 2016, the same year she was named WNBA MVP.

"I've learned there's power in knowing when to walk away. For so long, that strength meant finding a way to keep pushing. Now, it means recognizing when you feel complete," Ogwumike said (h/t ESPN's Alexa Philippou ). "I find myself grateful, fulfilled, and at peace with everything this game has given me and everything I've poured into it."

In a post on Instagram, Atlanta Dream forward Angel Reese paid tribute to Ogwumike's career, writing , "Since I came into the league, you've shown me nothing but love and treated me like I was one of your own. My first vet. One of my GOATS."

"Thank you for always pouring into me, believing in me, and having my back," Reese added. "Like I already told you, your 15 years in this league were FLAWLESS, but somehow the person you are off the court speaks even louder than everything you accomplished on."

WNBPA executive director Terri Carmichael Jackson also released a statement praising Ogwumike's career.

"Nneka Ogwumike's impact on this union, and on the women's game, cannot be overstated. Her leadership has been extraordinary. She has served this union with a level of commitment, courage, integrity, and purpose that is truly unparalleled," she wrote. "As President for the last decade, Nneka understood that leadership was not simply about having a seat at the table; it was about using that seat to move the game and the business of the game forward for every player — today and for generations to come.

"We are profoundly grateful for the countless ways Nneka has championed her teammates, strengthened this union, and helped shape its future. We celebrate her remarkable career and the next chapter ahead. Nneka's legacy will forever be woven into the fabric of this union and women's basketball."

The No. 1 pick in the 2012 WNBA draft out of Stanford, Ogwumike made an immediate impact when she entered the league, earning Rookie of the Year honors. She went on to become an 11-time All-Star, an eight-time All-WNBA selection and a seven-time All-Defensive selection. She was named to the WNBA 25th Anniversary Team in 2021.

In addition to suiting up for the Sparks, Ogwumike spent two seasons with the Seattle Storm in 2024 and 2025 before returning to Los Angeles for the 2026 campaign. She's started all 34 of her appearances for the 12-23 Sparks this season and is averaging 16.9 points, 8.7 rebounds, 3.0 assists and 1.1 steals.

Ogwumike's impact off the court has also been commendable, as she earned the Kim Perrot Sportsmanship Award four times in her career, including in 2025.

Ogwumike will be remembered as one of the most consistent two-way players the WNBA has ever seen, and she will now get to enjoy the next chapter of her life when the 2026 season comes to an end.

articles.title: Luka Doncic Charters Plane to Slovenia for Lakers, Details for Team-Bonding Trip Revealed in Video
articles.summary: It was already known Luka Dončić was planning a team-bonding trip to Slovenia for his Los Angeles Lakers teammates, but now we have details of what the trip will entail.
articles.body:
It was already known Luka Dončić was planning a team-bonding trip to Slovenia for his Los Angeles Lakers teammates, but now we have details of what the trip will entail.

Appearing on ESPN Los Angeles' Mason & Ireland show, ESPN's Ramona Shelburne explained Dončić chartered a plane for 14 members of the Lakers, who will receive gift bags, eat at his favorite restaurant, fish at Lake Bled and golf during the five-day excursion.

ESPN's Dave McMenamin reported last month that Dončić was preparing a four-day "minicamp" in August to help the revamped roster develop chemistry away from the court.

It was believed that at least 16 of the 17 players under contract to the Lakers were planning to go, including Austin Reaves, Walker Kessler and Bronny James.

This has been a significant offseason for the Lakers, in ways both anticipated and unexpected. The departure of LeBron James in free agency wasn't a total shock.

It did open the door for the front office to continue reshaping the roster to better fit around Dončić. Their biggest move was acquiring Kessler from the Utah Jazz in a sign-and-trade in which he signed a four-year, $130 million contract.

The Lakers also added Sandro Mamukelashvili, Quentin Grimes via free agency and drafted Cameron Carr in the first round.

articles.summary: The Philadelphia 76ers' two newest stars have officially started working out together.
articles.body:
The Philadelphia 76ers' two newest stars have officially started working out together.

LeBron James and Jaylen Brown were photographed working out with Tyrese Maxey in Los Angeles in photos shared by trainer Chris Johnson on Instagram .

Both returning Sixers star Maxey and Brown , who was acquired earlier this offseason from the Boston Celtics, reportedly played roles in recruiting James to sign with the Sixers.

Maxey and James have been photographed working out with one another since that deal was signed.

The duo has now been joined by Brown with about four weeks left until the start of training camp and just over two months remaining until the Sixers tip off the regular season Oct. 20 against the New York Knicks.
