articles.title: Tyrese Maxey Talks Who Takes Last Shot for 76ers After LeBron James, Jaylen Brown Additions
articles.summary: Philadelphia 76ers star Tyrese Maxey weighed in on the team's No. 1 scoring option in clutch scenarios following the offseason additions of LeBron James and Jaylen Brown.
articles.body:
Philadelphia 76ers star Tyrese Maxey weighed in on the team's No. 1 scoring option in clutch scenarios following the offseason additions of LeBron James and Jaylen Brown.

"I think it depends on what the situation is, you know what I'm saying? I think we have confidence in a lot of different guys," Maxey said in an interview with HoopsHype's Sam Yip . "I think people want to say VJ is our fifth option, but last year he took a lot of shots in the clutch. He made a lot of shots in the clutch. There was a couple times, where I got doubled and Joel [Embiid] got doubled and we had to kick it out to VJ [Edgecombe] and he had to make a shot. It's going to be different people. We're going to see how it goes and see how it flows."

Maxey also explained that nobody on the 76ers' new-look starting lineup can have an ego in order for the team to be successful.

"I think the biggest thing is we can't have anybody, nobody on this team can have an ego," Maxey told Yip. "We have two guys that have won regular-season MVPs, two guys that have won Finals MVPs, multiple gold medal winners on this team, multiple 25-plus points per game, All-Stars, All-NBA. We're all pretty accomplished. So the ego has to drop and you have to do it collectively."

After wrapping up a 45-37 finish and advancing to the second round of the playoffs last season, the 76ers acquired Brown in a blockbuster trade with the Boston Celtics on July 1 before landing James in free agency on July 24.

They're set to join a starting lineup that already includes Maxey, Joel Embiid and VJ Edgecombe.

It'll be intriguing to see how Philadelphia's pecking order on offense develops with two new stars entering the mix.

Brown and Maxey ranked No. 2 and No. 3 among all players in field-goal attempts per game last season, respectively. Meanwhile, Embiid has served as the 76ers' leading scorer throughout the majority of his career and averaged 26.9 points on a nightly basis during his 2025-26 campaign.

James also has plenty of experience as an offensive engine and has remained productive in close games, shooting 57.6 percent from the field in clutch situations last year (via NBA.com ).

The Sixers will open the 2026-27 season against the New York Knicks on Oct. 20.

articles.title: The Denver Nuggets Are Failing Nikola Jokić
articles.summary: August is often a quiet stretch of the NBA's calendar, but the volume ratcheted way up Wednesday when ESPN's Shams Charania reported that the Denver Nuggets were trading one of Nikola Jokić's most intriguing young teammates, Peyton Watson, to the Cleveland Cavaliers in a five-team deal.
articles.body:
August is often a quiet stretch of the NBA's calendar, but the volume ratcheted way up Wednesday when ESPN's Shams Charania reported that the Denver Nuggets were trading one of Nikola Jokić's most intriguing young teammates, Peyton Watson, to the Cleveland Cavaliers in a five-team deal.

In a vacuum, the move is maybe justifiable.

Offseason Overreactions for Every Team 🫨

Watson has a career average of 8.7 points and a 36.1 three-point percentage. Without the one truly high-level stretch of his NBA career (January of this year), those numbers are even worse .

With little more than that context to rely on, Denver's unwillingness to pay him $22 million per year and plunge itself that much further past the second apron might seem fair. (The Nuggets were already above the second apron even without Watson.)

The problem is that there's more context. A lot more.

Chief among the reasons why this deal has been widely pilloried is what it appears to say about the organization's commitment to Jokić.

He isn't just the best player in franchise history. Statistically, he's one of the best players in NBA history .

Jokić is first all-time in career player efficiency rating , box plus/minus and win shares per 48 minutes (catch-all metrics that endeavor to quantify a player's impact in a single number). He's tied for first all-time in career triple-doubles (including the playoffs). He's one of just 10 players in league history with three MVPs. And he's sixth all-time in career MVP shares, behind only LeBron James, Michael Jordan, Kareem Abdul-Jabbar, Larry Bird and Magic Johnson.

Despite all of the accolades he's already piled up, Jokić is smack-dab in the middle of his prime. The 31-year-old has a mostly ground-bound game that should age relatively well. And his team basically just punted on the restricted free agency of its biggest and perhaps best upside bet.

Moving Watson for a first-round pick that won't convey until Jokić is 36 years old—with no players along with it, young or otherwise—all but seals this summer being a fourth straight loser since the Nuggets won the championship in 2023.

In the offseason immediately after the title run, Denver lost Bruce Brown (although CBA rules made that one inevitable). The next summer, Kentavious Caldwell-Pope walked. In 2025, they traded Michael Porter Jr. and draft capital for Cameron Johnson and lost Russell Westbrook. Along the way, they signed Dario Šarić, Jonas Valančiūnas, both of whom are gone.

This summer, they lost Watson and Tim Hardaway Jr. For most of that stretch, Zeke Nnaji's inexplicable four-year extension (which comes with a $7.5 million player option in 2027-28) has been on the books. And at one point, the front office attached three second-round picks to salary dump Reggie Jackson.

Individually, up until the Watson move—and with the exception of a handful of others, like Nnaji and Jackson—there were reasonable explanations. The Porter-for-Johnson swap, in particular, added flexibility without losing shooting. However, MPJ quickly showed how much higher the Nuggets' ceiling might've been with him when he averaged 25.6 points, 3.8 threes and 3.2 assists while shooting 39.8 percent from deep in his first 38 games with the Brooklyn Nets.

Even some of the moves that could be justified at the time, like the Porter deal or Christian Braun's extension, are off to rough starts. When you look at everything over the last four offseasons together, it feels disastrous.

Jokić is the kind of talent whose presence on a roster guarantees competitiveness, but winning at the highest level requires more than that. It certainly requires more than tactically retreating year after year.

If the basketball world at large perceives Denver's post-championship approach as that, it's not hard to imagine Jokić starting to see it the same.

For years, whenever the subject comes up, Jokić has insisted that he wants to stick with the Nuggets for his entire career. He opted not to sign an extension this summer because he can sign for more (five years and more than $350 million) next summer, but nothing's guaranteed.

This roster is better than the general reaction it's gotten this summer. Jamal Murray is in his prime and played at an All-NBA level last season. Aaron Gordon is among the best and most versatile third options in the league. For long stretches of last season, Johnson looked like the ideal gap-filler for this roster.

If Braun is healthier, he could bounce back to around the level that earned him his big payday. Marvin Bagley III was an underrated pickup this summer. And though he wouldn't come with the same upside as Watson, the rumored acquisition of DeMar DeRozan would uplift the bench.

The group could certainly outperform expectations, get back into the hunt for championships and give Jokić plenty of confidence to sign a massive contract next summer. But again, nothing is guaranteed.

Gordon's health has been a massive question mark since the Nuggets' title run. Johnson shot the ball well last season and is more consistent defensively than MPJ, but his offensive highs may not be as high. Braun may have just caught lightning in a bottle the season before signing his extension. And the non-Jokić minutes have been a wild ride for most of his MVP era.

With the Oklahoma City Thunder and San Antonio Spurs younger and more athletic than Denver, the Nuggets' kryptonite Minnesota Timberwolves adding LaMelo Ball and fewer teams blatantly tanking, Jokić could be in for another early playoff exit this coming season.

If that happens on the heels of these last four offseasons, especially if Watson's breakout continues for the Cavaliers, it would be hard to blame Jokić's eye for wandering toward other teams.

articles.title: Matas Buzelis Says Luka Doncic Dropped 'Nasty' Trash Talk During Bulls vs. Lakers Matchup
articles.summary: Luka Dončić is one of the best players in the NBA. He is also one of the league's best trash-talkers.
articles.body:
Luka Dončić is one of the best players in the NBA. He is also one of the league's best trash-talkers.

During an appearance on Cousins with Vince Carter & Tracy McGrady (53-minute mark), the Chicago Bulls forward recalled a time when Dončić was saying things he couldn't even repeat all while dropping 51 points in a Los Angeles Lakers victory.

"I don't really want to get into detail because it was some really like nasty things said, but he just started he started baking me bad, like 12 in a row, bad, and I was like I don't care, keep doing that, I don't care what you doing, keep scoring, we'll see if you can keep scoring," Buzelis said. "I have 20 at half and he has 22. So I'm chilling.

"So I end with like 23. ... And he ends with like 50. And it's just man, he hit this one shot. ... And I'm not even trying to glaze or anything, but he shot it. … He was isoing, and he does that step back, shot it. I feel like in midair he like points directly down at me, and I'm in the corner, and he like turns around mid shot and it just went straight back rim. I was like, 'Oh god, that's not good.' They beat us by like 20. In the media I was saying that I'm probably not going to trash talk again to him, but I really don't care. I'm going to do it again."

While Buzelis deserves some credit for not backing down when it comes to the trash-talk department, there is something to be said about not poking the bear when it comes to some players in the NBA.

And Dončić is certainly one of those players.

The specific game Buzelis referenced was Los Angeles' 142-130 victory over the Bulls on March 12. Dončić ended up with 51 points, 10 rebounds and nine assists on 17-of-31 shooting from the field and a head-turning 9-of-14 shooting from deep.

Austin Reaves also ended up with 30 points, but he, along with everyone else, was an afterthought to Dončić's individual brilliance.

It was yet another reminder of how unstoppable the future Hall of Famer can be when he gets rolling, and he surely let Buzelis and everyone else on the Bulls know about it as he was dropping 51 points.

articles.title: UNC to Face Kentucky, Arkansas, Indiana on Non-Conference Schedule for Michael Malone's 1st Season
articles.summary: Heading into Michael Malone's first season as head coach, North Carolina has finalized its non-conference schedule for the 2026-27 campaign.
articles.body:
Heading into Michael Malone's first season as head coach, North Carolina has finalized its non-conference schedule for the 2026-27 campaign.

The Tar Heels dropped their 17-game out-of-conference games on Thursday, including marquee matchups against Indiana on Oct. 18, Arkansas on Dec. 1 and Kentucky on Dec. 19.

Six of the games will be played at neutral-site locations. Gainbridge Fieldhouse in Indianapolis will play host to the matchup with the Hoosiers. The game will also be a preseason exhibition contest.

The Tar Heels will face Kentucky at Madison Square Garden. Other venues they will play in include Spectrum Center in Charlotte (vs. West Virginia), First Horizon Coliseum in Greensboro (vs. NC State) and Bridgestone Arena in Nashville (vs. Illinois).

In addition to its non-conference schedule, North Carolina will play 17 games against ACC competition. Dates and times for those games has not yet been announced.

This season marks the start of a new era in Chapel Hill with Malone taking over as head coach. He is replacing Hubert Davis, who was fired in March after the Tar Heels lost in the first round of the NCAA tournament to VCU.

Davis went 125-54 in five seasons and made the NCAA tournament four times, reaching the Final Four in his first season in 2021-22.

Malone was hired on April 7, marking his first stint as a head coach at the college level. He has experience in college, having spent eight seasons as an assistant at three different universities from 1994 to 2001.

The 54-year-old Malone has 12 seasons of head-coaching experience in the NBA, including a 10-year run with the Denver Nuggets from 2015 to '25. He owns a 510-394 career record and won the 2022-23 NBA championship.

articles.title: Dan Hurley Shares Photos Rewatching UConn's Dramatic March Madness Win vs. Duke on IG
articles.summary: Sports fans constantly relive old games and highlights, especially the dramatic ones that saw their teams prevail.
articles.body:
Sports fans constantly relive old games and highlights, especially the dramatic ones that saw their teams prevail.

It turns out, so does UConn men's basketball coach Dan Hurley.

UConn's 73-72 victory over Duke to clinch a spot in the Final Four was arguably the most dramatic game of the entire NCAA men's tournament last season, and the Huskies head coach relived it and experienced some of the emotions that came with Braylon Mullins' buzzer-beater all over again:

If Hurley is going to watch old highlights and post about them online, there are far worse games to choose than the one he did.

After all, it seemed like the Blue Devils were going to cruise to an Elite Eight victory when they built a 19-point lead in the first half. However, UConn gradually cut into the deficit and gave itself a chance in the final seconds.

With Duke leading by two in those final seconds, the Huskies deflected a Cayden Boozer pass near midcourt. The ball ended up in Mullins' hands, and he launched a shot from well beyond the arc to win it.

"It just felt like the window where you've just got to let March Madness take over," Hurley told reporters at the time. "March magic."

UConn ended up defeating Illinois in the Final Four before losing to Michigan in the national championship game. It was quite the run for a program that also won back-to-back national championships in 2023 and 2024 and has established itself as one of the gold standards in the sport.

Hurley was the head coach for both of those titles as well, but the Duke win has to be among the most memorable of his entire tenure.

So memorable, in fact, that he is reliving the highlights during the offseason.

It turns out, so does UConn men's basketball coach Dan Hurley.

UConn's 73-72 victory over Duke to clinch a spot in the Final Four was arguably the most dramatic game of the entire NCAA men's tournament last season, and the Huskies head coach relived it and experienced some of the emotions that came with Braylon Mullins' buzzer-beater all over again:
If Hurley is going to watch old highlights and post about them online, there are far worse games to choose than the one he did.

After all, it seemed like the Blue Devils were going to cruise to an Elite Eight victory when they built a 19-point lead in the first half. However, UConn gradually cut into the deficit and gave itself a chance in the final seconds.

With Duke leading by two in those final seconds, the Huskies deflected a Cayden Boozer pass near midcourt. The ball ended up in Mullins' hands, and he launched a shot from well beyond the arc to win it.
"It just felt like the window where you've just got to let March Madness take over," Hurley told reporters at the time. "March magic."

UConn ended up defeating Illinois in the Final Four before losing to Michigan in the national championship game. It was quite the run for a program that also won back-to-back national championships in 2023 and 2024 and has established itself as one of the gold standards in the sport.
Hurley was the head coach for both of those titles as well, but the Duke win has to be among the most memorable of his entire tenure.
So memorable, in fact, that he is reliving the highlights during the offseason.

articles.title: Cavs' Updated Salary Cap, Roster After James Harden's 3-Year, $97M Contract in NBA Free Agency
articles.summary: The Cleveland Cavaliers have been busy.
articles.body:
ESPN's Shams Charania reported Thursday the Cavs team agreed to a new three-year, $97 million contract with James Harden that includes a player option and a kicker.

A day earlier, Charania reported the Cavaliers acquired Peyton Watson in a deal with the Denver Nuggets and Los Angeles Clippers. ESPN's Bobby Marks said after the Watson deal that the Cavaliers would waive-and-stretch Cam Whitmore—who they also landed in the deal—over three years, which would allow the team to sign Harden.

Heat still have 2 rosters spot left after signing Klay

Jayson Tatum's dad blunt about Celtics roster

Max Strus ended up with the Clippers as part of the agreement, while Watson and the Cavaliers agreed to a new four-year, $88 million deal that features a player option and a trade kicker.

Here is a look at where things stand in Cleveland following those moves:

With Donovan Mitchell, Evan Mobley and Jarrett Allen already in place, trading for Watson and then giving a three-year deal to someone who turns 37 this month is a clear signal the front-office is in complete win-now mode.

Such an approach isn't particularly surprising seeing how Cleveland reached the Eastern Conference Finals last season and is coming off four straight playoff appearances.

Still, it is fair to wonder about the team's overall ceiling.

The New York Knicks swept the Cavaliers in those Eastern Conference Finals, suggesting Cleveland still has a ways to go to close the gap on the reigning champions. What's more, other teams in the Eastern Conference such as the Philadelphia 76ers and Miami Heat improved considerably this offseason.

Harden is a future Hall of Famer and one of the best players of his generation, but he likely isn't going to improve in his age-37 season and beyond. There are plenty of defensive concerns with a starting backcourt of Mitchell and Harden, although Watson at least gives the Cavaliers a versatile playmaker they didn't have last season.

For his part, this gives Harden some long-term certainty near the presumed end of his career.

He can continue adding to a resume that includes a league MVP, three scoring titles, two assist titles, eight All-NBA selections, a Sixth Man of the Year and 11 All-Star nods. And while he wasn't MVP level in 26 regular-season games for the Cavaliers in 2025-26 after they acquired him from the Los Angeles Clippers, he still put up solid numbers.

The Arizona State product averaged 20.5 points, 7.7 assists and 4.8 rebounds a night in those games and will look to build on that performance over the course of his new three-year deal.

articles.title: Dillon Brooks Says He 'Loves' Facing LeBron James, Lakers Playoff Game Meme 'Was Not Scripted'
articles.summary: One of the NBA's most notable recent rivalries is the one between LeBron James and Dillon Brooks.
articles.body:
One of the NBA's most notable recent rivalries is the one between LeBron James and Dillon Brooks.

But Brooks said he doesn't consider it a rivalry at this point.

"I love playing against him," Brooks said (5:30 mark). "Honestly, it's not even a rivalry; it's like a competitive spirit because I've watched him my whole life."

Jayson Tatum's dad blunt about Celtics roster

Brooks added that the meme of him sitting courtside at a Los Angeles Lakers game wasn't "scripted."

Brooks and the Phoenix Suns didn't face James in the playoffs this year, but that didn't stop him from getting a courtside seat to the Lakers' loss against the Oklahoma City Thunder.

That was just the latest wrinkle in the back-and-forth between Brooks and James.

The origin of the beef dates back to Brooks' time on the Memphis Grizzlies when he matched up against James and the Lakers in the first round of the 2023 NBA playoffs.

Brooks took his first shot at James after a chippy Game 2.

"I don't care—he's old. You know what I mean?" Brooks said after Memphis won Game 2. "I was waiting for that. I was expecting him to do that [in] Game 4, Game 5. He wanted to say something when I got my fourth foul. He should have been saying that earlier on. But I poke bears. I don't respect no one until they come and give me 40."

That quote, plus some of Brooks' antics on the court, sparked a years-long rivalry that hasn't seemed to slow down. Earlier this offseason, Brooks called himself James' "top" hater and told him to "stop all this waiting s--t" as James mulled his free agency decision.

With James getting closer and closer to retirement, it remains to be seen whether Brooks will lighten up when he goes up against the all-time great.

articles.title: Dillon Brooks Names Luka Doncic Among NBA's Top Foul-Baiters in New Video Ahead of 2026-27 Season
articles.summary: Foul-bating has become a widespread issue in the NBA, and Dillon Brooks isn't a fan of it.
articles.body:
Foul-bating has become a widespread issue in the NBA, and Dillon Brooks isn't a fan of it.

The Phoenix Suns forward recently named his top foul-baiters, with Luka Doncic headlining the group. He also included Shai Gilgeous-Alexander and Trae Young in his list (4:20 mark).

Brooks has previously given his thoughts on foul baiting, calling out the Oklahoma City Thunder during the playoffs last season.

"There are a lot of foul-baiters on that team, so we gotta show our hands," Brooks said ahead of the start of the first round. "I hope it's the real playoffs. They calling too many calls. Show your hands. We gotta follow the scout. Funnel them in the paint. Be able to have our rotations proper because they shoot it great at home. There's a reason they're the No. 1 team in the NBA."

NBA commissioner Adam Silver said in June that the league plans to address flopping further, and whether that will make a difference remains to be seen.

articles.title: Klay Thompson Calls Out 'Casuals' Over Ray Allen Debate, Cites Warriors Stats During NBA Title Runs
articles.summary: Klay Thompson defended himself in a debate amongst fans on social media on Thursday.
articles.body:
Klay Thompson defended himself in a debate amongst fans on social media on Thursday.

An Instagram post from the Swish List podcast was debating whether Thompson or Ray Allen is a better all-time player, and Thompson made his case against the legendary sharpshooter. Some fans were bringing up the two players' scoring numbers, which Thompson said were a reflection of how good their teams were.

"You do realize I was the second leading scorer on two championship teams without [Kevin Durant]? You want me to go to a bad team and put up empty stats, that's easy buddy," he commented on the post.

Offseason Overreactions for Every Team 🫨

He also pointed out his performance in the 2016 NBA Finals as fans downplayed his success with the Golden State Warriors.

"Holy s--t I led the 2016 playoffs in points scored you casuals," Thompson wrote.

Both Thompson and Allen were tremendous players in their primes, and both played a huge role on championship teams. Allen won a title with the Celtics and another with the Heat, while Thompson won four with Golden State.

It's a fair debate to have, but most NBA fans likely recognize that both players are among the best of their respective generations.

Thompson, perhaps getting some confidence with age, has had no problem responding to digs on social media this summer. Earlier this month, he called out his former teammate Kevin Durant when he said the current Philadelphia 76ers are better than his Warriors teams.

While most NBA players avoid discourse from fans on social media, Thompson has perhaps earned the right to defend his name after all the success he's had during his career.

The question now is how Thompson will continue adding to his legacy.

He recently said that he wants to "compete" for a title and "play a role on a team that can make a deep playoff run," and it's fair to say that the Mavs aren't exactly built to win a championship right now.

Thompson is under contract this season, but whether he'll request a trade remains to be seen.

articles.title: Caitlin Clark, Bueckers, Cunningham's Final Box Score Stats, Highlights as Wings Beat Fever
articles.summary: A pair of premier guards matched up on Thursday as Paige Bueckers and the Dallas Wings downed Caitlin Clark and the Indiana Fever 91-85.
articles.body:
A pair of premier guards matched up on Thursday as Paige Bueckers and the Dallas Wings downed Caitlin Clark and the Indiana Fever 91-85.

The Fever came in as 2.5-point favorites, according to FanDuel Sportsbook , but the Wings were looking to get a big win to improve their playoff position.

Bueckers had a bit of an off night, but luckily she had Jessica Sheppard and Arike Ogunbowale to lead the way for Dallas.

Clark likewise struggled a bit in the loss as she couldn't get much going on offense, but Kelsey Mitchell continued her tremendous season and kept the Fever alive for most of the night.

Dallas held a steady lead for most of the fourth quarter, but Indiana made a push in the final minutes. Ultimately, the Fever came up just short as the Wings were able to hold off the late run.

With the win, Dallas improved to 21-16 but still sits in eighth place in the WNBA standings. Luckily for the Wings, they're still sitting comfortably ahead of the ninth-place Portland Fire.

The Fever dropped to 24-13 with the loss and are now tied with the Las Vegas Aces for the third-best record in the league, but Indiana is closing in on clinching a playoff berth.

articles.title: La historia de hermanamiento más bonita del deporte con el Partizán de Belgrado y el Fuenlabrada como protagonistas
articles.standfirst: El conjunto serbio aprovechó su partido con el Getafe de la Conference League para visitar el pabellón Fernando Martín de baloncesto
articles.summary: El conjunto serbio aprovechó su partido con el Getafe de la Conference League para visitar el pabellón Fernando Martín de baloncesto
articles.body: Hay historias en el mundo del deporte que merecen ser contadas una y otra vez sin que uno se canse de escucharlas y disfrutarlas por asombrosas que son y por la repercusión emocional y deportiva que tienen. Y una de esas historias la protagonizan el Baloncesto Fuenlabrada y el Partizán de Belgrado. La historia de hermanamiento entre el conjunto del Sur de Madrid y el serbio nació la temporada 91-92, cuando en plena guerra de los Balcanes, el Partizán encontró cobijo en Fuenlabrada para disputar sus partidos de Euroliga en el Fernando Martín fuenlabreño, haciendo de la localidad madrileña un pequeño barrio serbio en el que encontró una afición que le llevó en volandas hacia el título europeo. Años más tarde ese hermanamiento sigue alimentándose y poniéndose de manifiesto cada vez que hay oportunidad, de hecho en los próximos días los de Iñaki Martín viajarán hasta Belgrado para disputar un amistoso de pretemporada donde son siempre recibidos con los brazos abiertos y con un cariño inimaginable haciendo de su visita a tierras serbias una ocasión perfecta para volver a celebrar aquella Euroliga.  Es tal la amistad entre ambos equipos y aficiones que aprovechando el partido de previa de la Conference League entre el Getafe y el Partizán de Belgrado que se disputó en el Coliseum, los ultras serbios quisieron aprovechar el viaje y peregrinar hasta Fuenlabrada, a escasos kilómetros de donde se disputaba su partido de fútbol, para visitar el Fernando Martín, pabellón donde hace más de treinta años se sintieron como en casa dejando claro una vez más que la historia entre el Baloncesto Fuenlabrada y el Partizán de Belgrado va más allá del básket, el fútbol o cualquier otra cosa, va de hermanamiento y de agradecimiento.

articles.title: Jury Says The New York Times Defamed Alabama Basketball Player with Incorrect Story About Shooting
articles.summary: TUSCALOOSA, Ala. (AP) — An Alabama jury on Thursday awarded $9.25 million in damages after finding that The New York Times defamed a college basketball player by incorrectly reporting that he was at the scene of a fatal shooting in Tuscaloosa.
articles.body:
TUSCALOOSA, Ala. (AP) — An Alabama jury on Thursday awarded $9.25 million in damages after finding that The New York Times defamed a college basketball player by incorrectly reporting that he was at the scene of a fatal shooting in Tuscaloosa.

Kai Spears, who played for the University of Alabama men's team, sued the Times in 2023 after it published a report , citing a person familiar with the investigation, that indicated he was a passenger in a car involved in the shooting. The Times reported that the person had spoken "on the condition of anonymity to discuss sensitive matters."

Days later, the Times acknowledged its error in an editor's note and corrected the story.

The eight-person jury delivered its verdict after a nine-day trial in the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of Alabama. Matt Glover, an attorney for Spears, said he was pleased with the decision and believes "this verdict will improve journalism throughout the country."

The Times was reviewing its legal options after losing in court, spokesperson Charlie Stadtlander said.

"We're disappointed the jury found The Times liable for an honest mistake," Stadtlander said in a statement Thursday. "We thank the jury for its service, but believe the verdict and award of damages are contrary to law and not supported by the evidence."

Three other basketball players from the school were present at the January 2023 shooting , which killed a 23-year-old mother. In the lawsuit, Spears claimed the inaccurate reporting had caused him emotional distress and forever linked him with a murder.

A Times article reporting on the verdict Thursday said the newspaper "had not lost a defamation lawsuit brought in the United States over one of its articles in more than 50 years."

articles.title: Is GG Banks Really Worth the Hype? Grading Every Aspect of the High School Phenom's Game
articles.summary: You might've seen the 17-year-old drilling shots alongside Shakira Austin and Elena Delle Donne at last month's WNBA All-Star Shooting Stars competition. Or maybe you've seen the viral clips of a shifty guard putting defenders in a blender at Overtime Select.
articles.body:
You might've seen the 17-year-old drilling shots alongside Shakira Austin and Elena Delle Donne at last month's WNBA All-Star Shooting Stars competition. Or maybe you've seen the viral clips of a shifty guard putting defenders in a blender at Overtime Select .

Well, that's GG Banks, a rising senior who is ranked No. 4 in the 2027 recruiting class. There's a lot of hype surrounding her, but just how good of a prospect is Banks?

I went through her film to break down every part of her game, from her athleticism and pick-and-roll playmaking to the shooting, defense and everything in between. Also, since she's only 17, a lot can change over the next few years, so there's plenty of upside baked into these grades.

When you watch Banks' film, it doesn't take long to realize just how ridiculous of an athlete she is. Guards who move like this don't exactly grow on trees.

She's incredibly explosive, but it's the combination of her speed, flexibility and change of direction that's really special. Banks can get downhill in a hurry, change speeds on a dime without losing much momentum and maneuver through tight spaces in ways most players can't.

That athleticism is especially dangerous in transition. Once Banks gets out in the open court, she covers ground in an instant before blowing past defenders. There's no question she will be one of the best transition scorers in college basketball.

And then there's the physical profile. Banks is listed on most sites at 5'8", but she has a 6'0" wingspan, which is significantly longer than most guards at her size. That length shows up when Banks is finishing with arms fully extended around the rim, but it also helps her make plays in passing lanes defensively.

Advantage creation is the name of the game at the point guard position. The best of them constantly put pressure on the defense, whether that's forcing help to come over off the drive or drawing two to the ball in pick-and-roll. That ability is one of the most impressive parts of Banks' game.

She has unbelievable feel for creating out of ball screens, and a lot of that starts with her handle. Banks is extremely creative with the ball, using inside-out dribbles, hesitations and left-right crossovers to keep defenders off balance. She loves to use her outside foot to sell defenders in one direction, then drive the other way.

Once you combine her improvisational skills with top-tier burst and acceleration, she's almost impossible to keep out of the paint. She gets to the rim so quickly she's consistently forcing weak-side defenders to help over, which leads to a lot of free throws and opens up things for her as a passer, too.

If you just watch Banks' highlights, one of the first things that jumps out is how impressive her gathers and high-difficulty finishes are. She has an incredible ability to contort her body around defenders to create openings. But sometimes, that creativity is a little too much.

Banks will often have a relatively easy layup available, only to make the finish much harder than it needs to be. Some of that comes down to her biggest improvement area: the left hand. At the high school level, Banks is so athletic and so skilled with the ball, she can get away with exclusively finishing with her strong hand right now. That won't always be the case at higher levels.

On the passing front, Banks is unsurprisingly really creative. She is a high-risk, high-reward passer, who attempts passes most players wouldn't even see. She consistently uses her eyes to manipulate defenders in ball screens and isn't afraid of making tight window passes.

Similar to all-world creators like Caitlin Clark and Olivia Miles, this style leads to a lot of assists but a good amount of turnovers as well. Across 16 games at 17U Nike EYBL, Banks averaged the third-most assists (5.5) and second-most turnovers (4.6) on the circuit.

The biggest question when it comes to Banks' on-ball operation is whether she can become a consistent shooter.

Right now, the three-point numbers just aren't there. She shot just 24 percent from three at 17U and 13.6 percent (3-of-22) across 5 games at Overtime Select, a league featuring the top high school players in the country.

One mechanical thing that stands out is the deep knee bend when she shoots. It can slow down her release, and at times, you'll see it cause her to leave shots short—especially off the dribble. The upper body mechanics aren't always compact, either.

Banks also attempted just one pull-up three (a miss) with Team USA at the U18 AmeriCup in June. Though, she did shoot 37.5 percent on catch-and-shoot threes (3-of-8), which were mostly all uncontested.

According to an article by On3's Hunter Shelton , Banks said her midrange game is one of the areas she's working hardest to improve.

If Banks can become even a reliable shooter, it changes the equation completely. Opponents already have to respect her first step and ability to get to the rim at-well. If she can punish them for going under screens with a consistent jumper, even more things will open up for her offensively—on and off the ball.

There's a lot of upside with Banks defensively, but there's definitely some inconsistency right now. Her footwork navigating screens can get a little choppy, and there are possessions where she simply isn't as engaged as you'd like.

But when she's locked in, you can see the flashes she has as a really disruptive defender. Banks' hands are extremely active, and she does a good job using her athleticism and length to get into passing lanes and create turnovers. She averaged 3.3 steals per game at 17U, which ranked second on the circuit.

The next step is to be more consistent on a possession-by-possession basis, but this isn't an unusual issue for a high-usage offensive creator at the high-school level. Banks has the athletic tools and a plus-wingspan; it's just about dialing in on the details.

The easy comparison for Banks is LSU's MiLaysia Fulwiley, particularly with their athletic profiles and process creating off the bounce.

Both are explosive, creative guards who put a ton of pressure on the rim with their athleticism and handle. They have that improvisational ability to make something out of seemingly nothing.

Fulwiley and Banks also have similar questions as prospects. Neither players are consistent shooters, and both struggle to use their left hand consistently.

At the WNBA level, there's some overlap with Portland's Carla Leite, in terms of their ability to dominate a game in ball screens and live in the paint. Also imagine if Seattle's Jade Melbourne had a better handle; that's sort of the idea here.

The ideal system for Banks is up-tempo offense that puts her in a lot of ball screens, surrounds her with shooting and gives her plenty of space to attack downhill. The more she can get the ball in hands with a runway to the rim, the more you actualize her athleticism and creativity.

Banks has interest from schools across the country, but according to an interview with CBS Sports' Isabel Gonzalez , Texas, LSU, South Carolina and Ohio State are the programs she's hearing from the most.

Here's how those four teams ranked in Barrtorvik's adjusted tempo metric last season: LSU (No. 7), Ohio State (No. 20), Texas (No. 104) and South Carolina (No. 115).

LSU and Ohio State are probably the best contexts for her to play the style of game she's best at, while spending four years at South Carolina would likely get the most out of her defensively, as an off-ball player and in the weight room.

Texas is the one fit that makes the least sense. They play at a slower pace, rely heavily on midrange pull-ups and generally don't create the kind of spacing that would allow Banks to flourish as a driver. And considering shooting is already one of the biggest questions in her game, I'm not sure that environment would put her in the best position to develop.

Well, that's GG Banks, a rising senior who is ranked No. 4 in the 2027 recruiting class. There's a lot of hype surrounding her, but just how good of a prospect is Banks?

I went through her film to break down every part of her game, from her athleticism and pick-and-roll playmaking to the shooting, defense and everything in between. Also, since she's only 17, a lot can change over the next few years, so there's plenty of upside baked into these grades.
When you watch Banks' film, it doesn't take long to realize just how ridiculous of an athlete she is. Guards who move like this don't exactly grow on trees.

She's incredibly explosive, but it's the combination of her speed, flexibility and change of direction that's really special. Banks can get downhill in a hurry, change speeds on a dime without losing much momentum and maneuver through tight spaces in ways most players can't.

That athleticism is especially dangerous in transition. Once Banks gets out in the open court, she covers ground in an instant before blowing past defenders. There's no question she will be one of the best transition scorers in college basketball.

And then there's the physical profile. Banks is listed on most sites at 5'8", but she has a 6'0" wingspan, which is significantly longer than most guards at her size. That length shows up when Banks is finishing with arms fully extended around the rim, but it also helps her make plays in passing lanes defensively.

Advantage creation is the name of the game at the point guard position. The best of them constantly put pressure on the defense, whether that's forcing help to come over off the drive or drawing two to the ball in pick-and-roll. That ability is one of the most impressive parts of Banks' game.

She has unbelievable feel for creating out of ball screens, and a lot of that starts with her handle. Banks is extremely creative with the ball, using inside-out dribbles, hesitations and left-right crossovers to keep defenders off balance. She loves to use her outside foot to sell defenders in one direction, then drive the other way.

Once you combine her improvisational skills with top-tier burst and acceleration, she's almost impossible to keep out of the paint. She gets to the rim so quickly she's consistently forcing weak-side defenders to help over, which leads to a lot of free throws and opens up things for her as a passer, too.

If you just watch Banks' highlights, one of the first things that jumps out is how impressive her gathers and high-difficulty finishes are. She has an incredible ability to contort her body around defenders to create openings. But sometimes, that creativity is a little too much.

Banks will often have a relatively easy layup available, only to make the finish much harder than it needs to be. Some of that comes down to her biggest improvement area: the left hand. At the high school level, Banks is so athletic and so skilled with the ball, she can get away with exclusively finishing with her strong hand right now. That won't always be the case at higher levels.

On the passing front, Banks is unsurprisingly really creative. She is a high-risk, high-reward passer, who attempts passes most players wouldn't even see. She consistently uses her eyes to manipulate defenders in ball screens and isn't afraid of making tight window passes.

Similar to all-world creators like Caitlin Clark and Olivia Miles, this style leads to a lot of assists but a good amount of turnovers as well. Across 16 games at 17U Nike EYBL, Banks averaged the third-most assists (5.5) and second-most turnovers (4.6) on the circuit.
The biggest question when it comes to Banks' on-ball operation is whether she can become a consistent shooter.

Right now, the three-point numbers just aren't there. She shot just 24 percent from three at 17U and 13.6 percent (3-of-22) across 5 games at Overtime Select, a league featuring the top high school players in the country.

One mechanical thing that stands out is the deep knee bend when she shoots. It can slow down her release, and at times, you'll see it cause her to leave shots short—especially off the dribble. The upper body mechanics aren't always compact, either.

Banks also attempted just one pull-up three (a miss) with Team USA at the U18 AmeriCup in June. Though, she did shoot 37.5 percent on catch-and-shoot threes (3-of-8), which were mostly all uncontested.
According to an article by On3's Hunter Shelton , Banks said her midrange game is one of the areas she's working hardest to improve.

If Banks can become even a reliable shooter, it changes the equation completely. Opponents already have to respect her first step and ability to get to the rim at-well. If she can punish them for going under screens with a consistent jumper, even more things will open up for her offensively—on and off the ball.

articles.title: Los terremotos impiden al Granada jugar en su pabellón
articles.standfirst: Tiene que disputar en Córdoba su primer amistoso ante el Cajasol Coto
articles.summary: Tiene que disputar en Córdoba su primer amistoso ante el Cajasol Coto
articles.body: El enjambre sísmico que sufre Granada ha motivado que no se puedan disputar partidos en el Palacio de los Deportes de la capital al tener que realizarse labores de mantenimiento en sus gradas, por lo que el choque de la Copa Andalucía de la próxima semana entre Covirán Granada y Cajasol Coto Córdoba se jugará finalmente en tierras cordobesas. El Covirán Granada informó este viernes en un comunicado de que, "tras la evaluación realizada" en el Palacio de Deportes granadino "después de la serie de terremotos registrada en la provincia durante los últimos días, se deben llevar a cabo labores de mantenimiento en la grada del recinto". Esto ha llevado a la Federación Andaluza de Baloncesto a trasladar a Córdoba la sede del partido entre el Covirán Granada y el Cajasol Coto Córdoba correspondiente a la Copa de Andalucía y que se iba a disputar la próxima semana en Granada. El club rojinegro ya ha comunicado que "procederá a la devolución del importe de las entradas que ya habían sido adquiridas por los aficionados para el partido". El duelo andaluz se disputará el miércoles a las ocho de la tarde en el Palacio de Deportes Vista Alegre de Córdoba. Los terremotos llevaron al Covirán Granada a suspender sus entrenamientos previstos en las jornadas del martes, el miércoles y el jueves, mientras que el equipo dirigido por Arturo Ruiz ya se ejercita con normalidad desde este viernes pese a que el enjambre sísmico sigue afectando a Granada capital y su área metropolitana con continuos temblores.

articles.title: Caitlin Clark 'Wouldn't Mind Seeing' Taylor Swift Wear Nike Caitlin 1 Signature Shoe
articles.summary: Indiana Fever star Caitlin Clark could be hoping her past hangouts with Taylor Swift will lead to the pop star endorsing her new signature Nike shoe.
articles.body:
Indiana Fever star Caitlin Clark could be hoping her past hangouts with Taylor Swift will lead to the pop star endorsing her new signature Nike shoe.

When asked in a recent Q&A by SLAM 's Jared Ebanks what celebrities she would like to see wearing the Nike Caitlin 1, Clark answered, "I wouldn't mind seeing Taylor Swift in a couple versions that I think she would probably like."

"Other than that, I honestly think it's really cool just seeing other WNBA players or other NBA players wear your shoe," Clark added. "I think that's really special. So, I'll definitely be trying to get as many college hoopers, NBA hoopers, WNBA hoopers."

The Nike Caitlin 1 is set to debut Oct. 1 in the "Racer Blue" colorway, which is one of more than 10 colorways Clark has teased ahead of the shoe's release.

Clark was spotted sitting next to Swift as the singer's now-husband Travis Kelce played for the Kansas City Chiefs game last October.

The Fever star later said in a January appearance on Kelce's New Heights podcast she "definitely" had interest in making a Chiefs colorway or player edition of the Nike Caitlin 1.

"Maybe we can get Andy Reid to coach in them at some point," Clark told Travis and Jason Kelce.

Clark has already gotten some celebrity endorsement ahead of the Nike Caitlin 1's release. She shared a photo earlier this offseason of Travis Scott trying on the shoes in an all-black colorway.

articles.title: DeMar DeRozan, Nuggets Reportedly Agree to Contract After Peyton Watson Trade, Updated Salary Cap
articles.summary: After two years with the Sacramento Kings, DeMar DeRozan has found a new home.
articles.body:
After two years with the Sacramento Kings, DeMar DeRozan has found a new home.

The veteran will reportedly sign a new contract with the Denver Nuggets, per Chris Haynes of NBA on Prime. The one-year deal will be worth $3.9 million per Shams Charania of ESPN.

Heat still have 2 rosters spot left after signing Klay

This move continues a tight salary cap crunch for the Nuggets.

They were already $1.3 million over the second apron before the deal, per Bobby Marks of ESPN.

The Kings waived DeRozan and the remainder of his expiring contract on July 6. DeRozan would have counted for $25.7 million against the cap had he stayed in Sacramento.

As soon as DeRozan hit free agency, it was clear a number of contenders were going to try to get him on their roster. After the Nuggets traded Peyton Watson to the Cleveland Cavaliers, their focus reportedly shifted to DeRozan.

While DeRozan is 36 years old, he's remained consistent as he's gotten older. Last year, he put up 18.4 points, 4.1 assists and 2.9 rebounds per game while starting 77 contests. He's also avoided injury throughout his career and has played 70 or more games in each of the last five seasons.

He might not have the same athleticism and explosiveness that he had in his youth, but he should be able to serve as a valuable option alongside Nikola Jokić and Jamal Murray.

The signing also gives DeRozan the chance to play for a contender rather than the Kings, who are likely on their way to another rough season. Whether the 2026-27 campaign will see DeRozan win his first title remains to be seen.

The Nuggets didn't have a huge budget to work with this offseason, but picking up DeRozan is a valuable signing that could be the difference for them this postseason.

articles.title: Jonathan Kuminga Updated Landing Spots After Klay Thompson, DeMar DeRozan Contracts
articles.summary: The market for free agent forward Jonathan Kuminga might have become clearer now that Klay Thompson and DeMar DeRozan have reportedly landed with their next teams.
articles.body:
The market for free agent forward Jonathan Kuminga might have become clearer now that Klay Thompson and DeMar DeRozan have reportedly landed with their next teams.

The Minnesota Timberwolves and Los Angeles Lakers remain top potential landing spots for Kuminga after Thompson and DeRozan reportedly committed to the Miami Heat and Denver Nuggets, respectively.

Kuminga is currently an unrestricted free agent after the Atlanta Hawks declined his team option. NBA insiders Marc Stein and Jake Fischer previously reported the Hawks are expected to be "pretty choosy" with any potential sign-and-trade scenarios involving Kuminga.

Offseason Overreactions for Every Team 🫨

ESPN's Shams Charania reported Friday the Miami Heat are expected to sign Thompson after he clears waivers following a buyout by the Dallas Mavericks.

That will put the Heat on track to use most of the team's remaining midlevel exception to sign Thompson, per the Miami Herald 's Barry Jackson and Anthony Chiang.

NBA insider Chris Haynes reported later the same day the Denver Nuggets are signing DeRozan.

Some other potential landing spots for Kuminga had already taken themselves out of the running with acquisitions earlier this offseason.

The Cleveland Cavaliers approached the first luxury tax apron by signing Peyton Watson and James Harden, while the Hawks spent the offseason adding former Oklahoma City Thunder players Aaron Wiggins and Lu Dort.

The Timberwolves remain a potential landing spot for Kuminga, in whom HoopsHype's Michael Scotto recently reported the team had "expressed interest" after missing out on signing LeBron James.

The Wolves have "their starting power forward spot up for grabs and their $6.06 million taxpayer mid-level exception available for the taking," Scotto noted.

The Athletic's Dan Woike previously reported the Lakers had expressed interest in Kuminga, but that as of July "momentum has stalled with the sides far apart on terms and L.A. not overly motivated to push significant draft capital into sign-and-trade scenarios."

Woike noted Kuminga "could re-emerge as a target if his market remains tepid."

ESPN's Brian Windhorst said in Friday's episode of The Hoop Collective podcast he feels there is "still a window" for the Lakers to complete a sign-and-trade deal featuring Kuminga and Lakers guard Jaden Hardy.

With the final NBA roster spots filling up, teams have about two months left to complete any late offseason moves before Opening Day rosters are finalized Oct. 19.

articles.title: Caitlin Clark Reveals New Colorway of Nike Caitlin 1 Signature Shoe in IG Photo
articles.summary: Caitlin Clark unveiled a new colorway of her Nike Caitlin 1 signature shoe on Friday.
articles.body:
Caitlin Clark unveiled a new colorway of her Nike Caitlin 1 signature shoe on Friday.

Clark posted a photo of the shoes, which contain seafoam green and blue colors, on her Instagram story.

The three-time All-Star has already revealed several colorways of her Nike Caitlin 1s both on and off the court during her 2026 campaign with the Fever.

Clark discussed the multitude of colorways in a recent interview with SLAM 's Jared Ebanks .

"I think it represents an aspiration and ambition," Clark told Ebanks. "And I feel like the shoe, when you look at it, has a lot of fire and spunk, especially with a lot of the different colors that we have coming out, and even with the first blue one and the yellow one. They're bright, they're powerful. So, I think that's kind of what I wanted to feel when I play in the shoe."

The 24-year-old is in the midst of another strong season for the Fever, averaging 21.7 points and 8.3 assists per game on 44.4/35.4/85.1 shooting splits. Indiana sits at No. 4 in the WNBA standings with a 24-13 record.

articles.title: Klay Thompson, muy cerca de firmar por los Miami Heat
articles.standfirst: El jugador quiere rubricar un contrato por dos temporadas con los de Florida
articles.summary: El jugador quiere rubricar un contrato por dos temporadas con los de Florida
articles.body: Klay Thompson está a un paso de firmar con los Miami Heat tras superar el proceso de la compra de su contrato con los Dallas Mavericks. La idea de Thompson es vincularse a los de Florida para las dos próximas temporadas y 13 millones de dólares, siendo la segunda de ellas una opción para el jugador, tal y como informa la cadena ESPN. Thompson ha renunciado a los 17 millones de su último año con los Mavs, liquidando el contrato con un 'buyout', por su deseo de jugar para un equipo que tuviera ciertas aspiraciones, sobre todo tras el 26-56 de los Mavs en la última Liga regular. Los Heat convirtieron a Klay en su objetivo una vez concluído uno de los grandes traspasos de la pretemporada con la llegada de Giannis Antetokounmpo, que cambia la lista de prioridades de la franquicia para esta temporada. Thompson llegaría a los Heat para fortalecer el perímetro en un intento de la franquicia por hacer una plantilla competitiva en torno a Giannis y a Bam Adebayo. Klay deja los Mavs tras dos temporadas promediando 12,9 puntos por partido y es el cuarto mejor anotador de triples de la historia con 2.899. Ahora los sumará en los Heat.

articles.title: El Barça anuncia el décimo fichaje de su nuevo proyecto: Yoan Makoundou
articles.standfirst: El ala-pívot francés tiene 26 años, mide 2,07 y ficha hasta 2028
articles.summary: El ala-pívot francés tiene 26 años, mide 2,07 y ficha hasta 2028
articles.body: El Barça ha anunciado este sábado la contratación del ala-pívot Yoan Makoundou hasta el 30 de junio de 2028, por lo que el jugador francés se convierte en el décimo fichaje del renovado proyecto azulgrana que dirige el esloveno Aleksander Sekulic. El versátil jugador francés, de 26 años y 2,07 metros, llega procedente del AS Monaco, tras formarse en el Cholet Basket, y cuenta con experiencia en la Euroliga. Durante su trayectoria, Makoundou también ha jugado cedido en el Buducnost Podgorica y el Turk Telekom Ankara, mientras que la pasada temporada disputó un breve período con los Fujian Sturgeons, de la liga china. Se trata de un interior que puede jugar en diferentes posiciones, con mucha energía y capacidad atlética, y que, según el comunicado de la entidad, es una incorporación "de presente y de futuro". Makoundou ya estuvo en el radar del club azulgrana en el mercado de verano de la temporada 2025-26, pero la operación finalmente no fructificó. Debutó en la LNB francesa en la temporada 2019/20 con el Cholet, aunque el salto definitivo a la élite llegó la temporada siguiente, con buenos registros en la competición doméstica y, sobre todo, en la Liga de Campeones de la FIBA, donde registró una media de 10,4 puntos, 5,2 rebotes, 13,4 de valoración en los 5 partidos que disputó. En la temporada 2021/22. se consolidó, con una mejora en el tiro exterior -pasó de un 27 a un 34,5% desde la línea de tres- y unas estadísticas interesantes de media en la LNB, con 10,2 puntos, 5,4 rebotes y 12,5 de valoración en 33 partidos de fase regular. Su progresión le permitió debutar con la selección francesa absoluta, con la que disputó 13 partidos en diferentes ventanas de clasificación para el Mundial del 2023 y el Eurobasket de 2025. En la temporada 2022-23, Makoundou fichó por el Mónaco con el que jugó sus primeros ocho partidos en la Euroliga, además de gozar de protagonismo en la liga francesa. En los dos siguientes cursos, encadenó dos cesiones al Budcnost Podgorica (2023-24) montenegrino y al Turk Telekom Ankara turco (2024-25). Con el equipo balcánico, registró una media de 11 puntos, 4,6 rebotes, 12,6 de valoración de media en la Eurocopa y se convirtió en una pieza clave para conseguir el título nacional gracias a sus aportación (con 12,8 puntos, 5 rebotes) en los 'play-off'. En el Turk Telekom, promedió 11,2 puntos, 4,9 rebotes y 12,4 de valoración en la Eurocopa, mientras que en los 'play-off' por el título de la liga turca alcanzó los 11,3 puntos y 5 rebotes de media. El curso pasado jugó en las filas del Mónaco, aunque a mediados de temporada rescindió el contrato y firmó por los Fujian Sturgeons de la liga china, donde en 19 partidos anotó 15,2 puntos y capturó 6,2 rebotes de media. Tras su experiencia asiática, el Mónaco recuperó al jugador parisino para disputar los 'play-off' por el título con unos registros notables de 11 puntos y 3,6 rebotes. Makoundou es la décima incorporación del Barça para la temporada 2026-27 tras los fichajes de los bases Justin Robinson y Umoja Gibsol, el escolta Agustín Ubal, los aleros Stanley Umude y Tyrese Martin, los ala-pívots Tosan Evbuomwan y Olivier Nkamhoua, y los pívots Olek Balcerowski y Josh Nebo. La dirección deportiva capitaneada por Xevi Pujol trabaja en cerrar la plantilla con la incorporación de un último jugador interior.

articles.title: Caitlin Clark, Fever Clinch 2026 WNBA Playoff Berth, Updated Bracket Picture and Standings
articles.summary: Caitlin Clark and the Indiana Fever are going to the playoffs for a third straight year.
articles.body:
Caitlin Clark and the Indiana Fever are going to the playoffs for a third straight year.

Indiana clinched a postseason spot with the Portland Fire's 82-79 loss to the Toronto Tempo on Friday night.

Following the clinching, Indiana is in fourth place in the WNBA standings and playoff picture:

The fourth seed will play the fifth seed in the first round of the WNBA playoff bracket, which means the Fever are currently slotted into a matchup against the Angel Reese and the Atlanta Dream.

There are only two games separating the Golden State Valkyries as the No. 2 seed and Dream in the fifth spot, so plenty of things can change over the final month of the regular season.

The WNBA is preparing to take a three week hiatus after Aug. 28 for the FIBA World Cup before play resumes on Sept. 18.

While a championship is the end goal for the Fever, they are surely focused on remaining healthy in the playoffs as well. After all, they reached the WNBA semifinals last season despite Clark, Sophie Cunningham, Sydney Colson and Aari McDonald all being sidelined with injuries.

Indiana defeated the Atlanta Dream in the first round and pushed the Las Vegas Aces to overtime in the decisive fifth game of the second round. Considering Las Vegas went on to win the championship, it was quite the effort from the shorthanded Fever.

Ideally for Clark and Co., they will be much healthier as they pursue the title this time around.

Everything in Indiana starts with the Big Three of Clark, Kelsey Mitchell and Aliyah Boston, which gives the team enough offensive firepower and versatility to play with and defeat even the best opponents in the league come playoff time.

All three of them made the All-Star Game this season and are averaging a combined 63.3 points per game. While role players such as Cunningham, Monique Billings and Lexie Hull provide some depth, the entire offense runs through the trio.

Clark is one of the faces of the league and a dominant scorer and facilitator who opens up looks for everyone else because of the defensive attention she draws. Mitchell has taken advantage of that more than anybody and is the team's leading scorer with an arsenal that includes three-point shooting and the ability to finish through contact as she drives the lane.

As for Boston, she is a double-double threat every time she steps on the floor and someone who provides important interior defense to take some of the pressure off Clark and Mitchell.

That lets Clark and Mitchell provide even more scoring, and they did so in record-setting fashion this season:

If the guard duo that represents one of the best one-two punches in the league continues to pour in the points and Boston continues to dominate on the inside, the ceiling for a healthy Fever team that is now heading to the postseason is the WNBA title.

articles.title: Bronny James Reacts to LeBron Leaving Lakers for 76ers in New Trending Video
articles.summary: Bronny James doesn't have any strong takes about his father leaving the Los Angeles Lakers to join the Philadelphia 76ers this offseason.
articles.body:
Bronny James doesn't have any strong takes about his father leaving the Los Angeles Lakers to join the Philadelphia 76ers this offseason.

When a fan asked Bronny about LeBron James signing with the Sixers, the Lakers guard had a simple response: "It's whatever, it's my dad."

Bronny and LeBron played two seasons together in Los Angeles. They became the first father-son duo to appear in the same NBA game when Bronny made his debut against the Minnesota Timberwolves on Oct. 22, 2024.

Overall, the James duo shared the court for 294 minutes over the past two years. Their last appearance together as teammates was Game 3 of the Western Conference semifinals against the Oklahoma City Thunder on May 9.

The Lakers' season ended the next game, leading to LeBron ending his eight-year tenure with the club. He went on to sign a two-year, $8 million contract with the Sixers in free agency.

Bronny is entering year three with the Lakers. He showed improvement from his rookie campaign in limited playing time with 2.9 points on 40.9 percent shooting and 1.2 assists per game in 42 appearances last season.

The first time Bronny and LeBron might meet as opponents is on Christmas Day when the Sixers visit Crypto.com Arena to take on the Lakers.

articles.title: Los Nuggets fichan a DeRozan para crear un nuevo 'Big Three'
articles.standfirst: El equipo de Colorado contará con el talento de DeMar durante la próxima temporada
articles.summary: El equipo de Colorado contará con el talento de DeMar durante la próxima temporada
articles.body: Lo de los 'Big Three', aquella fórmula que, aunque usada muchos años antes, se puso de moda cuando LeBron James se fue a Miami para juntarse con Chris Bosh y Dwyane Wade, sigue en boga en la NBA. Hace unos años sólo unos pocos tenían el privilegio de contar con uno, ahora casi todos los equipos lo tienen. Los Nuggets ya tienen el suyo. Mientras Nikola Jokic se divierte jugando partidos FIBA con Serbia, Denver trata de construir un equipo contendiente al título no sea que el riesgo de que su estrella quiera marcharse crezca cada año más. Tras el frustrante traspaso de Peyton Watson a Cleveland por las necesidades del límite salarial, la reacción de los de Colorado ha sido sonada: DeMar DeRozan. Es cambiar futuro (Watson, 24 años) por presente (DeRozan, 37), pero los Nuggets quieren pelear por el anillo esta misma temporada y por ello se han fijado en un anotador puro con una extraordinaria experiencia en la NBA y con una probada durabilidad. A pesar de sus 37 años y de que comenzará su temporada 17, DeRozan es un jugador habitual en los partidos, poco propenso a los problemas físicos. De hecho estuvo en 77 de los 82 partidos que jugó su equipo la pasada temporada y ha disputado al menos 70 partidos en las cinco últimas campañas. Pero sobre todo es un anotador puro capaz de producir 18,4 puntos por noche con cerca del 50% de acierto. Justo antes de la campaña recién terminada había encadenado al menos 20 puntos de media en 12 temporadas. DeRozan firma por una temporada y 3,9 millones de dólares. Es una simbiosis, el jugador llega a un equipo necesitado de talento, y el equipo recibe a un jugador que quiere ganar un anillo, que aún no tiene. DeRozan habló durante la pretemporada con los Miami Heat, los Washington Wizards y los New Orleans Pelicans. Estuvo cerca de los primeros a los que incluso se le vinculó tras una reunión con Ban Adebayo, pero los Heat pusieron su radar más cerca de Klay Thompson, al que han terminado por convencer. Acuciados por el límite salarial, los Kings cortaron a DeRozan a principios de la pretemporada y este se convirtió en agente libre. Ahora llega a un equipo en el que tiene qye mezclar con Jamal Murray y Nikola Jokic. Precisamente cada movimiento de los Nuggets se hace pensando en el serbio y esos rumores de que si el equipo no lucha por estar arriba y ganar un título, podría demandar un traspaso. Los Nuggets saben que 'el Joker' aún tiene al menos un anillo potencial en sus manos y quieren lograrlo rodeándole de experiencia y talento. Y en ese aspecto, DeRozan cumple con todas las exigencias.

articles.title: BIG3 League Championship 2026 Winner, Prize Money, Highlights, Box Score and Top Player Stats
articles.summary: The 2026 BIG3 league came to an exhilarating conclusion on Saturday as the Boston Ball Hogs defeated Dallas Power in the title game behind a game-winner from Jeremy Pargo.
articles.body:
The 2026 BIG3 league came to an exhilarating conclusion on Saturday as the Boston Ball Hogs defeated Dallas Power in the title game behind a game-winner from Jeremy Pargo.

The Ball Hogs entered the matchup as 3.5-point underdogs, according to FanDuel Sportsbook , but pulled off an upset with an incredible performance from its starters.

Jayson Tatum's dad blunt about Celtics roster

In its ninth season since being founded by Ice Cube and Jeff Kwatinetz in 2017, eight teams battled for the prize money.

Last season, it was announced that "the two winning teams coming out of the Week 9 playoffs will be awarded the $1 million win bonus," in addition to their regular-season salaries, according to BIG3's Hannah Palacios .

The Ball Hogs went 6-3 during the season behind co-captains Garlon Green and Deshawn Stephens, wrapping it all up with their first championship, led by an MVP performance from Pargo.

The Power finished a dominant season behind co-captains Cameron Smith and Glen Rice Jr., going 8-1.

Despite an impressive season and a standout championship performance from Elijah Stewart, who scored 19 points, they could not get it done in the final game.

Former Georgetown University big man Greg Monroe got things started in the 2026 championship game with a tough bucket under the rim before the two teams began their back-and-forth battle for the lead heading into halftime.

The Ball Hogs held a narrow two-point lead at halftime, with Green, Pargo and Stephens accounting for all of their points.

The race to 50 points came down to the wire, with Power within three points of the target and eyeing their second championship while the Ball Hogs were stuck at 43.

Boston's Pargo launched a 4-pointer to tie the game at 47-all, refusing to roll over as both teams eyed a 3-pointer to win it.

After an and-one put Monroe at the free-throw line with a chance to put the game away, he missed the opportunity, and Boston's Pargo called game with a 4-pointer to clinch the comeback victory and secure Boston's first-ever championship.

articles.title: España gana el oro y culmina un Europeo perfecto
articles.standfirst: Gana en la final a Eslovenia 40-87, en otro choque decidido antes de llegar al descano
articles.summary: Gana en la final a Eslovenia 40-87, en otro choque decidido antes de llegar al descano
articles.body: España cerró otro extraordinario verano en las categorías de formación. La Federación española de baloncesto, ejemplo absoluto en el mundo, vuelve a recoger una cosecha brillantísima con medallas en seis de los siete campeonatos en los que ha participado. Sólo en el Europeo masculino sub 20 (cuartos) no se tocó metal, y destacan la plata del Mundial sub 17, el oro del femenio sub 18, y los bronces del masculino sub 20 y sub 16 y el femenino sub 16. Pero la útima, la lograda por las selección sub 16 femenina, es colosal. Un oro de dominio absoluto en un campeonato perfecto. La selección, que ganó la final a Eslovenia 40-87, acabó con una media de anotación de 104,5 por partido por tan sólo 35,8 en contra, ganando partidos incluso por más de 100 puntos. Quizá desde los tiempos de tiranía de los equipos de la URSS, no se veía algo así. Y esto ha sido incluso superior. Un dato que corrobora esto es que si los partidos del torneo se hubieran disputado sólo con el primer y segundo cuarto, España hubiera ganado el oro igualmente. En los siete partidos que disputó, la selección de Madelen Urieta llegó al descanso con 20 o más puntos de diferencia, es decir, decidiendo los partidos en apenas 20 minutos. Sus segundas partes fueron casi un trámite. Eso pasó también contra Eslovenia, a la que España ya ganaba con enorme claridad cuando ambos equipos enfilaban el túnel de vestuarios (19-39). Para el choque, las premisas de Urieta eran que España fuera España, que jugara con ritmo, que corriera y que abusara de la pintura. Y que defendiera, pero sobre todo el perímetro. Con superiordad interior, lo que España quiso es evitar que las eslovenas se metieran en el partido desde el triple, que tantos réditos les dio en las semifinales ante Francia. La misión fue perfecta y las balcánicas acabaron anotando su primer (y único) triple a un minuto del final del tercer cuarto y con todo decidido. Tras un primer cuarto demoledor, 9-21, en el que España provocó 11 pédidas del rival, el segundo acto sólo mostró más defensa española y más superioridad interior. En ese aspecto, asusta pensar la progresión que pueden llegar a tener Amelia Alonso, jugadora fabulosa por calidad e instinto y Anastasia Lishchuk, dominante a lo largo de todo el campeonato siendo sub 14. También ha brillado mucho, en un bloque en el que sobresalir es complicado, Paula Reynal. Para el final del tercer cuarto, las de Arieta ya rondaban los 30 de diferencia, 32-61, una ventaja que fue creciendo durante el último cuarto, convertido ya en una fiesta española en la ciudad rumana de PItesti. El +47 final representa la mayor paliza en una final en la historia del campeonato, superando los 25 puntos logrados por la URSS ante Bulgaria (72-67, 1984), la URSS ante la República Checa (83-58, 1987) y Rusia de nuevo ante la República Checa (72-47, 2014). Paula Reynal fue la mejor anotadora de la final con sus 18 puntos. Acabó como la líder en anotación de un equipo sensacional. Por detrás de ella en la final, Sara Fernandez de Cuevas aportó 13 puntos, Blessing Ajisebutu hizo 12 y Amelia Alonso, tremendo su rendimiento en los dos aro, acabó con 9 puntos y 8 rebotes. La medalla ganada en Rumanía es la duodécima de oro para España y la vigésima en total. La selección lidera el medallero con esos 12 oros por los 8 que ganó la URSS. Eslovenia repite la plata que logró el pasado año perdiendo precisamente contra España.
paragraphs: España cerró otro extraordinario verano en las categorías de formación. La Federación española de baloncesto, ejemplo absoluto en el mundo, vuelve a recoger una cosecha brillantísima con medallas en seis de los siete campeonatos en los que ha participado. Sólo en el Europeo masculino sub 20 (cuartos) no se tocó metal, y destacan la plata del Mundial sub 17, el oro del femenio sub 18, y los bronces del masculino sub 20 y sub 16 y el femenino sub 16. Pero la útima, la lograda por las selección sub 16 femenina, es colosal. Un oro de dominio absoluto en un campeonato perfecto. La selección, que ganó la final a Eslovenia 40-87, acabó con una media de anotación de 104,5 por partido por tan sólo 35,8 en contra, ganando partidos incluso por más de 100 puntos. Quizá desde los tiempos de tiranía de los equipos de la URSS, no se veía algo así. Y esto ha sido incluso superior. Un dato que corrobora esto es que si los partidos del torneo se hubieran disputado sólo con el primer y segundo cuarto, España hubiera ganado el oro igualmente. En los siete partidos que disputó, la selección de Madelen Urieta llegó al descanso con 20 o más puntos de diferencia, es decir, decidiendo los partidos en apenas 20 minutos. Sus segundas partes fueron casi un trámite. Eso pasó también contra Eslovenia, a la que España ya ganaba con enorme claridad cuando ambos equipos enfilaban el túnel de vestuarios (19-39). Para el choque, las premisas de Urieta eran que España fuera España, que jugara con ritmo, que corriera y que abusara de la pintura. Y que defendiera, pero sobre todo el perímetro. Con superiordad interior, lo que España quiso es evitar que las eslovenas se metieran en el partido desde el triple, que tantos réditos les dio en las semifinales ante Francia. La misión fue perfecta y las balcánicas acabaron anotando su primer (y único) triple a un minuto del final del tercer cuarto y con todo decidido. Tras un primer cuarto demoledor, 9-21, en el que España provocó 11 pédidas del rival, el segundo acto sólo mostró más defensa española y más superioridad interior. En ese aspecto, asusta pensar la progresión que pueden llegar a tener Amelia Alonso, jugadora fabulosa por calidad e instinto y Anastasia Lishchuk, dominante a lo largo de todo el campeonato siendo sub 14. También ha brillado mucho, en un bloque en el que sobresalir es complicado, Paula Reynal. Para el final del tercer cuarto, las de Arieta ya rondaban los 30 de diferencia, 32-61, una ventaja que fue creciendo durante el último cuarto, convertido ya en una fiesta española en la ciudad rumana de PItesti. El +47 final representa la mayor paliza en una final en la historia del campeonato, superando los 25 puntos logrados por la URSS ante Bulgaria (72-67, 1984), la URSS ante la República Checa (83-58, 1987) y Rusia de nuevo ante la República Checa (72-47, 2014). Paula Reynal fue la mejor anotadora de la final con sus 18 puntos. Acabó como la líder en anotación de un equipo sensacional. Por detrás de ella en la final, Sara Fernandez de Cuevas aportó 13 puntos, Blessing Ajisebutu hizo 12 y Amelia Alonso, tremendo su rendimiento en los dos aro, acabó con 9 puntos y 8 rebotes. La medalla ganada en Rumanía es la duodécima de oro para España y la vigésima en total. La selección lidera el medallero con esos 12 oros por los 8 que ganó la URSS. Eslovenia repite la plata que logró el pasado año perdiendo precisamente contra España.

images.caption: España levanta la copa de campeonas de Europa sub 16. FIBA PHOTO.

Kimberly Kanayan N'Simba /Francia), Amelia Alonso y Paula Reynal (España), Nadine Graudina (Letonia) y Veronika Ferjancic (Eslovenia), formaron el quinteo ideal del torneo. Alonso fue la MVP. FIBA PHOTO.

articles.title: Angel Reese, Dream Clinch 2026 WNBA Playoff Berth, Updated Bracket Picture and Standings
articles.summary: The Atlanta Dream extended their WNBA playoff streak to four seasons.
articles.body:
The Atlanta Dream extended their WNBA playoff streak to four seasons.

Atlanta is assured of a top-eight position with a 99-89 win over the Phoenix Mercury. Angel Reese scored a career-high 31 points and hauled in 14 rebounds for her 26th double-double of the season.

With the result he Dream sit fourth overall at 24-13.

2. Golden State Valkyries (25-11); clinched

11. Los Angeles Sparks (13-24); eliminated

By this point, simply qualifying for the postseason doesn't count as success for the Dream. They didn't make it out of the first round in any of their last three trips, and they've won just one playoff game since 2018.

Especially with the core of the squad largely remaining for the last few years, Atlanta can't afford to keep hitting the same ceiling when it counts.

There might be some concern within the fanbase that that's exactly what will happen again this fall when it feels as though we've seen this story before.

Allisha Gray, Rhyne Howard and Reese were all All-Stars, but none of the three has taken a huge leap on the court.

Howard is averaging 18.2 points per game, which is close to her scoring average between 2023-25 (17.4 points). Gray is a good offensive engine who's setting a career high with 19.4 points, but her three-point shooting (32.5 percent) has gone backwards. Reese is still a walking double-double (16.3 points, 12.0 rebounds), yet the same concerns about her inefficiency and lack of range remain.

Adding further worry for Atlanta is that some of the supporting players aren't matching the heights they enjoyed in 2025.

Sixth Player of the Year Naz Hillmon has regressed as a floor-spacer. Guard Te-Hina Paopao was shooting just 34.4 percent overall before she was sidelined by a right leg injury. Four-time All-Star Brionna Jones hasn't looked as sharp since suffering a torn meniscus while playing overseas.

It's not as though the sky is falling for the Dream. They rank third in net rating (plus-6.8), per WNBA.com , but it's impossible not to contrast their performance now with that of a season ago, when they tied for the league's second-best record (30-14) and were second in net rating (plus-9.3).

Reese is a big wild card too because she didn't make the playoffs in her two years with the Chicago Sky. She's unproven on that stage, and her limited range is the kind of thing an opposing team will try to target in a postseason series.

At their best, the Dream can compete with just about any other team in the league, but few will have them as Finals favorites. Should they fail to turn a corner, general manager Dan Padover may need to take a long, hard look at the roster construction.
