articles.title: Jokic vuelve a superar a 'Wemby', pero Serbia cae sobre la bocina
articles.standfirst: Jaylen Hoard anota la canasta ganadora gala a pesar de la remontada de 19 puntos de los serbios
articles.summary: Jaylen Hoard anota la canasta ganadora gala a pesar de la remontada de 19 puntos de los serbios
articles.body: Los Francia - Serbia van camino de convertirse en la nueva gran rivalidad del baloncesto europeo y casi mundial. Y no sólo porque se enfrenten dos escuadras de enorme calidad y que siempre tratan de llegar lo más lejos posible en los torneos que compiten. Tener a dos de los cinco mejores jugadores del planeta ayuda y mucho. Decía Nikola Jokic tras el primer amistoso: "Un amigo me dijo un día que no hay amistosos, sino partidos de preparación. Siempre he entendido que cualquier partido es importante y me gusta afrontarlos así". Para el serbio no hay partidos relajados, da igual lo que haya en juego. Y lo volvió a demostrar en Orleans. Francia ganó a Serbia, 91-90, en un choque en el que de nuevo el que iba ganando se relajó y tuvo que volver a ganar el partido al final, como en el primer partido, pero al revés. Los franceses llegaron a mandar hasta por 19 cuando al descanso el marcador lucía un 54-35. Si ya en cualquier partido remontar 19 puntos es complicado, en un amistoso parece misión casi imposible. Pero no cuando está Jokic jugando. El serbio lideró a su país para que se metiera en el partido y luego los triples de Jovic y Dobric hicieron el resto. Serbia fue acortando poco a poco su desventaja con un parcial de 4-18 hasta ponerse por delante, 72-76 a falta de 6:48. Fueron entonces los franceses los que reaccionaron para volver a controlar el choque. Con Sylvain Francisco dirigiendo y Luwawu-Cabarrot anotando, Francia volvió a irse, 85-77, y ya parecía algo definitivo. Pero no, los balcánicos volvieron al partido y a cinco segundos para el final se colocaron por delante, 89-90 con una canasta de Guduric. La canasta final de Jaylen Hoard sobre la bocina en un error defensivo serbio, dio la victoria a Francia. Lo celebraron como un triunfo oficial. En Francia Francisco fue el mejor anotador con 20 puntos, mientras que Luwawu-Cabarrot hizo 19 y Wembanyama aportó 18 y cinco rebotes en 24 minutos. Jokic volvió a dar otro recital con 34 puntos, 13 rebotes y cinco asistencias jugando casi 30 minutos para 34 de valoración. Jovic anotó 13 puntos y Guduric, 11. El de Orleans ha sido el último partido de preparación de ambas selecciones. Ya en las Ventanas, Francia jugará contra Eslovenia (27 de agosto) y Suecia (30), con la tranquilidad que da su 5-1 en el grupo L, mientras que Serbia lo hará ante Islandia (28) e Italia (31), algo más apurado por el 4-2 que lucen.

articles.title: España aplasta a Bélgica en una prueba de mucho valor
articles.standfirst: El partido deja claro que el trabajo de Méndez y la selección va por muy buen camino
articles.summary: El partido deja claro que el trabajo de Méndez y la selección va por muy buen camino
articles.body: Una cosa ha quedado clara en Tenerife: jugando a este nivel, el demostrado ante Bélgica, España puede aspirar a cualquier cosa. 'Volvamos a soñar' es el lema de la gira de la selección y el equipo está dando los pasos para poder soñar de verdad. La selección aplastó a Bélgica, 95-67 en el tercer partido del torneo Internacional de Tenerife. Es cierto que esto es un partido de preparación y las conclusiones deben ser sacadas con perspectiva, pero ante las campeonas de Europa se vio un equipo que cada vez avanza más hacia la idea que su seleccionador quiere. Una defensa casi impenetrable que dispara luego un ataque eléctrico y muy eficiente. España llevaba cuatro derrotas seguidas ante Bélgica incluyendo dos finales de Europeos. Ganar este partido puede ser crucial si en algún momento ambos equipos cruzan sus caminos en el Mundial, que puede ocurrir. Las belgas ya saben lo que esta selección española puede dar. La puesta en escena del equipo de Méndez fue formidable. Por un lado el ataque funcionó a la perfección, y no sólo los tiros, sino también las penetraciones o los contraataques culmindos tras robo. Y todo eso con una enorme defensa que desactivó a Meeseman, su principal referente. Ya en el primer cuarto se vieron las intenciones españolas con el 25-16 al final del periodo. El despertar de Meeseman acercó a Bélgica, 33-31, pero los triples de Helena Pueyo volvieron a disparar a la selección. Al descanso, 45-42 por los siete puntos encajadas en los últimos instantes. Pero en la reanudación, las de Méndez seguían de subida y fueron disparando la ventaja. Los triples siguieron cayendo (13 anotó España de 25 intentos), demostando que si están acertadas desde el arco, es un equipo muy difícil de ganar. Una muestra del acierto español fueron los 5/8 de Pueyo, el 2/3 de Maite Cazorla y, sobre todo, el 4/4 de Elena Buenavida. La ventaja se disparó hasta los 30 puntos y una máxima de 33, 91-58, para acabar con el +28 final que quizá no da la imagen real entre ambos equipos, pero que pone de manifiesto dónde está España ahora mismo. Las últimas dos pruebas de la selección serán en Zaragoza ante Mali y China. Luego, ya pueden soñar con el Mundial. Iyana Martín acabó con 15 puntos y 8 asistencias, Pueyo también hizo 15 puntos, Cazorla aportó 14 y seis asistencias y Buenavida e Irati Etxarri firmaron 12. En Bélgica, Lisowa fue la mejor con 12 y Meeseman se quedó en 10.

articles.title: Klay Thompson Signs Heat Contract After Agreeing to Mavs Buyout, Details Revealed
articles.summary: Klay Thompson has officially signed with the Miami Heat:
articles.body:
Klay Thompson has officially signed with the Miami Heat:

The announcement shows Thompson wearing No. 11, which would be a return to the number he wore during his 11 years with the Golden State Warriors. He wore No. 31 most recently with the Dallas Mavericks.

Heat still have 2 rosters spot left after signing Klay

Offseason Overreactions for Every Team 🫨

According to The Athletic's Sam Amick and Darnell Mayberry , the veteran signed a two-year, $11.5 million contract with the Heat after reaching a buyout with the Mavs.

After clearing waivers on Sunday, he was able to officially sign with Miami.

The deal reportedly includes a player option for the second year and also includes a 15 percent trade kicker.

The Mavericks announced Friday that they are buying out the final year of Klay Thompson's contract. The five-time All-Star was due to earn $17.5 million for the 2026-27 season

Dallas' move is a sign of how far Thompson's value has diminished around the NBA. Once one of the best two-way players in the league, he fell out of the Mavericks' starting rotation midway through last year.

In 69 appearances, he averaged 11.7 points and set career lows in overall field-goal percentage (39.3) and three-point percentage (38.3).

Jason Kidd shifted Thompson to the bench after seven games, which made for a delicate situation considering Dallas promised him a starting spot when it made its pitch during the 2024 offseason.

Kidd indicated it was only a temporary tactical change, and the 36-year-old was with the first unit again in a loss to the New York Knicks in mid-November. But he eventually assumed a reserve role again.

The Warriors saw the writing on the wall with a player who had become a franchise icon.

Head coach Steve Kerr and general manager Mike Dunleavy Jr. were pragmatic rather than sentimental with Thompson's usage during the 2023-24 season and then regarding how they approached his subsequent free agency.

Breaking up the "Splash Brothers" wasn't a move anybody in the Bay Area wanted to make, but the Warriors understood Thompson was on a downward trajectory. Missing two full seasons because of a torn ACL and a torn Achilles accelerated the inevitable decline that was coming as he got older.

A change of scenery and a desire to prove Golden State wrong didn't spark a renaissance in his first year with Dallas. He averaged 14 points per game, his lowest output since his rookie season, and his field-goal percentage (41.2) was a personal worst at the time.

The Mavs knew they weren't getting Thompson at his peak when they signed him. They presumably envisioned him occupying a role similar to Ray Allen during his two-year run with the Miami Heat and toward the end of his Boston Celtics tenure. Allen remained a capable three-point specialist as his career wound down, shooting 37.5 percent from beyond the arc in his final season.

Thompson's long-range prowess has even started to desert him, though, which makes the other flaws in his game tougher to ignore. He's not as dogged a defender and he can't score off the dribble like he once did.

The days of Thompson being a big difference-maker on a contender may be over, but he's a low-risk addition for a Heat team that saw Giannis Antetokounmpo enter the fold this summer.

Kidd indicated it was only a temporary tactical change, and the 36-year-old was with the first unit again in a loss to the New York Knicks in mid-November. But he eventually assumed a reserve role again.
The Warriors saw the writing on the wall with a player who had become a franchise icon.

Head coach Steve Kerr and general manager Mike Dunleavy Jr. were pragmatic rather than sentimental with Thompson's usage during the 2023-24 season and then regarding how they approached his subsequent free agency.

Breaking up the "Splash Brothers" wasn't a move anybody in the Bay Area wanted to make, but the Warriors understood Thompson was on a downward trajectory. Missing two full seasons because of a torn ACL and a torn Achilles accelerated the inevitable decline that was coming as he got older.

A change of scenery and a desire to prove Golden State wrong didn't spark a renaissance in his first year with Dallas. He averaged 14 points per game, his lowest output since his rookie season, and his field-goal percentage (41.2) was a personal worst at the time.

The Mavs knew they weren't getting Thompson at his peak when they signed him. They presumably envisioned him occupying a role similar to Ray Allen during his two-year run with the Miami Heat and toward the end of his Boston Celtics tenure. Allen remained a capable three-point specialist as his career wound down, shooting 37.5 percent from beyond the arc in his final season.

Thompson's long-range prowess has even started to desert him, though, which makes the other flaws in his game tougher to ignore. He's not as dogged a defender and he can't score off the dribble like he once did.
The days of Thompson being a big difference-maker on a contender may be over, but he's a low-risk addition for a Heat team that saw Giannis Antetokounmpo enter the fold this summer.

articles.title: Enes Kanter Freedom Ejected from Fever-Sky Game After He Was Confronted by Sky's Cloud
articles.summary: CHICAGO (AP) — Former NBA center Enes Kanter Freedom was ejected from Sunday night's Indiana-Chicago WNBA game after Sky guard Natasha Cloud yelled and pointed in his direction late in the third quarter.
articles.body:
CHICAGO (AP) — Former NBA center Enes Kanter Freedom was ejected from Sunday night's Indiana-Chicago WNBA game after Sky guard Natasha Cloud yelled and pointed in his direction late in the third quarter.

Freedom was sitting along the baseline. He had on a black shirt that read "WOMAN noun. adult human female."

The Fever called for a timeout after Cloud scored inside with 1:22 left in the third. Cloud then went to confront Kanter, who held his arms and took one step on the court. Security and a handful of Sky players stepped in between the two before the dispute escalated.

No Cunningham-Carrington Issues in Rematch (AP)

Freedom then was escorted from the court area. He displayed his shirt as he walked toward the lobby. He had a conversation with a group of police officers before departing Wintrust Arena.

Freedom and Royce White, another former NBA player, declared themselves eligible for the WNBA draft this month, saying they identify as women.

articles.title: Caitlin Clark, Sophie Cunningham's Final Box Score Stats, Highlights as Fever Beat Sky
articles.summary: The Indiana Fever's short losing streak is over.
articles.body:
The Indiana Fever's short losing streak is over.

Indiana ended its two-game losing streak and improved to 25-14 on the season with a 113-90 victory over the Chicago Sky on Sunday. Caitlin Clark and the Fever entered the contest as 3.5-point favorites on FanDuel Sportsbook and finished the season sweep of Chicago even though Aliyah Boston was sidelined with a lower leg injury.

Clark and Kelsey Mitchell continued their season-long brilliance with 14 combined three-pointers, while Sophie Cunningham added three points off the bench. Natasha Cloud led the way for Chicago in a losing effort, but there was only so much she could do to counter Clark making more history:

Indiana entered the game on a poorly timed mini-slide that knocked it into fifth place in the standings that have just a handful of games separating the second seed from the eighth seed. The standings flip with seemingly every result, so Sunday was an important opportunity to bounce back against an opponent they have controlled play against this season.

Yet Chicago was ready to put up a fight in the early going.

The home team used a balanced attack to seize a 51-50 halftime advantage with eight different players scoring at least four points before intermission. The Sky's bench provided a much-needed boost, which helped counter Clark dominating play on an individual level with her combination of outside shooting and facilitating when defenders collapsed.

Makayla Timpson also got off to a quick start for Indiana, which helped make up for the loss of Boston. Clark even found her on a behind-the-back pass, although the visitors still found themselves behind early due to their defensive issues without their frontcourt star.

Still, offensive dominance is often enough to overcome defensive woes on the other side, as Clark and Mitchell reminded the Sky in the third quarter.

The duo of backcourt stars took over with an array of deep threes, floaters and drives into the lane, and Chicago had no answer. Frankly, there may be no team in the entire league that will have a counter for the guards when they are both playing at their best, although the Sky were still well within striking distance heading to the fourth thanks in part to an offensive flurry from Cloud.

But there would be no fourth-quarter rally for Chicago.

The Clark and Mitchell show led the way, but the Fever finally dialed up the defensive intensity when the game was on the line as well. The Sky failed to generate any offensive momentum until it was too late, and it would have required quite the offensive performance to overcome the two Indiana guards.

With Sunday's win secured, the Fever will now look to start a winning streak and climb the standings as they host the Connecticut Sun on Friday.

articles.title: Enes Kanter Freedom ejected from WNBA game after being confronted by Sky’s Natasha Cloud
articles.summary: The WNBA has been the subject of recent debates about whether transgender women should be allowed to play in the league. There has never been such a player in the WNBA.
articles.body: CHICAGO — Former NBA center Enes Kanter Freedom was ejected from Sunday night’s Indiana-Chicago WNBA game after he was confronted by Sky guard Natasha Cloud late in the third quarter. Freedom was sitting along the baseline. He had on a black shirt that read “WOMAN noun. adult human female.” The Fever called for a timeout after Cloud scored inside with 1:22 left in the third. Cloud then did a chest bump with teammate Aicha Coulibaly before turning around and walking in Kanter’s direction. Cloud, 34, started yelling and pointing at Kanter, also 34, as she approached him. A standing Kanter held his arms out and took one step on the court as security and a handful of Sky players moved in between the two. “There was just a fan incident and the security handled it, and we’re just going to focus on the game,” Chicago forward Azura Stevens said after the Sky’s 113-90 loss. Chicago coach Tyler Marsh said Cloud was concerned about being a distraction for the team. “I told her she wasn’t,” Marsh said. “I told her that we all embrace her as someone that protects our team and protects people that need to be protected and so Tash is always going to stand on that, and we stand for Tash.” Freedom stopped near the basket to plead his case to security as he was escorted from the court area. He spun around while holding his shirt out and encouraged the crowd to respond as he walked toward the front lobby. He had a conversation with a group of police officers before departing Wintrust Arena. “I didn’t see it. We were talking about the next play in our huddle,” Indiana star Caitlin Clark said. “So I think that’s probably a question for Chicago.” Cloud met with team and league security after the game. She did not speak with the media. The WNBA has been the subject of recent debates on whether transgender women — people assigned male at birth who transition to align with their gender identity — should be allowed to participate in the league. There has never been such a player in the WNBA. Although the league’s collective bargaining agreement says the WNBA is restricted to women, it contains no more specific language about gender identity or sex assigned at birth. Fever guard Sophie Cunningham said in an ESPN profile published last month that she was opposed to transgender girls and women competing in girls’ and women’s sports. Freedom and Royce White, another former NBA player, have declared themselves eligible for the WNBA draft, saying they identify as women. Kanter joined a small rally in support of Cunningham outside the arena before the game. Asked if he had a message for Kanter, Marsh praised the league and its players. “If you come to a game you should probably come to enjoy the basketball,” he said, “and that seems pretty simple to me. I think these players deserve that and have earned that. Being a former basketball player, you should probably understand and feel that too.”

articles.title: El nuevo Real Madrid se estrenará en la SuperCup de la Euroliga
articles.standfirst: La competición se disputará en Abu Dabi los días 18 y 19 de septiembre
articles.summary: La competición se disputará en Abu Dabi los días 18 y 19 de septiembre
articles.body: La Euroliga anunció este lunes el nacimiento de una nueva competición. Ya se habló de ello en julio, aunque no hubo anuncio oficial. Pero la nueva SuperCup ya ha recibido la luz verde y por lo tanto habrá un nuevo título que sumar a la lista de los objetivos de esta temporada. La SuperCup que se celebrará en Abu Dabi los próximos 18 y 19 de septiembre reúne un cartel de lujo: Olympiacos, Real Madrid, Fenerbahce y Dubai Basketball. Los griegos acuden por su condición de actuales campeones de la Euroliga, el Madrid por ser finalista, los turcos por ser el anterior campeón y el Dubai como equipo anfitrión. Es cierto que, como ocurre con otras 'supercopas' se trata de un torneo entre la pretemporada y el inicio oficial de la competición, pero no deja de ser un título y sobre todo con un cartel tan atractivo como el que ofrece en este caso la SuperCup. El Madrid, muy renovado, podrá poner a prueba su proyecto a las primeras de cambio contra equipos que, en mayo, estén peleando por entrar en la Final Four que, en principio, también se celebrará en Abu Dabi. El equipo de Pedro Martínez cuenta con numerosas novedades en su plantilla: el propio entrenador, Jaime Pradilla, Timothe Luwawu-Cabarrot, Mikael Jantunen, Max Shulga, Olivier Sarr y Eli Ndiaye a falta de que Damian Jones sea presentado y quizá a la llegada de un dos, aunque este podría llegar en los descartes de la NBA. El Madrid ya habrá jugado partidos de preparación ya que participará en el torneo Costa del Sol de Málaga junto a La Laguna Tenerife y Unicaja, pero no jugará la Supercopa Endesa en Badalona, que, por cierto, coincide en fechas con la europea (19 y 20). Disputar dos partidos ante equipos punteros de la Euroliga es una excelente puesta a punto para los de Martínez. Además, se da la circunstancia de que los blancos debutarán en la Euroliga precisamente en Dubái el próximo 24 de septiembre, cinco días después de jugar la SuperCup, por lo que podrán quedarse en Dubai para disputar el partido ya oficial de Liga regular. En el torneo de la Euroliga se podrán ver también algunas novedades en equipos muy favoritos como el Olympiacos: Jean Montero o Codi Miller-McIntyre, Fenerbahce: Sertac Sanli, Shavon Shields, Trent Forrest, Braxton Key, Shane Larkin o Will Clyburn, o el Dubai con el estreno de Xavi Pascual y las llegadas de Tornike Shengelia, Mamadi Diakite, Jaron Blossomgame o Elie Okobo. El formato de la SuperCup será igual que el de una Final Four. El viernes 18 se disputarán las semifinales con el Olympiacos - Fenerbahce a las 16.00 hora peninsular (18.00 hora local), y el Real Madrid - Dubai Basketball a las 19.00 en España (21.00 en Abu Dabi). El sábado habrá un tercer y cuarto puesto (16.00 en España) y la final tres horas después (19.00). "La SuperCup refleja nuestra ambición de seguir innovando y ampliando el alcance del baloncesto de clubes europeo", valoró el CEO de la Euroliga Chus Bueno. "Lanzar esta nueva competición en Abu Dabi nos permite conectar con nuevas audiencias y, al mismo tiempo, ofrecer a aficionados, clubes y socios un evento de primer nivel que exhibe lo mejor de nuestro deporte. Esperamos consolidar la SuperCup como una cita destacada en el calendario internacional de baloncesto".

articles.title: Enes Kanter provoca su expulsión en un partido de la WNBA
articles.standfirst: El turco se enzarzó en una discusión con Natasha Cloud y luego publicó varios mensajes
articles.summary: El turco se enzarzó en una discusión con Natasha Cloud y luego publicó varios mensajes
articles.body: La polémica que estalló con el anuncio de Enes Kanter de presentarse al Draft de la WNBA de 2027 porque "me siento mujer", alimentada por otro ex NBA como Royce White, no sólo está muy lejos de acabar, sino que es alimentada a lo bestia día a día. El último capítulo tuvo lugar en un Chicago Sky ante Indiana Fever y lo protagonizó el propio ex jugador turco, con un mensaje en su camiseta, una publicación en el descanso y un final abrupto que supuso su expulsión del Wintrust Arena de Chicago. Kanter se presentó en el partido con una camiseta en la que se podía leer: "Mujer. Sustantivo. Ser humano adulto femenino". El turco sigue manteniendo que en las normas de la WNBA se indica que sólo las mujeres pueden jugar en su competición. Pero según el polémico ex jugador, no hay una definición concreta del término mujer. Y mantiene que si él se siente mujer, puede jugar en la Liga. Otra de las provocaciones de Kanter llegó en el descanso. Publicó en redes un mensaje en el que ponía: "Es medio tiempo y mecesito usar el lavabo. Las reglas son las reglas", acompañado de una foto en la que se le veía en el lavabo de las mujeres. Finalmente llegó su expulsión. Natasha Cloud, jugadora de las Sky, le fue a buscar a la pie de pista, donde estaba Kanter, y se enzarzó con él en una discusión que el turco, claro, no sólo no rehuyó, sino que elevó a lo máximo. Finalmente Kanter, se ve en la imagen, fue invitado a abandonar el pabellón y lo hizo pidiendo más ruido al público y mostrando ostensiblemente el mensaje que llevaba en su camiseta. Poco después Kanter publicó un nuevo mensaje en las redes: ¡Acabo de ser expulsado de un partido de la WNBA por apoyar a las MUJERES! Que eso cale hondo, ¡AMÉRICA!. Antes había publicado otro: "Siempre son mujeres criticando a otras mujeres".  Es un capítulo más de una polémica que está a años luz de resolverse. Al menos de momento. Y lo que está ocurriendo con Kanter y la WNBA en realidad es un resumen de una sociedad dividida entre los partidarios de que los deportistas trans puedan participar en competiciones de mujeres y los que no. Y el debate seguirá.

articles.title: Caitlin Clark Achieves Rare Stat More Than All Players in WNBA History Combined in Just 3 Seasons
articles.summary: Indiana Fever star Caitlin Clark stands alone in the WNBA record books with regard to one statistical distinction.
articles.body:
Indiana Fever star Caitlin Clark stands alone in the WNBA record books with regard to one statistical distinction.

The three-time All-Star had 37 points and 10 assists in Sunday's 113-90 win over the Chicago Sky. The team pointed out her five career 30/10 performances are more than all of the others in league history:

Las Vegas Aces star A'ja Wilson remains the heavy favorite for the 2026 MVP, with Minnesota Lynx rookie Olivia Miles entrenched in the second spot.

Clark is doing her best to make things interesting in the stretch run. Since the All-Star break, she has averaged 24.3 points on 47.5 percent shooting along with 9.0 assists.

Granted, Fever teammate Kelsey Mitchell has been equally as electric. Mitchell added to her own WNBA record by scoring 20-plus points for the 23rd straight game.

Assuming the MVP winds up in Wilson's hands for a fifth time, Clark and Mitchell will be too occupied with getting Indiana back to the WNBA semifinals and perhaps beyond.

The Fever are hitting their stride at the right time and only trail the second-place Golden State Valkyries by 1.5 games.

The three-time All-Star had 37 points and 10 assists in Sunday's 113-90 win over the Chicago Sky. The team pointed out her five career 30/10 performances are more than all of the others in league history:
Las Vegas Aces star A'ja Wilson remains the heavy favorite for the 2026 MVP, with Minnesota Lynx rookie Olivia Miles entrenched in the second spot.

Al combinado de Mateo le toca resolver la clasificación para el Mundial de Qatar 2027, que tiene medio encauzada y que puede terminar de abrochar en estas ventanas de agosto, ante Portugal en Zaragoza (este viernes día 28) y frente a Grecia en Atenas (31). Después, la expedición de la selección viajará hasta Zaragoza, donde quedará concentrada. hasta el partido del viernes (21.00 h) en el Príncipe Felipe ante Portugal.

articles.title: La perla Diego Niebla se incorpora a la concentración de la selección
articles.standfirst: El alero de 2,02 y 18 años del Joventut, que destacó mucho en el EuroBásket sub18, ayudará en los entrenamientos durante la estancia en Zaragoza
articles.summary: El alero de 2,02 y 18 años del Joventut, que destacó mucho en el EuroBásket sub18, ayudará en los entrenamientos durante la estancia en Zaragoza
articles.body: Diego Niebla, jugador del Asisa Joventut, se incorporará a la concentración de la selección en Zaragoza. El alero entrenará junto al resto del equipo durante los entrenamientos programados esta semana que servirán para preparar los partidos de clasificación para la Copa del Mundo 2027 ante Portugal en Zaragoza (viernes 28) y frente a Grecia en Atenas (lunes 31). Niebla, alero gallego de 2,02 y 18 años, ve así recompensado su buen papel este verano con la selección U18 en el Eurobasket de la categoría, donde fue incluido en el cinco Ideal del torneo. La pasada temporada fue uno de los jugadores de más destacados en la Liga U, promediando 10,8 puntos y 2,7 rebotes por partido. Se proclamó también máximo anotador del Campeonato de España Júnior. Es uno de los grandes proyectos del baloncesto español.  La FEB y Chus Mateo, quisieron agradecer, en un comunicado de la Federación Española de Baloncesto, la "predisposición y colaboración del Asisa Joventut para facilitar la incorporación del jugador a la concentración de Zaragoza".

articles.title: Ibon Navarro echa a rodar a su Estrella Roja
articles.standfirst: El vitoriano comienza su aventura lejos de Málaga y la ACB
articles.summary: El vitoriano comienza su aventura lejos de Málaga y la ACB
articles.body: Ibon Navarro ya ha comenzado a trabajar con su Estrella Roja después de poner fin a su etapa en el Unicaja de Málaga y afrontar el reto de dirigir al conjunto serbio. El entrenador vitoriano se estrenó este lunes en una sesión en la que empezó a tomar contacto con un grupo que presenta muchas novedades respecto al curso anterior. El técnico no estará solo en esta aventura. Alberto Miranda vuelve a formar parte de su equipo de trabajo y también hay un rostro especialmente conocido para los seguidores del Unicaja: Tyson Carter, que vuelve a ponerse a las órdenes de Ibon después de coincidir con él en la Costa del Sol. La gran novedad en el banquillo la aporta Nikola Kalinic. El ya exjugador ha decidido dar el salto a los banquillos tras su retirada y se incorpora al staff del Estrella Roja para iniciar una nueva etapa profesional dentro del baloncesto. El conjunto de Belgrado afronta el curso con una plantilla de 17 jugadores y una profunda renovación. El club ha incorporado este verano a jugadores como Nick Weiler-Babb, Patrick Baldwin Jr., Johnathan Motley y David Kramer, aunque este último todavía se encuentra concentrado con Alemania. Al frente de la planificación deportiva está Milos Teodosic, responsable de construir un proyecto ambicioso que ya ha empezado a rodar. Con las primeras sesiones de Ibon Navarro, el Estrella Roja comienza a poner los cimientos de una temporada en la que las expectativas volverán a ser máximas.

articles.title: 2025 NBA Contenders Who Need a Trade Most
articles.summary: The NBA trade deadline is fast approaching, and the wheeling and dealing has already begun ahead of February 6.
articles.body:
The NBA trade deadline is fast approaching, and the wheeling and dealing has already begun ahead of February 6.

The Los Angeles Lakers, Golden State Warriors and Phoenix Suns have made moves. And there could be a lot of movement in the coming weeks as teams load up for playoff runs.

Many players could be on the move. The Brooklyn Nets, Utah Jazz and Portland Trail Blazers could be sellers at this draft.

Of course, the Jimmy Butler trade demand hangs over the Miami Heat. The Suns are interested in moving Bradley Beal with his pesky no-trade clause. Zach LaVine's name continues to be thrown into trade rumors. Cameron Johnson's name is burning up the phone lines (he'll be mentioned a lot below).

Several teams need to make trades. Some of these moves can turn teams into contenders or strengthen contenders.

It's been an interesting season for the Sacramento Kings.

At one point, they looked like sellers at the deadline, with some De'Aaron Fox unhappiness. That resulted in the firing of head coach Mike Brown. Since then, the team has caught fire under Doug Christie. The Kings are now buyers in the trade marketplace.

Based on how the Kings have been playing since the coaching change, they should be considered a contender. Under Christie, they have the second-best win percentage in the NBA, just behind Oklahoma City. However, they do need a three-and-D wing player with more of an emphasis on shooting.

Adding another shooter to the roster will create more driving lanes for Fox, DeMar DeRozan and Malik Monk. The Kings are 22nd in three-point attempts and 20th in three-point percentage.

There were rumors that Sacramento already inquired about the Brooklyn Nets' Cameron Johnson. No deal seems imminent between the two teams, but it does show what the Kings will be looking for on the market.

Several contenders will be looking for players like Johnson. The Los Angeles Lakers already took Dorian Finney-Smith off the market. The Kings are playing great basketball, 11-4 over their last 15 games. If Sacramento wants to jump into the contender tier, it needs to make a trade at this deadline and cannot stand pat.

After a woeful start to the season, the Milwaukee Bucks have stabilized and are sitting fourth in the Eastern Conference. Giannis Antetokounmpo has been a dominant force, averaging 31.5 points and 12.2 rebounds a game. Damian Lillard has found his groove from three after the dip last season. Even with the duo rolling, the Bucks must move by February 6th.

This was supposed to be a trio though, Khris Middleton has been held back by injuries. His scoring is down again this season after returning to the court in December. The Bucks need a third star on the wing. Preferably someone who can also help bolster their porous perimeter defense.

The Bucks have been at the center of several rumors, from interest in Jimmy Butler to a possible Bradley Beal or Zach LaVine landing spot and everything in between. Beal and LaVine won't help with their perimeter defensive issues, but their ability to score offensively can offset the Bucks's weakness there.

The Bucks need a shot in the arm to help attack the Cleveland Cavaliers, Boston Celtics, and New York Knicks. They are 0-8 against the top teams in the East. The Bucks have to take a swing to have a true shot at taking down any of the top three in the conference.

Everyone's heads turned when the Golden State Warriors started 12-3 this season. Then, the wheels fell off the wagon, and the Warriors have gone 10-20 since that start. One can argue that maybe they should have found a deal for Lauri Markkanen in the offseason, as we rumored, but that ship has sailed. They cannot miss the boat this time around.

Golden State made a trade, bringing in Dennis Schroder from the Brooklyn Nets. Adding another ball handler to the roster was a smart move, but more importantly, they made the trade early enough that Schroder could be included in another trade by deadline day.

The Warriors desperately need to add someone who could take some of the scoring pressure off Stephen Curry. There is not a reliable second option on the roster; some nights, it is Andrew Wiggins, Jonathan Kuminga (who has been injured since 1/5), and Buddy Hield. That is not good enough.

The real problem for the Warriors is that the options for a second option that are available are not earth-shattering. LaVine, Beal, and even Butler are interesting names, but the price tag will be too high for the Warriors. Brandon Ingram from New Orleans is available, but he is currently injured, does not have a great history with Steve Kerr stemming from his Team USA run, and will be looking for a big contract in the offseason.

The Warriors' options are not great. It might be better to sit out this trade deadline, but doing that will be punting on this season. If Golden State cannot find a solid second consistent scorer, they are wasting another Curry season, and that is unforgivable.

Before discussing what the Memphis Grizzlies should do this deadline, let's take a quick look back. It was not that long ago that Memphis looked like they were going to conquer the Western Conference.

Everyone knows what happened next, but most don't remember that the Grizzlies made a run at a wing/forward at the 2023 deadline. The price for OG Anunoby was too high for Memphis, but it will remain a fun what-if.

This time, with the deadline approaching, the Grizzlies' standing in the league is different, but their need is very similar. They are just a half-game out of second in the West but do not have full contender status. To get there, Memphis needs to add offensive and defensive firepower.

The Grizzlies should be in the market for a player similar to Anunoby. Cam Johnson should be a target for Memphis, putting them on that contender track. The price the Toronto Raptors were asking for in 2023 was high. It is rumored that the Brooklyn Nets are seeking two first-round picks for Johnson, which are lower than the price of Anunoby in the past.

If the Grizzlies' chase for Johnson is too much, they should look at other targets, like maybe Jerami Grant in Portland. They can also take a flyer on Kyle Kuzma, who is having a down year and could be in need of a change of scenery.

Memphis needs to level up if it is going to compete with the Oklahoma City Thunder, and its best chance is to make a move at the deadline.

articles.title: Jayson Tatum's Dad Calls Celtics Roster 'S--t' & Tells LaVar Ball Knicks Will Win 2027 NBA Title
articles.summary: The father of Jayson Tatum offered a candid assessment of the Boston Celtics' championship hopes in 2026-27.
articles.body:
The father of Jayson Tatum offered a candid assessment of the Boston Celtics' championship hopes in 2026-27.

Appearing on Ultimate Dads Unplugged , a podcast hosted by LaVar Ball, Dwyane Wade Sr., and Quenton Brown Sr., Justin Tatum said the New York Knicks are his early 2027 Finals pick. Asked about the Celtics, he described their roster as "s--t."

The exchange begins at the 11:33 mark of Saturday's episode.

The elder Tatum was being a little too negative toward the Celtics, but there's no getting around the fact that the team might've taken a step back through the Jaylen Brown trade. Going from Brown to Paul George is a decline in the short term, and signing Mitchell Robinson to address the center position is risky given his injury record.

A starting five that includes George, Jayson Tatum and Derrick White should be good enough to keep Boston at a playoff level in the Eastern Conference.

But a sizable gap exists between the Celtics and the likes of the Knicks and the Philadelphia 76ers.

articles.title: "España puede llevarse el oro en el Mundial"
articles.standfirst: La escolta del Valencia Leticia Romero, que no estará en la cita, optimista con las opciones de las españolas
articles.summary: La escolta del Valencia Leticia Romero, que no estará en la cita, optimista con las opciones de las españolas
articles.body: La jugadora del Valencia Basket Leticia Romero compartió este lunes su opinión sobre el posible papel de la selección española el Mundial de baloncesto que se celebra en Alemania entre 4 y el 13 de septiembre y colocó a España como una de las favoritas al título. "España siempre va a estar ahí. Seguro que está en el 'top' tres y ojalá que queden primeras, aunque yo diría que puede llevarse el oro", dijo Romero en declaraciones a los medios tras el primer entrenamiento en pista de la pretemporada del conjunto 'taronja'. Romero también valoró el papel de la selección femenina en categorías inferiores que este verano se colgó la medalla de oro en el Europeo sub16 y sub18 y la plata en el Mundial sub17, entre otros éxitos. "Se nota el buen trabajo que se hace desde la base. España siempre ha sido una potencia europea y las jugadoras son cada vez más competitivas, más fuertes y juegan mejor a baloncesto", explicó la base canaria, que añadió que la selección española "siempre está en los puestos altos de cualquier ranking".

Romero también valoró el papel de la selección femenina en categorías inferiores que este verano se colgó la medalla de oro en el Europeo sub16 y sub18 y la plata en el Mundial sub17, entre otros éxitos. "Se nota el buen trabajo que se hace desde la base. España siempre ha sido una potencia europea y las jugadoras son cada vez más competitivas, más fuertes y juegan mejor a baloncesto", explicó la base canaria, que añadió que la selección española "siempre está en los puestos altos de cualquier ranking".

articles.title: Jugar la SuperCup tiene premio: esto es lo que se llevarán los participantes
articles.standfirst: La nueva competición de la Euroliga tendrá lugar en Abu Dabi los días 18 y 19 de septiembre
articles.summary: La nueva competición de la Euroliga tendrá lugar en Abu Dabi los días 18 y 19 de septiembre
articles.body: Los próximos días 18 y 19 el baloncesto europeo verá nacer una nueva competición. Se trata de la SuperCup de la Euroliga, un torneo que vale como pretemporada para los equipos pero que, dado el nivel de los rivales, se puede considerar un competición más, con un título en juego, y con mucho prestigio para repartir. Y el prestigio no será lo único que se reparta. Jugar la SuperCup tiene premio económico para los cuatro equipos que estarán presentes en el Etihad Arena de Abu Dabi. Además de presentar un cartel con cuatro equipos que estarán luchando por llegar a la Final Four en mayo, los participantes de la SuperCup se llevarán un pico por tratar de ganar el primer título continental en juego. Los cuatro equipos participantes, Olympiacos (campeón), Real Madrid (subcampeón), Fenerbahce (campeón del año anterior) y Dubai Basketball (anfitrión), se llevarán 500.000 euros cada uno, sólo por estar en Abu Dabi esos dos días. El ganador final podrá aumentar la bolsa a unos 750.000 euros en total. Además, de lo ingresado, la Euroliga utilizará el resto para gastar en el evento y para aumentar la distribución económica a todos los equipos. En materia de entradas el abanico de precios es muy grande. Están las más económicas, que salen por unos 134 euros, y las más caras, la de primera fila, que ya se van a 2.547 euros, que contempla un paquete VIP. Entre medias ha varios precios, dependiendo del lugar en el pabellón. La Euroliga ya ha puesto las entradas a la venta desde este lunes en un paquete para los dos días. El 31 de agosto saldrán a la venta las entradas por día, permitiendo al aficionado acudir a los partidos del viernes o del sábado. En ese sentido, la entradas ya van desde la más barata, 55 euros hasta los 138 euros del viernes, o el tramo entre 102 y 256 para los del sábado dependiendo de la localidad en el pabellón.

articles.title: El Baskonia ficha a 'Manimal' para reforzar su juego interior
articles.summary: El Baskonia ha llegado a un acuerdo para fichar a Kenneth Faried, tal y como ha informado el periodista Chema de Lucas. Es un fichaje necesario para el equupo vitoriano que está tratando de recomponer su juego interior tras la marcha de jugadores como Eugene Omoruyi y, sobre todo, Mamadi Diakite.
articles.body: El Baskonia ha llegado a un acuerdo para fichar a Kenneth Faried, tal y como ha informado el periodista Chema de Lucas. Es un fichaje necesario para el equupo vitoriano que está tratando de recomponer su juego interior tras la marcha de jugadores como Eugene Omoruyi y, sobre todo, Mamadi Diakite. De hecho, Kenneth Faried no será el último interior que fiche el equipo azulgrana que buscará otro pívot más en el mercado. Faried se unirá como novedad en el Baskonia a los ya fichados Damion Baugh, DJ Stewart, Chris Duarte, A.J. Lawson. Faried, conocido como 'Manimal', jugó el pasado año en el Panathinaikos en su segunda experiencia en la Euroliga. En realidad firmó por dos meses para paliar la plaga de lesiones del equipo griego y acabó completando toda la temporada. Eso sí, su irrupción fue colosal y fue perdiendo fuerza a medida que avanzaba la campaña hasta contar muy poco para Ergin Ataman. Faried arrancó la Euroliga con tanta fuerza que fue elegido MVP del mes de noviembre. Acabó la pasada temporada con 5,8 puntos y 3,9 rebotes en 13 minutos en 35 partidos. El PAO comunicó que no contaba con él a principios del verano y Faried decidió seguir en la Euroliga ahora en el Baskonia.

articles.title: R.J. Luis Jr. Cleared by Judge to Play for LSU After Spending Time with 2 NBA Teams
articles.summary: BATON ROUGE, La. (AP) — RJ Luis Jr., a former St. John's standout who recently signed with LSU after spending time with two NBA clubs, was cleared by a court Monday evening to start practicing and potentially play for the Tigers this season.
articles.body:
BATON ROUGE, La. (AP) — RJ Luis Jr., a former St. John's standout who recently signed with LSU after spending time with two NBA clubs, was cleared by a court Monday evening to start practicing and potentially play for the Tigers this season.

Luis, who briefly was under contract with the Utah Jazz and Boston Celtics but never played in an NBA game, hugged LSU coach Will Wade after the ruling by East Baton Rouge Parish District Court judge Ronald R. Johnson.

After a five-hour hearing, Johnson granted the player's request for a preliminary injunction against the NCAA, which had argued Luis was unlikely to win reinstatement after leaving college to turn pro in 2025.

"This is precedent. It's monumental," said Baton Rouge-based attorney Tony Clayton, who represented Luis along with Elliot Abrams of Raleigh, North Carolina. "This allows him to go practice, go play and we'll let the legal process work itself out."

The timeline for that process was not immediately clear.

"I don't know, but there's a lot of discovery that Elliot and I have to obtain," Clayton said. "We've got a lot of questions."

Luis' attorneys noted that the NCAA had granted exceptions allowing numerous players from overseas professional leagues to join college basketball programs, and argued that American players must be afforded the same opportunity.

They stressed that Luis not only had never played in an NBA game, but also had not played for the Celtics' G League affiliate because of an injury, and had far less of a professional basketball resume than numerous college players who'd been recruited from abroad.

NCAA attorney Taylor Askew argued that Luis' situation was not comparable to those who played for the developmental squads of pro organizations overseas because Luis chose to leave college for the NBA.

Askew noted that the only player in a similar situation to Luis was Alabama's Charles Bediako, who won a temporary retraining order allowing him to play five games for Alabama last season before an Alabama judge ultimately sided with NCAA assertions that he was ineligible.

"I understand Mr. Luis is disappointed that he was not drafted and did not play in the NBA as much as he would have liked," Askew said. "Actions have consequences. Decisions have outcomes and they're not always the right ones or the ones that you want."

As he made his ruling, Johnson said, "In the court's mind, (Luis) did not actually play professional basketball," and that whether Luis was properly advised of his options at the time he left college "lingers heavily before this court."

articles.title: Una camiseta de Jordan podría ser el objeto deportivo más valioso de la historia: ¡100 millones de dólares!
articles.standfirst: El 15 de septiembre se subasta la prenda que el mito vistió en el tercer partido de la final de 1998, cuando conquistó su sexto anillo con los Bulls antes de retirarse
articles.summary: El 15 de septiembre se subasta la prenda que el mito vistió en el tercer partido de la final de 1998, cuando conquistó su sexto anillo con los Bulls antes de retirarse
articles.body: La camiseta que Michael Jordan utilizó en el tercer partido de la final de la NBA en 1998 podría convertirse en el objeto más valioso en la historia del deporte. Se pondrá a subasta el 15 de septiembre y es posible que alcance los ¡100 millones de dólares! Se trata de la camiseta blanca que el mito usó en el tercer encuentro de la serie ante los Jazz. Además de ser uno de sus últimos partidos con los Bulls, durante la temporada de su 'Last dance', la vistió en una cita que terminó con el marcador de 96-54. Para hacer aún más única a la prenda, esos 42 puntos son la mayor diferencia en un partido de las finales de la NBA. Aquel 7 de junio, dado el amplio margen en el marcador, Jordan jugó sólo 32 minutos, su cifra más baja en aquellos playoffs, y metió 24 puntos. El actual propietario de la camiseta es el inversor deportivo y actor Rob Gough, que llegó a ella hace años a través de distintos intermediarios sin llegar a conocer a quien realmente la poseía. Él tiene otras piezas históricas que vistieron mitos como Kobe Bryant, Wilt Chamberlain, Tom Brady y Wayne Gretzky. "Se trata de conseguir piezas que se encuentren en la intersección del mejor atleta, el mejor escenario y un momento decisivo", asegura. Ahora la pone a subasta porque cree que no estaba siendo valorada como merece. "Tengo muchas obras de arte estupendas. Y cuando la gente viene a casa, se las salta para ir directamente a la camiseta. Fue entonces cuando me di cuenta de que esto es el nuevo arte moderno", cuenta Gough. Otra camiseta de Jordan, utilizada en el primer encuentro de aquellas finales de la NBA de 1998 fue vendida por 10,1 millones de dólares en 2022. Sin embargo, los Bulls cayeron en aquel encuentro por 88-85 después de una prórroga. "Yo no compro piezas de partidos en los que un jugador pierde porque uno piensa: 'Esa camiseta en la pared, ¿recuerdan cuando Michael Jordan perdió ese partido?' Simplemente no se dice eso", sentencia. Gough ya se hizo un nombre en la industria de los objetos de colección después de comprar una rara tarjeta de la estrella del béisbol Mickey Mantle de 1952 por 5,2 millones de dólares en 2021.

articles.title: Anthony Edwards tendrá que pagar 14.000 dólares al mes por mantener a un hijo al que no piensa conocer
articles.standfirst: La estrella de los Wolves tuvo en 2024 tres hijos con tres mujeres distintas
articles.summary: La estrella de los Wolves tuvo en 2024 tres hijos con tres mujeres distintas
articles.body: Los problemas extradeportivos vuelven a acuciar a Anthony Edwards. El escolta de los Timberwolves tendrá que pagar 14.000 dólares al mes en concepto de manutención para un hijo nacido en 2023 al que, según admitió bajo juramento, no conoce en persona y con el que renuncia a cualquier derecho a pasar tiempo con él. La cantidad a pagar, según informa el medio estadounidense TMZ, se determinó en función de los ingresos del jugador, una de las grandes estrellas de la NBA, que la próxima temporada ganará 48,9 millones de dólares. A ello se añade una póliza de seguro de vida que debe ser contratada por valor de 2,6 millones de dólares con la madre del niño como beneficiaria. Edwards ha protagonizado varios escándalos de relaciones personales con demandas por paternidad. En 2024, el escolta de los Wolves fue padre en tres ocasiones con tres mujeres distintas. Hace tiempo, ya había recibido la orden de pagar 3.000 dólares a la madre de otra niña. En diciembre de 2023, salieron a la luz los lamentables mensajes que el jugador envió a una modelo en los que le pedía que abortara. "Diablos, no puedo hacerlo", "no quiero niños" o "hazte un aborto jajaja", eran algunas de las frases que escribió Edwards, que también habría hecho a la mujer una transferencia de 100.000 dólares para llevar a cabo el procedimiento. Posteriormente, tuvo que disculparse públicamente por todo ello. A lo largo de la historia de la NBA, son muchos los jugadores que, pese a haber ganado grandes cantidades de dinero, se han visto arruinados, entre otras razones, por tener que mantener a su descendencia. Edwards, que todavía tiene 25 años, parece no ir por buen camino.

articles.title: El Kosner Baskonia anuncia el fichaje del exNBA Kenneth Faried
articles.standfirst: El pívot de 36 años y 2,05 metros jugó 478 encuentros entre Nuggets, Nets y Rockets y la temporada pasada militó en el Panathinaikos
articles.summary: El pívot de 36 años y 2,05 metros jugó 478 encuentros entre Nuggets, Nets y Rockets y la temporada pasada militó en el Panathinaikos
articles.body: El veterano Kenneth Faried reforzará la próxima temporada el juego interior de Kosner Baskonia, tras disputar la Euroliga con el Panathinaikos. El pivot norteamericano de 2.05 metros y 36 años cuenta con una amplia experiencia con más de 450 partidos de NBA donde llegó tras jugar en la NCAA, en la filas de Morehead State Eagles. Jugó 7 temporadas en Denver Nuggets y fue internacional con la selección estadounidense, con la que ganó el campeonato del mundo en 2014. Posteriormente, continuó su carrera en Brooklyn Nets, Capitanes de la Liga mexicana o CSKA Moscú, donde debutó en la máxima competición europea en la campaña 2021-22. La pasada campaña, en las filas del Panathinaikos, logró convertirse en el MVP del mes de noviembre en la Euroliga. "Con su incorporación, el club azulgrana suma experiencia y físico a sus filas para la temporada 2026-27", indicaron desde el club en una nota de prensa. El curso pasado firmó 5,2 puntos y 3,7 rebotes en los 35 duelos que disputó con el conjunto griego.

articles.title: Jassel Pérez, ritmo y talento ofensivo para el FIATC Girona
articles.standfirst: El escolta de 24 años y 1,90 metros llega al conjunto catalán tras ganar la Liga de Puerto Rico con Vaqueros de Bayamón promediando 18,9 puntos en playoffs
articles.summary: El escolta de 24 años y 1,90 metros llega al conjunto catalán tras ganar la Liga de Puerto Rico con Vaqueros de Bayamón promediando 18,9 puntos en playoffs
articles.body: El escolta dominicano Jassel Pérez se ha convertido este martes en nuevo jugador del FIATC Girona, que le ha hecho un contrato para las dos próximas temporadas, según ha anunciado el club catalán. Pérez, de 24 años y 1,90 metros, llegará a Fontajau justo después de proclamarse campeón de la liga de Puerto Rico con la camiseta de los Vaqueros de Bayamón. Allí ha promediado 21,4 puntos, 4 rebotes y 3,3 asistencias por partido en la fase regular y 18,9 puntos, 5,3 rebotes y 4,4 asistencias en las eliminatorias al título. La temporada pasada jugó primero en la Primera Federación con el Grupo Alega Cantabria (15,1 puntos, 4,1 rebotes y 3,3 asistencias) y desde diciembre en la Liga Endesa con el Coviran Granada, con el que disputó 23 partidos y promedió 11,3 puntos y 3,8 rebotes. Jassel Pérez es "una pieza necesaria" que "encaja perfectamente" en el estilo del FIATC Girona, según ha asegurado su director deportivo, Fernando San Emeterio en unas declaraciones distribuidas por el club catalán. "Tiene un talento natural y una exuberancia física que le hace diferencial a campo abierto, sobre todo en el momento de atacar el aro. También es capaz de defender muy bien porque es muy proactivo", ha añadido. San Emeterio también ha afirmado que el nuevo fichaje es "un jugador en clara progresión" que ha evolucionado en los dos últimos años y que es "muy humilde" y tiene "hambre de crecer y competir".

Jassel Pérez es "una pieza necesaria" que "encaja perfectamente" en el estilo del FIATC Girona, según ha asegurado su director deportivo, Fernando San Emeterio en unas declaraciones distribuidas por el club catalán. "Tiene un talento natural y una exuberancia física que le hace diferencial a campo abierto, sobre todo en el momento de atacar el aro. También es capaz de defender muy bien porque es muy proactivo", ha añadido. San Emeterio también ha afirmado que el nuevo fichaje es "un jugador en clara progresión" que ha evolucionado en los dos últimos años y que es "muy humilde" y tiene "hambre de crecer y competir".

articles.title: New Kyrie Irving Trade Rumors Reveal Rivals 'Wonder Aloud' About Mavs Star's Availability
articles.summary: Despite the Dallas Mavericks declaring that they plan to retain star point guard Kyrie Irving during the 2026-27 season, it sounds like other teams aren't convinced they will keep their word.
articles.body:
Despite the Dallas Mavericks declaring that they plan to retain star point guard Kyrie Irving during the 2026-27 season, it sounds like other teams aren't convinced they will keep their word.

According to NBA insider Marc Stein , rival teams "continue to wonder aloud about how firmly Dallas will stick to that stance once the season begins and the next in-season trade deadline on Feb. 11 gradually approaches."

Offseason Overreactions for Every Team 🫨

Upon his hiring in May, new Mavs president of basketball operations Masai Ujiri made it clear that the team hoped to have Irving leading the way alongside 2025 No. 1 pick and reigning NBA Rookie of the Year Cooper Flagg.

"There's a huge curiosity in our minds to see how Kyrie fits playing with Flagg," Ujiri said at the time . "He's just that kind of incredible talent and player. And I think we owe that to this organization."

When the Mavs hired Dusty May as their new head coach the following month, May also declared that he was looking forward to working with Irving.

"Kyrie knows what it takes to win a championship, so as a first-time NBA coach, I'm gonna lean on him in a lot of areas," May told reporters in June.

Still, it's hard to argue that Irving is Dallas' biggest trade asset as the team continues its rebuild. The nine-time All-Star missed the entire 2025-26 season while recovering from a torn ACL, but it can be expected that he's looking to return in top form during the upcoming campaign.

If the Mavs struggle to find success during the start of the 2026-27 season, they could become more open to the idea of trading Irving for the right offer.

articles.title: Más equipos grandes y mercados claves se comprometen para ser franquicias de la Euroliga
articles.standfirst: Recibe más de una docena de ofertas vinculantes de equipos para convertirse en franquicias que generarán más de 700 millones e inversiones de 3.200 millones en infraestructuras
articles.summary: Recibe más de una docena de ofertas vinculantes de equipos para convertirse en franquicias que generarán más de 600 millones e inversiones de 2.000 millones en infraestructuras
articles.body: El Board de la Euroliga celebrado esta mañana en Barcelona y que contó con la presencia de todos los representantes de equipos accionistas de la competición, anunció a bombo y platillo su imparable plan de expansión con el que lleva camino de monopolizar el baloncesto europeo, tomando una ventaja considerable sobre el proyecto de la NBA Europa cuyo estreno en principio está previsto para la temporada 2027-28. El CEO de la Euroliga, Chus Bueno, dio a conocer con luz y taquígrafos la recepción de más de una docena de ofertas vinculantes, con compromisos ya firmados, de equipos e inversores que han demostrado con documentos rubricados su deseo de convertirse en franquicias de la Euroliga a partir de la temporada 2027-28, en la que el torneo probablemente cambiará de formato y será dividido en dos Conferencias, ante el crecimiento del número de equipos. Esas ofertas vinculantes garantizan a la competición unos ingresos de más de 700 millones de euros sumando el canon -de diversa cuantía en función de su trascendencia en el mercado baloncestístico continental- que tendrán que abonar entre todos los nuevos socios, contratos vinculantes de varios equipos y ciudades entre los que se encuentran Valencia Basket, Dubai Basketball, PAOK Salónica, París Basketball, Hapoel Tel Aviv, Partizan o Estrella Roja. Además, añade a su imparable expansión nuevas ciudades muy estratégicos como Londres, Roma y Nápoles con los que la Euroliga consigue afianzar y proteger los siete mercados más importantes del baloncesto europeo: Turquía, Grecia, Italia, España, Alemania, Francia y Gran Bretaña. Amplía así sus fronteras, gana terreno en todo el baloncesto europeo y refuerza su dominio. Todos estos equipos y ciudades demuestran con sus ofertas vinculantes estar totalmente comprometidos e ilusionados con este proyecto, como prueba el hecho de que además de aportar entre todos ellos más de 700 millones de euros como canon, invertirán más de 3.200 millones de euros en infraestructuras. Todos estos nuevos equipos e inversores han pasado ya el primer 'due diligence' del Board de la Euroliga, un proceso de investigación, revisión y comprobación para constatar que tienen capacidad y son suficientemente solventes y competitivos para poder convertirse en franquicias de la competición. Aunque la aprobación final será en el Board of Owners o Asamblea de Dueños que tendrá lugar a finales de este próximo mes de septiembre y del que saldrán las nuevas franquicias cuyas propuestas sean aceptadas. Chus Bueno, que tomó las riendas de la Euroliga como nuevo CEO el 30 de enero de 2026, y su equipo ejecutivo han logrado en apenas ocho meses que el proyecto de la Euroliga siga avanzando a pasos agigantados con su ambicioso plan de expansión que parece no tener techo, logrando un crecimiento exponencial desde el punto de vista cuantitativo y cualitativo que le permite consolidar su dominio en el mercado del baloncesto europeo.      “La Euroliga está experimentando un fuerte impulso, tanto a nivel comercial como estratégico, con importantes renovaciones de acuerdos de colaboración a largo plazo acordadas en las últimas semanas y el lanzamiento de nuevos eventos que continúan expandiendo nuestra plataforma", explicó Bueno. El CEO de la Euroliga destacó también la consolidación del proyecto: "Al mismo tiempo, el interés que ha despertado el proceso de franquicias refleja claramente la confianza que clubes, inversores y nuevos proyectos depositan en el futuro de la Euroliga. Las ofertas vinculantes, cercanas a los 700 millones de euros, que representan una inversión total de más de 3.200 millones de euros en los próximos cinco años, demuestran la solidez de nuestro modelo de negocio y el valor que se genera en toda la Liga". Una inversión de los clubes que redundará íntegramente en ellos mismos, no en la organización. La Euroliga ha exigido a todos esos inversores su compromiso por escrito con el dinero que va a ser adelantado por los clubes para los propios clubes. Y esa es la premisa que más y mejor estimula el compromiso y la ilusión de todos ellos de apostar por una competición de la que los propios clubes serán los únicos beneficiarios.

articles.title: Breaking Down NBA 2K27's Best New Features for This Year's Game
articles.summary: NBA 2K27 is nearly here, and this year's entry sees the game's developers continue to provide the most realistic, authentic on-court experience for die-hard basketball fans while also enhancing the off-the-court options for the casual audience.
articles.body:
NBA 2K27 is nearly here, and this year's entry sees the game's developers continue to provide the most realistic, authentic on-court experience for die-hard basketball fans while also enhancing the off-the-court options for the casual audience.

Significant attention was paid to improving gameplay while also introducing a first-time-ever element to its popular The City mode.

Dive deeper into each of those in this breakdown of the new features.

Date: August 26 (Deluxe and Ultra editions), September 4 (Standard edition)

Platforms: PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X/S, Stream for PC, and Nintendo Switch 2

Cover Athletes: Victor Wembanyama (Standard), Caitlin Clark (Deluxe), Derrick Rose (Ultra)

2K has committed to bringing the most authentic NBA experience to gamers with this year's release by adding several new features to the gameplay engine.

Now players can make like Anthony Edwards and use the step-up up-and-unders to create separation and knock down game-sealing shots.

Expanded dribbling customization lets gamers add every element of a player's offensive attack to their arsenal, and a new layup tool prevents the ball from clipping parts of the rim or backboard.

A new timing- and logic-based dunk meter tightens when a defender confronts you at or near the rim, and rhythm shooting is upgraded.

Perhaps most interesting is the introduction of a more physical defense.

2K has made sure to emphasize an element of the game that may not be as omnipresent on the hardwood as some would like by making considerable upgrades to the defensive side of the ball.

Defensive cutoffs and a new collision system make offenses choose the right moves at the right times or face potential blocked shots and turnovers.

For the first time in NBA 2K history, male and female MyPLAYERS can play together in The City.

There will be thousands of options to outfit both men and women. More importantly, all modes within The City will be co-ed.

The game's official website notes that female MyPLAYERS are exclusive to The City, though.

articles.title: Career turning point: âIt changed my life foreverâ: How Angel Reeseâs LSU championship win over Caitlin Clark turned one unforgettable night into a career-changing rise to stardom
articles.summary: NBA News: Before Angel Reese became one of the biggest names in womenâs basketball, she was already an accomplished player with the talent to reach the highest .
articles.body: Before Angel Reese became one of the biggest names in womenâs basketball, she was already an accomplished player with the talent to reach the highest level. Her time at Maryland had established her as a major college prospect but transferring to LSU in 2022 gave her a new opportunity to become the centerpiece of a team with national championship ambitions. She took that opportunity and turned the 2022-23 season into the defining year of her college career.The biggest moment arrived on April 2, 2023, when LSU faced Caitlin Clark and Iowa in the NCAA championship game. LSU won 102-85 to claim the first national championship in program history, while Reese recorded 15 points, 10 rebounds, five assists and three steals. The victory made her a champion, but the attention surrounding the game did something even more significant. Reese's celebration, her exchange with Clark and the enormous audience watching the matchup pushed her into a different level of national fame. Looking back two years later, Reese showed the impact in one sentence: Damn I won a natty two years ago today & it changed my life forever.âHow did the LSU-Iowa championship become Angel Reeseâs biggest turning point?Reese arrived at LSU with plenty of expectations after transferring from Maryland, but the scale of what happened in Baton Rouge during her first season was difficult to predict. She immediately became one of the most dominant players in the country, averaging 23.0 points, 15.4 rebounds and 1.6 blocks per game during the 2022-23 campaign. Her production helped LSU establish itself as a serious championship contender, while Reese developed into the player the Tigers could rely on when games became difficult.That consistency carried into March Madness. Reese recorded double-digit points and rebounds in all six of LSUâs tournament games and averaged 21.3 points and 15.2 rebounds during the run. LSU defeated top-seeded Virginia Tech in the Final Four to reach the championship game, setting up a meeting with Iowa and Clark that immediately attracted national attention.Clark had already become a phenomenon. Her scoring, passing and ability to produce spectacular moments had helped make Iowa one of the most watched teams in college basketball. Reese represented a different kind of star. She was powerful around the basket, relentless on the boards and comfortable embracing the physical and emotional side of competition. When those two players met with a national championship on the line, the matchup carried a significance that went beyond the box score.LSU ultimately controlled the game and pulled away for a 102-85 victory. Reese produced a double-double and helped the Tigers complete an unbeaten tournament run. She was named the Final Four's Most Outstanding Player, giving her another individual honor to go with the national championship.Yet the lasting impact of the night was not limited to the trophy. The closing moments created an image that would follow Reese long after she left LSU. After making a gesture toward Clark that referenced Clark's own âYou can't see meâ celebration, Reese became the center of a huge national discussion. Some praised her confidence and competitive edge, while others criticized the way she celebrated. Either way, the moment ensured that Reese's name remained part of the conversation long after LSU's championship parade.That was the point when her career began to change in a way that statistics alone could not explain.How did one championship moment turn Angel Reese into a national star?The importance of the LSU-Iowa game became even clearer when Reese later reflected on what happened. In an episode of her podcast, âUnapologetically Angelâ, she described the championship as a moment that âchanged my life forever.â She also explained that the scale of the audience and everything surrounding the game had transformed her profile.That observation matters because Reese had already been a star before April 2023. She was not an unknown player who suddenly appeared in the championship game. She had spent years developing her game and had just produced a remarkable season at LSU.What changed was the size of the audience that knew her. The championship put Reese and Clark at the center of one of the most discussed women's basketball games in recent memory. The game reportedly drew 9.9 million viewers, while the moments between the two stars generated conversation across sports and mainstream media. Reese later described the impact in even broader terms, saying, âSeeing 9.9 million people watch that game, from my hand gesture, to winning, changed women's basketball forever.â She added, âMy life literally just completely changed from that game.âThat is the real reason the championship became a career turning point. Reese's talent had created the opportunity, but the championship gave her a platform. Suddenly, her personality mattered almost as much as her statistics. People wanted to know more about the player behind the celebration, the confidence and the competitive personality.The attention also came with pressure. Reese became a frequent subject of debate, particularly around her rivalry with Clark and the reaction to their increasingly high-profile matchups. Later, Reese spoke openly about some of the hostility she experienced from fans, saying, âI think it's really just the fans, her fans, the Iowa fans, now the Indiana fans, that are really just, they ride for her, and I respect that, respectfully. But sometimes it's very disrespectful.â She also said she believed racism played a role in some of the treatment she received.The experience showed both sides of becoming a national star. The attention created opportunities, but it also brought scrutiny that Reese had never faced at the same scale.How did the LSU championship shape Reeseâs professional rise?The national championship gave Reese momentum that continued through the final year of her college career and into the WNBA. She remained one of the biggest names in women's college basketball, and her growing profile made her valuable not only as an athlete but also as a personality and brand.After completing her LSU career, Reese entered the 2024 WNBA Draft and was selected seventh overall by the Chicago Sky. Her professional career gave her a new challenge, but the foundation had already been established in college. She entered the league with an enormous following and the kind of recognition that usually takes professional athletes years to develop.Her rookie season showed that the production that made her famous at LSU could translate to the professional level. Reese quickly became one of the WNBA's strongest rebounders and established herself as a physical presence around the basket. Although her rookie campaign eventually ended because of a hand injury, her popularity continued to grow.Her influence also moved beyond basketball. Reese built a strong commercial profile through partnerships with major brands and developed the âBayou Barbieâ identity that had become closely associated with her public image. She later created Unapologetically Angel, giving her a platform to discuss basketball, culture and her experiences away from the traditional media environment.Those opportunities are important when examining what Reese meant when she said the championship changed her life.The night did not magically create her talent. That talent had already been there.Instead, the championship amplified everything.It gave her a national audience, established her as one of the faces of the women's game and created the momentum that followed her into professional basketball and media. Her WNBA draft position was a major career milestone, but the groundwork for that level of recognition had already been laid in the LSU-Iowa championship.The rivalry with Clark also continued to influence Reese's professional journey. Their college history carried into the WNBA, where their matchups attracted significant attention and became part of the league's growing popularity. Their rivalry had evolved from a college championship storyline into one of the most recognizable individual narratives in women's basketball.For Reese, however, the significance of that original night was never simply about beating Clark. It was about what the moment unlocked.She entered the 2023 championship game as a dominant LSU forward chasing the biggest trophy of her college career. She left as a national champion whose name was suddenly known far beyond the usual women's basketball audience.Her transfer to LSU gave her the stage. Her performances made her a star. But the championship against Iowa gave her a moment that reached millions of people and changed the scale of her career.The WNBA would later give her another platform, while endorsements, media opportunities and her podcast helped build her identity away from the court. Yet the foundation of that rise was created in the final minutes of the 2023 championship game.Angel Reese later looked back at the anniversary and did not describe it simply as her greatest basketball achievement. She described it as something much more personal: âIt changed my life forever.âHence, that particular moment stands above the other milestones in Reese's career. LSU's first national championship gave the program its historic moment, but for Reese, the night became the beginning of a much bigger story.It was the night a championship turned into a platform, a rivalry became a national storyline and Angel Reese went from being a college basketball star to becoming one of the most recognisable athletes in women's sports.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. People wanted to know more about the player behind the celebration, the confidence and the competitive personality.The attention also came with pressure. Reese became a frequent subject of debate, particularly around her rivalry with Clark and the reaction to their increasingly high-profile matchups. Later, Reese spoke openly about some of the hostility she experienced from fans, saying, âI think it's really just the fans, her fans, the Iowa fans, now the Indiana fans, that are really just, they ride for her, and I respect that, respectfully. But sometimes it's very disrespectful.â She also said she believed racism played a role in some of the treatment she received.The experience showed both sides of becoming a national star. The attention created opportunities, but it also brought scrutiny that Reese had never faced at the same scale.How did the LSU championship shape Reeseâs professional rise?The national championship gave Reese momentum that continued through the final year of her college career and into the WNBA. She remained one of the biggest names in women's college basketball, and her growing profile made her valuable not only as an athlete but also as a personality and brand.After completing her LSU career, Reese entered the 2024 WNBA Draft and was selected seventh overall by the Chicago Sky. Her professional career gave her a new challenge, but the foundation had already been established in college. She entered the league with an enormous following and the kind of recognition that usually takes professional athletes years to develop.Her rookie season showed that the production that made her famous at LSU could translate to the professional level. Reese quickly became one of the WNBA's strongest rebounders and established herself as a physical presence around the basket. Although her rookie campaign eventually ended because of a hand injury, her popularity continued to grow.Her influence also moved beyond basketball. Reese built a strong commercial profile through partnerships with major brands and developed the âBayou Barbieâ identity that had become closely associated with her public image. She later created Unapologetically Angel, giving her a platform to discuss basketball, culture and her experiences away from the traditional media environment.Those opportunities are important when examining what Reese meant when she said the championship changed her life.The night did not magically create her talent. That talent had already been there.Instead, the championship amplified everything.It gave her a national audience, established her as one of the faces of the women's game and created the momentum that followed her into professional basketball and media. Her WNBA draft position was a major career milestone, but the groundwork for that level of recognition had already been laid in the LSU-Iowa championship.The rivalry with Clark also continued to influence Reese's professional journey. Their college history carried into the WNBA, where their matchups attracted significant attention and became part of the league's growing popularity. Their rivalry had evolved from a college championship storyline into one of the most recognizable individual narratives in women's basketball.For Reese, however, the significance of that original night was never simply about beating Clark. It was about what the moment unlocked.She entered the 2023 championship game as a dominant LSU forward chasing the biggest trophy of her college career. She left as a national champion whose name was suddenly known far beyond the usual women's basketball audience.Her transfer to LSU gave her the stage. Her performances made her a star. But the championship against Iowa gave her a moment that reached millions of people and changed the scale of her career.The WNBA would later give her another platform, while endorsements, media opportunities and her podcast helped build her identity away from the court. Yet the foundation of that rise was created in the final minutes of the 2023 championship game.Angel Reese later looked back at the anniversary and did not describe it simply as her greatest basketball achievement. She described it as something much more personal: âIt changed my life forever.âHence, that particular moment stands above the other milestones in Reese's career. LSU's first national championship gave the program its historic moment, but for Reese, the night became the beginning of a much bigger story.It was the night a championship turned into a platform, a rivalry became a national storyline and Angel Reese went from being a college basketball star to becoming one of the most recognisable athletes in women's sports.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates.
